0bAraCHvRO.one_liner: Benchmark of 43,468 expert field surveys of 363 California vegetation alliances for fine-grained, hierarchical vegetation classification by geospatial foundation models.
0bAraCHvRO.problem: Existing geospatial benchmarks focus on coarse land cover, so it is unclear whether geoFMs capture the fine-scale vegetation types needed for conservation and wildfire decisions.
0bAraCHvRO.method: VegBench standardizes decades of expert-collected vegetation classification and accuracy-assessment surveys across California and compares modern geoFMs against remote sensing and environmental covariate baselines, using accuracy, balanced accuracy and hierarchical accuracy.
0bAraCHvRO.key_idea: Evaluate models along a hierarchy from coarse ecosystem groups down to fine vegetation alliances using expert field-survey labels, exposing where accuracy degrades with ecological resolution.
0bAraCHvRO.evidence: 43,468 surveys of 363 vegetation alliances in California; geoFMs versus remote sensing and covariate baselines, with ablations and an expert-map comparison based on NAIP imagery per reviews.
0bAraCHvRO.claimed_gains: not stated as gains; the best models capture broad ecological structure but fall short at fine-scale resolution, and no accuracy figures are given in the abstract.
0bAraCHvRO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is well motivated, built on valuable expert field-survey data, and shows geoFMs fall short of fine-grained ecological needs.
0bAraCHvRO.main_concern: The dataset is small and geographically limited (California only, long-tailed alliances, few recent surveys), and the relevance of alliance classification from remotely sensed imagery is questioned.

lR8Dsgwyf3.one_liner: Statistical theory of low-frequency recovery in overparameterized diffusion models, with bounds independent of parallel-network count.
lR8Dsgwyf3.problem: Diffusion models learn global layouts more faithfully than fine details, but existing theory addresses full-distribution estimation rates and not how data and network capacity govern accuracy at different resolutions.
lR8Dsgwyf3.method: Uses the discrete Fourier transform to describe data by resolution, proves approximation and estimation guarantees for the score of the low-frequency component at a prescribed cutoff, and gives a distribution recovery bound separating a statistical error (set by an effective dimension of retained frequencies) from a remainder due to low-high frequency dependence.
lR8Dsgwyf3.key_idea: Control network complexity with cutoff-specific weight-matrix norm constraints so covering bounds stay unchanged as parallel networks grow, tying error to the effective dimension of the retained frequencies.
lR8Dsgwyf3.evidence: Theoretical approximation, estimation and distribution recovery bounds, with synthetic and CIFAR-10 experiments illustrating the effect of sample size and weight decay on frequency recovery.
lR8Dsgwyf3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is a substantial theoretical contribution that separates the projected full-distribution score from the low-frequency marginal score and gives norm-controlled guarantees independent of the number of parallel branches.
lR8Dsgwyf3.main_concern: The guarantees depend on a pre-specified, cutoff-specific norm budget, and the experiments (independent Fourier coordinates, single CIFAR-10 runs) give limited validation of the theory.

vxhfeLxrou.one_liner: Spherical quadrature attention with exact gauge equivariance, using Levi-Civita transport and scalar, vector and tensor hidden fields.
vxhfeLxrou.problem: It is unclear how spherical attention can use intrinsic vector and tensor field features consistently, although spherical tasks have spatial structure naturally described by such quantities.
vxhfeLxrou.method: The paper formulates a gauge-theoretic normalized aggregation on Riemannian manifolds that covers convolution and attention, and proves equivariance under structure-preserving isometries when explicit assumptions hold. A spherical quadrature realization uses exact spherical geometry and Levi-Civita transport to process scalar, vector and tensor fields.
vxhfeLxrou.key_idea: Aggregate features by normalized quadrature over parallel-transported tangent fields, so attention is exactly gauge-equivariant for scalar, vector and tensor hidden fields.
vxhfeLxrou.evidence: Rotating shallow-water dynamics and Stanford 2D-3D-S omnidirectional semantic segmentation, with ablations and comparisons against S^2 Transformer and S^2 SegFormer, plus evaluation across spherical discretizations.
vxhfeLxrou.claimed_gains: Ablations and comparisons show benefits of geometric intermediate representations and content-dependent attention weights; no numbers stated in the abstract.
vxhfeLxrou.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the mathematical treatment of gauge equivariance rigorous and clear, and see the two applications as supporting the use of geometric intermediate representations.
vxhfeLxrou.main_concern: The contribution is insufficiently distinguished from prior gauge-equivariant convolution and attention work (Cohen et al., Gerken et al., Weiler et al., GET, EMAN) and quadrature spherical attention.

4V1SAAqUku.one_liner: Shows a frozen random auxiliary encoder recovers much of the gain from cross-modal alignment in multimodal molecular pretraining.
4V1SAAqUku.problem: Gains from aligning a molecular graph encoder with a second view such as SMILES or 3D conformation are usually attributed to information learned by the auxiliary encoder, an explanation the paper finds often incomplete.
4V1SAAqUku.method: Controlled experiments keep the graph model and training fixed while replacing the trained auxiliary encoder with a frozen, randomly initialized network of the same architecture. Further controls test random graph encoders, fixed random codes and simple representation expansion.
4V1SAAqUku.key_idea: Replace the trained auxiliary encoder by a frozen untrained one as a random-target control, to test whether cross-modal gains come from transferred content.
4V1SAAqUku.evidence: Controlled comparisons on QM9, Alchemy, PCQM4Mv2 and QMugs with SMILES and 3D auxiliary views, GraphMVP fine-tuning, and random graph encoder, fixed random code and representation expansion controls.
4V1SAAqUku.claimed_gains: Random SMILES targets reduce mean raw-feature linear-probe error by 5.0% on QM9 and 3.0% on Alchemy relative to graph-only training.
4V1SAAqUku.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the overlooked evaluation issue relevant and important, the experimental design clear, and the many control experiments sound and comprehensive.
4V1SAAqUku.main_concern: The trained auxiliary encoder may not have converged or learned enough new information, the theory's assumptions are not verified, and the paper gives little guidance on when random targets help.

BnxBls3w8x.one_liner: Refines candidate molecules via learned 2-switch bond edits guided by spectrum-predicted fingerprints, for tandem mass spectra structure elucidation.
BnxBls3w8x.problem: Identifying small-molecule structures from formulas and tandem mass spectra is a bottleneck in metabolomics, and retrieved or generated candidates are often near the correct structure but still contain errors.
BnxBls3w8x.method: GEMS uses the pretrained MIST model to predict fingerprint probabilities once per spectrum, and a neural policy compares a candidate's fingerprint with them, links features to atoms and bonds, and scores all valid 2-switch edits in one forward pass. It is pretrained on molecular structures with shortest-path supervision, fine-tuned with predicted fingerprints, and searched from multiple starts ranked by fingerprint agreement and consensus.
BnxBls3w8x.key_idea: Learn a policy that scores formula- and valence-preserving 2-switch edits by comparing a candidate's fingerprint with the spectrum-predicted fingerprint, supervised by shortest edit paths.
BnxBls3w8x.evidence: NPLIB1 and MassSpecGym benchmarks with the target excluded from retrieval, a comparison with FRIGID's refinement from the same initial pool, an enumeration baseline, and oracle interventions for navigation and ranking.
BnxBls3w8x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find fingerprint-guided refinement of nearby candidates clear and well motivated, with comprehensive experiments and strong results on NPLIB1 and MassSpecGym.
BnxBls3w8x.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate key design choices (fingerprint-to-atom/bond correspondence and supervising all optimal actions), and the runtime comparison with FRIGID uses different timing boundaries.

qbVaigPfEP.one_liner: A weight-tied recurrent message-passing GNN represents set-valued equivariant maps through multiple attractors reached from different random initializations.
qbVaigPfEP.problem: Recurrent and equilibrium GNNs assume a unique fixed point or a single target per graph, but many problems have several valid solutions, and picking one imposes an arbitrary symmetry-breaking choice.
qbVaigPfEP.method: The authors prove existence of globally Lipschitz, permutation-equivariant multi-attractor dynamics that converge almost surely to valid solutions and reach every solution branch with positive probability, then prove a realization theorem that a recurrent message-passing GNN can approximate these dynamics.
qbVaigPfEP.key_idea: Use multiple equilibria of a recurrent GNN as the solution set, with each random initialization converging to a different valid solution.
qbVaigPfEP.evidence: Two theorems (existence of multi-attractor dynamics and a realization result for message-passing GNNs) plus experiments in three domains per reviews.
qbVaigPfEP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem framing is clear, since an arbitrary single target can violate equivariance on symmetric graphs, and that the theorems and experiments across three domains support the expressivity claim.
qbVaigPfEP.main_concern: The theory uses a hand-crafted non-smooth construction with no evidence that trained networks learn it, and novelty over prior work on set-valued attractor maps is limited.

9dnx1Dixlv.one_liner: UNSATZ benchmarks LLM agents that must build the ansatz of simulated systems themselves, scored on unseen experiments.
9dnx1Dixlv.problem: Equation-discovery benchmarks mostly supply the ansatz (variables, term library, or law to modify), leaving open-ended model formulation untested.
9dnx1Dixlv.method: Each task is a simulated system generated from a private seed as a program in a small modeling language, possibly with latent states, distorted sensors, and uninformative channels. The agent buys experiments within a budget, writes candidate programs, obtains coefficients from the benchmark's fitter, and is scored on held-out conditions, interventions, and longer runs.
9dnx1Dixlv.key_idea: Agents buy experiments and write candidate programs in a modeling language, scored only on how their final program predicts unseen experiments.
9dnx1Dixlv.evidence: 80 systems across 20 domains evaluated with nine language models plus classical and neural baselines, and an analysis of failed investigations showing the difficulty lies in finding structure rather than in the data.
9dnx1Dixlv.claimed_gains: Nine language models solve between 21% and 60% of 80 systems, and on the 64 deterministic systems the two strongest agents solve 39 and 31 while classical and neural baselines together solve 14.
9dnx1Dixlv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark fills a real gap by testing model-structure discovery rather than parameter fitting, with diverse domains and useful failure analysis.
9dnx1Dixlv.main_concern: External validity is limited: systems are generated in a fixed modeling language, there are only four systems per domain, classical baselines look weak, and many experiments were run once.

0Dk7YbB1pB.one_liner: Policy-update family derived from information-projection dynamics under beta-Bregman divergences, preserving base-model response diversity in RLVR while maximizing reward.
0Dk7YbB1pB.problem: GRPO improves reasoning accuracy but over-sharpens output distributions, suppressing alternative correct responses and reducing solution diversity.
0Dk7YbB1pB.method: betaBPO frames diversity preservation as information projection: it seeks the policy closest in beta-Bregman divergence to the base policy at a target expected reward, and derives representation-based policy updates from the projection dynamics. In a tabular model the projection flow is shown to minimize divergence from the base policy at every attained reward level.
0Dk7YbB1pB.key_idea: Update policies along an information-projection flow under beta-Bregman divergence, using representation-based leverage scores to keep probability mass spread among equally rewarded responses.
0Dk7YbB1pB.evidence: A tabular theoretical analysis, Hyper-Grid experiments, and mathematical reasoning experiments comparing Pass@1, Pass@k, and the KL-divergence versus accuracy frontier.
0Dk7YbB1pB.claimed_gains: Maintains competitive Pass@1 while improving Pass@k at large sampling budgets and achieves the KL-divergence-accuracy Pareto frontier; no figures stated.
0Dk7YbB1pB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the information-projection framing of diversity preservation clear and interpretable, with a clean separation of success probability from the within-class distribution and informative Hyper-Grid experiments.
0Dk7YbB1pB.main_concern: The theory holds for tabular representations and large sampling groups, while the LLM implementation uses learned representations and eight responses per prompt, so the link between the practical algorithm and the projection flow is unverified.

IKzzezuLKc.one_liner: Finds informative prefill queries from the user request's attention and scores keys by 2-hop attention for KV cache compression.
IKzzezuLKc.problem: Attention-sum KV compression methods weight prefill queries differently, but most queries are noisy and do not indicate which keys generation will read.
IKzzezuLKc.method: Q-Trust identifies informative queries from the attention of the user's request and selects the keys they point to through 2-hop attention, without training. A Triton kernel reuses FlashAttention's log-sum-exp to limit prefill overhead.
IKzzezuLKc.key_idea: Weight prefill queries by their relevance to the user request's attention, then propagate through a 2-hop attention path to select which keys to retain.
IKzzezuLKc.evidence: Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, and Mistral-7B-v0.3 on LongBench plus a needle task, against SnapKV and SnapKV with pooling.
IKzzezuLKc.claimed_gains: Improves accuracy over SnapKV by 1.72-2.56 points and over SnapKV with pooling by 0.78-1.58 points across three models, with prefill overhead limited to 3.5% for 16K-token prompts.
IKzzezuLKc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the query-informativeness analysis clear and the training-free scoring rule simple, with largest gains at the small 128-token budget and low kernel overhead.
IKzzezuLKc.main_concern: Closely related query-selection methods (e.g., Lookahead Q-Cache, NACL) lack direct comparison, SnapKV with pooling beats it on QA and retrieval tasks, and end-to-end latency is not reported.

0pOYfKBTmN.one_liner: Mem4Act learns a fixed-size latent memory for robot policies using multi-granularity aggregation, QA and DINO supervision, and memory-first training.
0pOYfKBTmN.problem: Long-horizon manipulation needs memory, but existing approaches either expose the policy to ever-longer histories or compress history in ways that can drop task-relevant temporal, semantic, and perceptual information.
0pOYfKBTmN.method: Mem4Act organizes history through multi-granularity temporal aggregation, keeps semantic and perceptual information via question answering and key-frame DINO feature reconstruction, and uses memory-first two-stage training to reduce reactive shortcuts. The result is a bounded, fixed-size latent memory interface to the action policy.
0pOYfKBTmN.key_idea: Aggregate history into fixed-size latent tokens at multiple temporal granularities, supervised by question answering and key-frame DINO reconstruction, with memory-first training so the policy uses them.
0pOYfKBTmN.evidence: Evaluated on RoboMME, RMBench, and four real-world manipulation tasks, with ablations on the auxiliary losses and temporal hierarchies.
0pOYfKBTmN.claimed_gains: Success rates of 49.88% on RoboMME, 61.0% on RMBench, and 81.50% on four real-world manipulation tasks.
0pOYfKBTmN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the empirical results are strong, the coverage/content/utilization decomposition is clear, and the ablations on auxiliary losses and temporal structure are extensive.
0pOYfKBTmN.main_concern: The semantic QA and DINO supervision depend on subgoal annotations and task-specific heuristics (QA templates, keyframes at subgoal boundaries), which may limit scalability.

1jP2hufr3z.one_liner: Derives effect-oriented guardrail rules, hardens them with counterexample-guided refinement, and adds agent-steer denial messages to curb agents' guardrail evasion.
1jP2hufr3z.problem: Blocking an unsafe tool call does not block its harmful effect because agents retry or reroute to reach the same outcome, and existing guardrails either let risky actions through or hinder legitimate work as agents disregard or misinterpret the verdict.
1jP2hufr3z.method: The system derives effect-oriented rules from reported incidents, hardens them against effect-preserving rewrites through counterexample-guided refinement, and augments each denial message with an agent-steer prompt that curbs evasion without disrupting legitimate work. One rule set transfers across agents, benchmarks, and harnesses.
1jP2hufr3z.key_idea: Rules target the effect of a tool call rather than its syntax and are refined against effect-preserving rewrites, while the denial message steers the agent to halt or reroute safely.
1jP2hufr3z.evidence: Four existing guardrails evaluated on RedCode and SABER across five settings, including a DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash agent in OpenCode, with Pareto comparisons of safety, utility, and cost against four baselines.
1jP2hufr3z.claimed_gains: On RedCode it cuts the attack success rate of a DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash agent in OpenCode from 49.7% to 7.8%, below every baseline, and lies on the Pareto front of safety, utility, and cost in all five settings.
1jP2hufr3z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that outcome-level evaluation of guardrail evasion addresses an important gap, with comprehensive experiments and ablations showing large attack-success reductions while preserving task success.
1jP2hufr3z.main_concern: Claims are scoped too broadly (the 'every guardrail' claim covers only four guardrails), the comparison disables ActPlane's native denial feedback, and evaluation assumes non-adaptive agents mostly in Linux shell settings.

eRW0CRmSe6.one_liner: On-policy self-distillation from the model's own predictions conditioned on privileged persona context to internalize persona-specific beliefs.
eRW0CRmSe6.problem: Persona prompting and fine-tuning yield persona-consistent behavior that can remain shallow, without changing the factual beliefs the model internally represents as true.
eRW0CRmSe6.method: Persona-SDFT is an on-policy self-distillation method that transfers a persona's worldview into a model from its own predictions conditioned on privileged context about that persona, using carefully structured persona-specific context. Reviews note KL-based teacher supervision and EMA updates.
eRW0CRmSe6.key_idea: Distill the model's own persona-context-conditioned predictions into the context-free model on-policy, so persona beliefs are absorbed into the weights rather than only prompted.
eRW0CRmSe6.evidence: Qwen3-8B across 15 historical personas (reviews also cite Llama) against Open Character Training and belief-modification baselines, with ablations, truth-representation probes, and a training-text overlap audit.
eRW0CRmSe6.claimed_gains: On Qwen3-8B across 15 historical personas, generalization to related persona beliefs rises from 55.5% to 77.4% and robustness under challenge from 45.6% to 66.8% versus Open Character Training with less observed GPU time, and truth-representation probe lift increases from 0.190 (the abstract is cut off before the new value).
eRW0CRmSe6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the persona belief internalization problem important and the results consistent across 15 personas, with strong baselines, thorough ablations, and valuable held-out belief evaluation.
eRW0CRmSe6.main_concern: The method largely reuses existing self-distillation and context-distillation ingredients, and baselines are neither tuned nor compute-matched.

v0xplpuNyk.one_liner: SeaStar-TS pretrains light-curve encoders by uncertainty-aware masked prediction of photometry and aligns them with class descriptions
v0xplpuNyk.problem: Hand-crafted features remain strong baselines for classifying irregular, noisy astronomical light curves, and far more variable stars and transients exist than can receive detailed follow-up.
v0xplpuNyk.method: Learns representations directly from photometry by predicting masked observations while accounting for measurement uncertainty (a Gaussian KL objective per a reviewer). Aligns representations with class names and descriptions to enable top-k recognition of classes omitted from supervised training.
v0xplpuNyk.key_idea: Pretrain by masked-observation prediction with a Gaussian KL objective that uses each measurement's uncertainty, then align embeddings to class descriptions for unseen-class recognition.
v0xplpuNyk.evidence: ELAsTiCC, MACHO, StarEmbed, and LEAVES under different label budgets and observing conditions, with ablations.
v0xplpuNyk.claimed_gains: Surpasses hand-crafted-feature baselines on ELAsTiCC and LEAVES; on StarEmbed its linear and MLP readouts exceed the feature-based readouts, and on MACHO it has the highest listed scores at two label budgets.
v0xplpuNyk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the evaluation across four datasets and label budgets, a principled and simple uncertainty-aware pretraining design, and comprehensive ablations.
v0xplpuNyk.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited, and the value of pretraining and semantic alignment is questioned (uncalibrated held-out top-1 accuracy of 3.5% is below the 5% chance level, and random initialization does well).

hRi4lYK2Y7.one_liner: Learned step-size predictor and handoff policy that warm-start PDHG for large-scale linear programs to cut end-to-end solve time.
hRi4lYK2Y7.problem: Unrolled neural accelerators for first-order LP solvers trade solver time for inference time poorly: each layer touches every variable and constraint, predicted iterates still need refinement, and every instance runs the same layers.
hRi4lYK2Y7.method: A weight-shared predictor reads compact solver statistics and rescales the primal and dual step sizes of a first-order LP solver while keeping its update rules, for a short warm-start phase. A learned handoff policy sets the number of warm-start iterations per instance and target accuracy, after which the solver finishes under its own termination criterion.
hRi4lYK2Y7.key_idea: Predict step-size rescalings from compact solver statistics while keeping PDHG updates, and learn per instance when to hand off to the plain solver, trained on wall-clock time.
hRi4lYK2Y7.evidence: Packing linear programs with up to 10^7 (abstract truncated); reviewers state evaluation uses only two synthetic families, packing and PageRank LPs, with no real-world or standard benchmarks.
hRi4lYK2Y7.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is truncated before any results.
hRi4lYK2Y7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that optimizing end-to-end solve time is a well-motivated objective and that the method is clear and preserves PDHG update directions, with the adaptive handoff seen as a practical idea.
hRi4lYK2Y7.main_concern: Evaluation covers only two synthetic LP families with no real-world or standard-benchmark instances, and novelty over PDHG-Net and RL-based learning-to-optimize work is questioned.

kJvgLmqvuz.one_liner: Recursive Successor Models learn short-horizon successor distributions with supervised training and compose them recursively at planning time.
kJvgLmqvuz.problem: One-step world models compound prediction errors in long-horizon planning, while bootstrapped successor-measure training is unstable.
kJvgLmqvuz.method: A supervised objective without bootstrapping learns successor distributions, and a recursive sampling procedure composes short-horizon distributions into long-horizon ones for planning.
kJvgLmqvuz.key_idea: Train successor measures with a non-bootstrapped supervised loss, and move long-horizon composition to inference by recursively sampling and chaining short-horizon distributions.
kJvgLmqvuz.evidence: Simulated benchmarks, including visual tasks, and real-world robot experiments, with ablations on key hyperparameters.
kJvgLmqvuz.claimed_gains: Improvements in policy performance, planning latency, and training convergence speed; no numbers stated.
kJvgLmqvuz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the decoupling of stable training from inference-time composition is a neat idea with solid simulated and real-robot validation.
kJvgLmqvuz.main_concern: Performance is bounded by an external proposal policy used for one-step best-of-N action selection, which cannot iteratively improve the policy.

el0jXlbsg5.one_liner: Trains white-box probes on the FIBS deception dataset, using an axial multi-layer multi-token probe, to detect sabotage and unverbalized deception.
el0jXlbsg5.problem: Monitoring LLM agents for deception and sabotage is hard, and black-box monitors cannot catch deception that is not verbalized in the transcript.
el0jXlbsg5.method: The authors collect FIBS, described as the largest deception dataset to date, and train probes with a novel architecture that aggregates information across many layers and tokens (an Axial probe that factorizes attention, per reviews). They evaluate on agentic coding benchmarks, introspective deception cases, and open-weight models lying about politically sensitive topics.
el0jXlbsg5.key_idea: Factorize attention over layers and tokens in a probe so activations can be aggregated cheaply, and train it on a large, diverse deception dataset.
el0jXlbsg5.evidence: SHADE-Arena and BashArena against text monitors, hidden-goal transcript discrimination, open-weight models lying on political topics, and transfer studies across training data families.
el0jXlbsg5.claimed_gains: 98.7% AUROC in SHADE-Arena and 98.0% in BashArena versus 97.7% and 97.6% for the strongest action-only text monitors, and up to 99.7% AUROC distinguishing a true hidden goal from other goals.
el0jXlbsg5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree FIBS and the systematic comparisons of data scale, diversity, and probe architecture are a substantial contribution showing probes generalize beyond their training settings.
el0jXlbsg5.main_concern: SHADE-Arena labels stay positive after sabotage onset and the probe relies on prefilled interrogation prompts, so results do not show timely detection of the first harmful action or deployment benefit.

QQpbfJFLca.one_liner: Proves pass@k lets learning from suboptimal demonstrations reach 1/eps sample complexity rather than 1/eps^2, using a greedy multiplicative-weights learner.
QQpbfJFLca.problem: Prior pass@k results assume optimal demonstrators, and it is unclear how multiple responses help when the demonstrator is not optimal.
QQpbfJFLca.method: In a finite reward-class model they derive matching upper and lower bounds under standard evaluation (reward fixed before training) and robust evaluation (one policy competes for every reward), and give a greedy multiplicative-weights learner achieving the upper bounds with no assumption on demonstrator quality.
QQpbfJFLca.key_idea: Let the learner return k responses that jointly cover different reward possibilities, so competing with a single-response demonstrator gives faster rates and better dependence on reward-class size.
QQpbfJFLca.evidence: Theoretical upper and lower bounds in a finite reward-class model; no experiments are described.
QQpbfJFLca.claimed_gains: Moving from pass@1 to any pass@k with k>=2 changes the worst-case dependence on target accuracy from 1/eps^2 to 1/eps, and under standard evaluation the dependence on reward class size N improves from log N to log N / log k.
QQpbfJFLca.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the matching bounds and the separation of the two benefits (faster accuracy rate versus reward-class dependence) are sound contributions for the practically relevant pass@k setting.
QQpbfJFLca.main_concern: The learner is not efficiently implementable for large reward classes, bounds scale with the log of the reward class size, analysis is limited to single-step settings, and the single-response demonstrator benchmark makes the 1/eps result less surprising.

n5HOLyOBdb.one_liner: LIVE-MLA corrects compressed-token value residuals in closed form from the exact recent window and weights conversion by attention mass.
n5HOLyOBdb.problem: Converting MHA or GQA models to MLA by low-rank decomposition leaves reconstruction residuals that fixed low-rank mappings cannot adapt to during inference.
n5HOLyOBdb.method: Residual Feedback fits sequence-specific value corrections in closed form from observed latent and value pairs as tokens leave a small exact recent region. Attention-weighted conversion weights each token's joint key-value reconstruction objective by the attention mass it receives, within a fixed cache budget.
n5HOLyOBdb.key_idea: Use the exact recent window as supervision to fit closed-form value corrections for older compressed tokens, and weight low-rank fitting by attention mass rather than raw KV error.
n5HOLyOBdb.evidence: Perplexity experiments on 8B models (Qwen3-8B-Base per a review) against training-free conversion baselines, with ablations, a byte-matched larger-window comparison, and decoding-efficiency timing.
n5HOLyOBdb.claimed_gains: Narrows the perplexity gap left by training-free conversion and further reduces recovery training (abstract text cuts off); no numbers stated.
n5HOLyOBdb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the techniques are principled and well supported, and that Residual Feedback offers more than simply keeping additional recent tokens.
n5HOLyOBdb.main_concern: Quality evaluations stop at 2K-4K contexts despite the long-context motivation, and the converted model keeps an exact recent KV window so it is not strictly MLA, complicating baseline comparisons.

ng3co6hvgZ.one_liner: Shows models use fewer tokens per task when tasks are composed, then groups tasks by fragility to cut token use.
ng3co6hvgZ.problem: Language models make many more errors when tasks are composed in one prompt even when each task is solved reliably in isolation, which independent error accumulation does not fully explain.
ng3co6hvgZ.method: Measures errors and per-task token use under composition across open-weight models and a frontier model, identifies fragile tasks as those needing longer solution traces in isolation, and groups tasks by fragility to manipulate the implicit budgeting.
ng3co6hvgZ.key_idea: Models implicitly shrink the thinking budget per task as tasks are composed, so tasks needing long traces become fragile; batching by fragility reallocates tokens.
ng3co6hvgZ.evidence: Math and linguistic tasks across open-weight models and a frontier model, comparing per-task token use and accuracy in isolation versus composition.
ng3co6hvgZ.claimed_gains: Grouping tasks by fragility reduces token usage by 43% across a range of math and linguistic tasks while preserving accuracy.
ng3co6hvgZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem practical, the unchanged-question control useful, and the power-law, implicit-budget, and fragility findings interesting and supported by the evidence.
ng3co6hvgZ.main_concern: Budget misallocation is not isolated as the cause, since batching also changes attention, order, and context, and parts of the finding such as shorter reasoning under batching appear in prior work.

30PUC2sxCa.one_liner: Determines the minimax regret of online isotonic regression on every finite poset and attains it with a polynomial-time Gumbel-perturbation learner.
30PUC2sxCa.problem: Efficient algorithms and the minimax rate for online isotonic regression on arbitrary partial orders were open problems posed by Kotłowski, Koolen and Malek and by Wang's conjecture.
30PUC2sxCa.method: The paper proves a squared-loss minimax regret that depends on the logarithm of Stanley's order polynomial, and gives a learner that perturbs scores with low-dimensional Gumbel noise and samples maximizers using one minimum cut per sample, with Gibbs domination showing this costs only a constant factor.
30PUC2sxCa.key_idea: Replace #P-hard exponential-weights prediction with Gumbel-perturbed score maximization solved by minimum cuts, with Gibbs domination bounding the regret cost to a constant factor.
30PUC2sxCa.evidence: Theory: matching upper and lower bounds for squared loss and log loss and a broad class of exp-concave losses; no experiments.
30PUC2sxCa.claimed_gains: Minimax regret is Θ(min{T, inf over K≥1 of [H_P(K) + T/K^2]}) on every finite poset up to absolute constants, where H_P(K) is the logarithm of Stanley's order polynomial at K+1.
30PUC2sxCa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper settles a recognized open problem with a tight characterization of minimax regret on every finite poset and a polynomial-time learner.
30PUC2sxCa.main_concern: Reviewers say the paper is dense and hard to follow, especially the algorithm section, with no simulations or runtime discussion, and one adds that constants are far apart and the exponential-weights upper bound is classical.

lb6Sg4Ue8t.one_liner: Simulation-free trajectory inference by regressing an acceleration field in phase space whose induced trajectories match prescribed marginals.
lb6Sg4Ue8t.problem: Existing trajectory inference methods carry computational burdens such as explicit spline constructions or simulating trajectories during training.
lb6Sg4Ue8t.method: Acceleration Matching lifts interpolation to phase space and regresses an explicit conditional acceleration field that induces random trajectories with smooth positional paths whose marginals agree under suitable assumptions; it needs only positional data and samples training states and targets by direct Gaussian conditioning.
lb6Sg4Ue8t.key_idea: Regress a conditional acceleration field of a kinetic Brownian process in phase space, sampling training states by Gaussian conditioning on velocity knots given all observed positions.
lb6Sg4Ue8t.evidence: Numerical experiments on several benchmark problems from the literature, with some baseline results taken from published papers (per reviews).
lb6Sg4Ue8t.claimed_gains: Competitive with or superior to existing algorithms on several benchmark problems; no numbers stated.
lb6Sg4Ue8t.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree Acceleration Matching is a novel, simulation-free extension of flow matching to second-order dynamics with smooth trajectories and theoretical grounding.
lb6Sg4Ue8t.main_concern: Reviewers say evidence for the claimed computational efficiency is missing, results are sensitive to the diffusion coefficient and initial velocity distribution without thorough study, and relevance to single-cell overdamped dynamics is unclear.

mvhZgiG0fa.one_liner: Contrastive encoder maps LFP segments to subject-agnostic functional coordinates used as transformer tokens across heterogeneous intracranial recordings.
mvhZgiG0fa.problem: Electrode count, placement and regional coverage vary across subjects, and anatomical coordinates such as MNI can fail to capture functional similarity.
mvhZgiG0fa.method: An encoder trained with contrastive objectives maps short LFP segments into a subject-agnostic embedding space, giving each electrode a functional identity. These functional coordinates serve as tokens for a transformer that models inter-regional relationships over variable channel sets.
mvhZgiG0fa.key_idea: Replace anatomical position embeddings with contrastively learned, signal-derived electrode embeddings that serve as transformer tokens for variable channel sets.
mvhZgiG0fa.evidence: Evaluated on a 20-subject basal ganglia-thalamic LFP dataset with heterogeneous electrode layouts (region-consistent clusters, within-subject discrimination, zero-shot transfer to unseen channels, cross-region LFP prediction); reviews also mention a public movie-viewing dataset.
mvhZgiG0fa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper clearly written and the learned representations cluster semantically by region, with functional coordinates improving cross-region reconstruction over MNI coordinates and region labels.
mvhZgiG0fa.main_concern: Evaluation is narrow: no downstream decoding task or comparison with Population Transformer, seegnificant or BaRISTA, and region labels used for contrastive training may reintroduce atlas dependence.

IxrXZ2FHdn.one_liner: Online safe RL method that backpropagates an augmented Lagrangian through a flow policy's generation path without score estimation.
IxrXZ2FHdn.problem: Gaussian actors can collapse onto one mode and primal-dual optimization over a nonconvex Lagrangian is unstable, while diffusion-actor methods need score estimation of an augmented-Lagrangian target.
IxrXZ2FHdn.method: RAFALE is an off-policy actor-critic that differentiates the augmented objective directly through the flow policy's generation path, adds FLAC's density-free kinetic-energy regularizer, and formulates the update as a constrained one-ended generalized Schrödinger bridge.
IxrXZ2FHdn.key_idea: Differentiate the augmented Lagrangian through the flow sampler with a kinetic-energy regularizer, a path-space bridge that reduces to an entropy-regularized action-space problem.
IxrXZ2FHdn.evidence: Theory derives the bridge reduction and cost-threshold reweighting; per the reviews, experiments use seven safe-RL tasks with five training seeds and a constraint-objective ablation.
IxrXZ2FHdn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is a coherent, computationally simple constrained flow-policy update that avoids score estimation, with clear derivations and competitive reward-cost trade-offs.
IxrXZ2FHdn.main_concern: Incremental novelty: RAFALE mainly combines FLAC's flow actor and kinetic regularization with an existing augmented-Lagrangian safety objective, and the ablations do not isolate the proposed mechanism.

AMbe31KIhr.one_liner: Compares student and teacher reasoning steps by expected return, then routes on-policy learning by trajectory outcome with step-level modulation.
AMbe31KIhr.problem: On-policy reasoning models can learn from task rewards or teacher signals, but these differ in form and can favor conflicting updates, so it is unclear which should guide a given step.
AMbe31KIhr.method: ERSR treats semantic reasoning steps as macro-actions and uses Monte Carlo student rollouts to estimate the expected final reward of student and teacher-proposed steps; R²OPL reinforces the student on successful trajectories and distills the teacher on failed ones, scaled by group success rate and student-probe gains.
AMbe31KIhr.key_idea: Estimate the expected final reward of student versus teacher-replaced steps from the same prefix, then reinforce on successful trajectories and distill from the teacher on failed ones.
AMbe31KIhr.evidence: Experiments across reasoning benchmarks and teacher-student configurations with ERSR analysis and ablations; reviewers cite Qwen 4B teachers with 1.7B and 4B students plus a Gemma configuration.
AMbe31KIhr.claimed_gains: R²OPL consistently outperforms strong baselines; no numbers are visible in the truncated abstract.
AMbe31KIhr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree ERSR is a useful diagnostic and that routing signals by trajectory outcome is intuitive, with broad gains across benchmarks and modest training overhead.
AMbe31KIhr.main_concern: The increment over SRPO is limited and the tuning protocol is unclear: answer-probe modulation adds little (59.4 to 58.8 when removed), baselines were modified and given different step budgets, and runs use a single seed.

o6HslrXCN0.one_liner: Analyzes how outliers evolve into persistent hot channels in NVFP4 pretraining and patches them online with residual compensation.
o6HslrXCN0.problem: NVFP4 pretraining keeps a persistent loss gap to BF16 because FP4's limited dynamic range makes training sensitive to outliers.
o6HslrXCN0.method: A longitudinal analysis locates outliers in architectural components (Softmax in SA, gating in LA, SwiGLU in FFN); Hot-Channel Patch identifies hot channels online and reinjects residuals with hardware-efficient kernels, and the CHON recipe adds protection of post-QK operations.
o6HslrXCN0.key_idea: Outliers become a small set of persistent hot channels, so identify them online and reinject their quantization residuals through extra NVFP4 GEMM channels.
o6HslrXCN0.evidence: Longitudinal outlier analysis across softmax and linear attention architectures, and a GLA-1.3B model trained on 90.6B tokens compared with BF16, with ablations.
o6HslrXCN0.claimed_gains: On GLA-1.3B trained for 90.6B tokens, CHON reduces the loss gap to BF16 from 0.94% to 0.58% while maintaining downstream (sentence truncated in the abstract).
o6HslrXCN0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the longitudinal outlier analysis is informative and that hot-channel compensation is a hardware-friendly design with controllable overhead.
o6HslrXCN0.main_concern: The practical benefit is under-evidenced: no measured memory or end-to-end throughput, the fixed 9.09% compensation ratio is unjustified, and causal explanations for outliers rest on correlations.

Q7duoTYzkL.one_liner: Trains a vision-language companion with nested credit assignment to decide when to intervene and what advice to give.
Q7duoTYzkL.problem: Proactive assistance requires jointly deciding when to intervene and what to say, but downstream task outcomes give ambiguous feedback for both decisions.
Q7duoTYzkL.method: PACE is an RL framework that compares estimated returns under silence and under alternative advice from the same interaction state to derive separate learning signals for intervention timing and conditional advice generation, jointly optimized against intervention cost.
Q7duoTYzkL.key_idea: Compare estimated returns of staying silent versus giving alternative advice from the same state, yielding separate credit for the intervention decision and the advice content.
Q7duoTYzkL.evidence: Experiments with multiple LLM-controlled players in ALFWorld and Minecraft against general-purpose LLMs and specialized companions, plus shared-credit PPO/GRPO comparisons and a 20-participant human study per the reviews.
Q7duoTYzkL.claimed_gains: Higher overall task success rates with lower intervention rates than general-purpose LLMs and specialized baselines; no numbers are visible in the truncated abstract.
Q7duoTYzkL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating feedback for intervention timing from advice content, with a silence branch, addresses a real attribution problem and is supported by ablations.
Q7duoTYzkL.main_concern: Evidence is narrow: only two environments with separately trained policies, limited isolation of why nested credit beats shared credit, and little direct validation of long-term credit estimates.

PqbSUqMSXs.one_liner: Scales compute that agents spend before the task arrives and while tools run, measuring accuracy-compute trade-offs.
PqbSUqMSXs.problem: Agents that can see their environment's context, such as a code repository, before a task arrives idle while waiting for the task and for tool calls.
PqbSUqMSXs.method: They scale proactive compute with budget forcing to study the context offline, use multi-agent parallel and serial studying when the context exceeds one window, and have agents keep working while commands run after the task arrives.
PqbSUqMSXs.key_idea: Spend idle time before and during the task on token-level study of the environment context, using budget forcing and parallel study agents, to replace later test-time work.
PqbSUqMSXs.evidence: Nine benchmarks in software engineering, legal work, algorithmic reasoning and mathematics on four model families, plus Harvey LAB's 134M-token legal filesystem and eight MLE-Bench tasks.
PqbSUqMSXs.claimed_gains: A 128k-token study lets a solver at T=64 match accuracy that otherwise needs a 7-221× larger test budget; on SWE-QA-Pro a 16k-token study more than halves test-time reasoning and cuts tool calls tenfold at matched performance; online agents reach the median human score 1.6-2.0× sooner on eight MLE-Bench tasks.
PqbSUqMSXs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled budget sweeps across many benchmarks and models show that idle-time preparation can substitute for downstream reactive compute.
PqbSUqMSXs.main_concern: The contribution over prior sleep-time compute and idle-time planning work is unclear, and the approach relies on hand-crafted prompting heuristics with hard-to-read result figures.

0vChnbhrut.one_liner: Decomposes variance-explained fidelity under distribution shift into reference credit, mean offset and centered fit, with a convex-set bound.
0vChnbhrut.problem: A single reconstruction-fidelity score mixes reference credit, mean error and centered fit under distribution shift, so it can mislead when judging transferred representations.
0vChnbhrut.method: Separates the score into classical mean-bias and centered-error terms and proves that for reconstructions confined to a convex set the score is at most the translated fit minus the squared distance from the target mean to the set. It tests this on archetypal dictionaries over text embeddings and on sparse autoencoders.
0vChnbhrut.key_idea: For convex reconstruction sets, geometry alone bounds the score by the translated fit minus the squared distance from the target mean to the set, which can force negative scores.
0vChnbhrut.evidence: Cross-corpus transfer of archetypal dictionaries (K = 32) over text embeddings in 48 settings, plus a sparse autoencoder study on Gemma 2 2B with Gemma Scope SAEs over three layers and five text distributions.
0vChnbhrut.claimed_gains: In cross-corpus transfer, 37 of 48 settings score below the target mean, and transferred dictionaries reach 32-77% of the target-informed translated fit.
0vChnbhrut.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the accounting is correct and clearly separates classical from new results, with convincing controlled-translation experiments and clear exposition.
0vChnbhrut.main_concern: The theory is a short step beyond classical results and the demonstrated harm is confined to niche cross-corpus archetypal transfer, with little overlap with standard sparse autoencoders.

ea9pUx9xjy.one_liner: Advantage-based on-policy distillation weights teacher actions by their counterfactual advantage under the student, estimated from student rollouts alone.
ea9pUx9xjy.problem: Standard on-policy distillation makes the student follow the teacher at every state, assuming teacher guidance always helps even when the student cannot use it.
ea9pUx9xjy.method: AOPD weights teacher actions by counterfactual advantage under the student. An estimator using teacher importance weights on student-sampled actions and terminal rewards gives unbiased advantage-weighted supervision without extra rollouts or reward evaluations.
ea9pUx9xjy.key_idea: Estimate each teacher action's advantage under the student via teacher importance weights on student-sampled actions and terminal rewards, reinforcing only actions that raise expected outcome.
ea9pUx9xjy.evidence: Math, coding and Medqa experiments in external-teacher and self-distillation settings against distillation (OPD, OPSD, KDRL) and RL (GRPO) baselines.
ea9pUx9xjy.claimed_gains: Gains over distillation and RL baselines in both external-teacher and self-distillation settings; no numbers stated.
ea9pUx9xjy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the distinction between teacher preference and student benefit is well motivated, the estimator reuses existing student rollouts, and experiments cover several domains and both teacher settings.
ea9pUx9xjy.main_concern: Attribution of gains is unclear: AOPD uses different sampling settings than OPD and OPSD, the advantage-centering term lacks an ablation, and the closest advantage-aware baseline is missing.

HgbFRA7qA5.one_liner: NeuBridge extends Schrödinger bridges variationally to infer stochastic latent dynamics and implied control from neural population activity.
HgbFRA7qA5.problem: Recovering low-dimensional dynamics from spontaneous neural activity is hard because there are no repeated trials or known inputs and the network shifts between internally generated and externally driven states.
HgbFRA7qA5.method: NeuBridge is a variational Schrödinger-bridge model that infers stochastic latent dynamics and the posterior control needed to move activity away from its intrinsic dynamics. It is fit to Neuropixels recordings from the brainstem of sleeping mice with optogenetic perturbation.
HgbFRA7qA5.key_idea: Treat latent neural trajectories as a Schrödinger bridge from intrinsic dynamics, so the control cost of the inferred posterior marks external perturbation.
HgbFRA7qA5.evidence: Large-scale Neuropixels brainstem recordings from sleeping mice across sleep-wake states with optogenetic stimulation, compared with existing latent-dynamics methods such as LFADS and FINDR.
HgbFRA7qA5.claimed_gains: Reconstructs firing rates more accurately than existing latent-dynamics methods and detects a clear increase in control cost during laser stimulation without being given its timing; no numbers stated.
HgbFRA7qA5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written, validated on real data against popular alternatives, and that inferring a control signal across recordings is a useful addition to latent-dynamics modeling.
HgbFRA7qA5.main_concern: Comparison and validation are incomplete: input-inferring baselines such as LFADS, ILQR-VAE and MR-LFADS are not compared on inferred inputs, and the control signal is not validated on synthetic data with known inputs.

MiQ3KbkgA3.one_liner: LLM-built task-relationship graphs combined with online learning progress estimate downstream benefit and readiness to guide curriculum decisions in RL.
MiQ3KbkgA3.problem: Local learning-progress signals miss the downstream value of training on a task, so the consequences of curriculum decisions are hard to predict.
MiQ3KbkgA3.method: Combines online learning-progress estimates with LLM-informed estimates of each task's potential downstream benefit and of whether direct training on it is currently likely to produce progress, using an offline LLM-built graph.
MiQ3KbkgA3.key_idea: Augment local learning progress with LLM-estimated downstream transfer benefit and current trainability of each task, computed offline from task and learner descriptions.
MiQ3KbkgA3.evidence: A custom benchmark of 256 textual goals in Craftax under different curriculum objectives, with five seeds per reviews and learners with different cross-task transfer mechanisms.
MiQ3KbkgA3.claimed_gains: Strongest gains when optimizing for individual target tasks; across the full task set, gains range from modest learning-speed improvements to larger gains that persist through the end of training; no numbers stated.
MiQ3KbkgA3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating recent learning progress from a task's downstream value is a clear, meaningful motivation and that the offline LLM-derived graph adds useful task knowledge.
MiQ3KbkgA3.main_concern: Evidence is narrow and partly confounded: a single LLM and a single Craftax benchmark, single-target selection screened with a shared seed, and missing baselines such as Tzannetos et al. (2024).

xOEtVpkpjU.one_liner: Auto-generates simulated web and MCP applications for prompt-injection evaluation, with a fork-based tree search that times and revises injections.
xOEtVpkpjU.problem: Evaluating agents against indirect prompt injection needs controllable, realistic environments, but building them manually is costly and hard to scale.
xOEtVpkpjU.method: ArenaWeaver simulates well-known applications from public documentation into composable interactive worlds with browser and MCP access. Counterfactual Forking Search uses recorded interactions and agent feedback to choose where to fork and how to deliver or revise injections.
xOEtVpkpjU.key_idea: Generate application simulators from documentation with shared browser and MCP state, and search injections by forking recorded agent runs at chosen points (Counterfactual Forking Search).
xOEtVpkpjU.evidence: A suite of 40 services with 1,263 web-UI routes and 1,179 MCP tools, and evaluation of 25 frontier models on 660 curated cases with environment-suspicion analysis and blinded judge validation.
xOEtVpkpjU.claimed_gains: Evaluating 25 frontier models on 660 curated cases reveals systematic robustness differences, and successful attacks often remain effective across interfaces; no performance gain for the search method is stated.
xOEtVpkpjU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the infrastructure is the main contribution: browser and MCP access over shared, resettable state enables controlled security experiments, backed by a large and careful evaluation.
xOEtVpkpjU.main_concern: Counterfactual Forking Search is never compared with a baseline such as full-restart search and its novelty is limited (checkpoint-and-branch with an LLM attacker), while outcome judging relies heavily on LLM judges.

eTU28s1e2I.one_liner: Reward model trained on within-trajectory progress relations from task events, anchored by demonstration temporal labels, for robot RL shaping.
eTU28s1e2I.problem: Reward models trained on normalized temporal labels from successful demonstrations mistake setbacks for progress, while failed and suboptimal executions lack usable absolute progress labels.
eTU28s1e2I.method: Event2Reward supervises progress predictions with within-trajectory progress relations supported by task events and combines them with temporal labels from successful demonstrations to fix the numerical scale. It is trained on an event-annotated dataset from about 100K real robot execution records and adapted with a few target-task executions.
eTU28s1e2I.key_idea: Learn progress from ordering relations between events within a trajectory so setbacks lower predicted progress, while demonstration time labels anchor the scale.
eTU28s1e2I.evidence: 40 tasks across four LIBERO suites and real-world SERL insertion and DSRL manipulation tasks under matched 30-minute wall-clock training budgets.
eTU28s1e2I.claimed_gains: Improves LIBERO suite-average success by 9.96-13.76 percentage points over the strongest baseline; in the real world reaches 60.0% versus 37.8% for Robometer on three SERL insertion tasks and 90.0% versus 81.7% for a baseline on three DSRL tasks.
eTU28s1e2I.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning reward from failure and recovery through relative progress is a well-motivated idea that improves policy learning over reward-model baselines.
eTU28s1e2I.main_concern: It is unclear why the method works, since the main text lacks ablations or analyses, annotation cost for about 100K rollouts is unreported, and comparison with VLM-based rewards is missing.

cVWMBb3mjv.one_liner: Characterizes the exact fixed-confidence cost of choosing whether the next trajectory keeps or resets the hidden task in meta-RL.
cVWMBb3mjv.problem: Meta-RL treats the grouping of trajectories into tasks as fixed, yet retaining or resetting the hidden task changes the statistical experiment and episodewise acquisition can carry zero information.
cVWMBb3mjv.method: Constructs finite meta-MDPs where a persistent experiment is informative while every episodewise experiment is not, then characterizes the exact fixed-confidence source cost for bounded finite persistent meta-MDPs as a Bellman-Chernoff game, computed with certified column generation.
cVWMBb3mjv.key_idea: Price the reset-or-continue choice as a Bellman-Chernoff dynamic program in which the next episodic policy and stopping rule face a least-favorable target alternative.
cVWMBb3mjv.evidence: Theory: separation constructions for every r >= 2, an exact characterization over randomized history-dependent experiment trees, certified approximate-design guarantees, and a calibration example (the abstract is truncated).
cVWMBb3mjv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the reset-or-continue acquisition decision is a meaningful formulation and that the examples showing episodewise acquisition can fail to identify the target are useful, with an exact fixed-confidence price.
cVWMBb3mjv.main_concern: The approximate-design theorem needs an explicit deterministic Cesaro-vanishing error envelope as in Theorem E.17, and the contribution over a reset-as-action POMDP formulation is unclear.

O2i4OKi55c.one_liner: Maps predicted trajectories into layered executable physical explanations, kinematic models, control laws and scene references, for counterfactual motion planning.
O2i4OKi55c.problem: Predicted ego and agent trajectories give little insight into the physical mechanisms behind the motion and are hard to vary systematically for counterfactual reasoning.
O2i4OKi55c.method: PHLEX is a predictor-agnostic framework that explains each predicted trajectory through kinematic models, longitudinal and lateral control laws and scene references. The explanations are executed and varied to generate counterfactual ego and agent futures that refine the ego plan.
O2i4OKi55c.key_idea: Express predicted motion as executable layers of kinematics, control laws and scene references, then perturb those mechanisms to generate physically grounded counterfactual futures.
O2i4OKi55c.evidence: Multiple predictors and datasets, stated as open-loop and closed-loop evaluation in the abstract (a reviewer reports all evaluations are open-loop), with ablation studies.
O2i4OKi55c.claimed_gains: Improves physical feasibility and planning safety while preserving trajectory accuracy; no numbers stated.
O2i4OKi55c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the executable, interpretable layered motion representation is interesting and gives consistent improvements across multiple predictor families, reducing kinematic violations and collisions.
O2i4OKi55c.main_concern: Evidence for planning benefit is thin: evaluation is open-loop, stronger physics-constrained refinement baselines are missing, and reliance on HD map information is unclear.

Qd5CJggfJb.one_liner: Learns forward and reverse-time latent dynamics from correct procedures and scores clinical skill by discrepancy from them.
Qd5CJggfJb.problem: VLMs recognize events but do not reliably track how interactions update procedural state and verify whether the resulting state evolution is valid, as clinical skill assessment requires.
Qd5CJggfJb.method: ATV organizes video into temporally aligned object-centric states, learns a forward predictor and a reverse-time reflector only from correctly performed procedures, and converts discrepancies between observed and normative transitions into rubric-conditioned evidence for scoring. The authors also build the ClinSkill-V dataset.
Qd5CJggfJb.key_idea: Verify procedures against normative dynamics: anticipate expected object-state evolution forward, check compatibility with antecedents in reverse, and score the discrepancy against a rubric.
Qd5CJggfJb.evidence: ClinSkill-V, 15,775 step-aligned clinical skill clips from 544 examination recordings with expert rubric-based ordinal scores, compared with MLLM and latent predictive baselines, plus ablations.
Qd5CJggfJb.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract gives only the ClinSkill-V size of 15,775 clips.
Qd5CJggfJb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that verifying against normative state dynamics is a well-motivated formulation and that ClinSkill-V is a useful, carefully annotated dataset for procedural skill assessment.
Qd5CJggfJb.main_concern: Baseline comparisons are confounded by different scoring losses and prompts, and experiments do not isolate state-transition reasoning (no order-invariant baseline) or test multi-step state tracking.

7wOZfGOW1n.one_liner: Carries a Continuous Thought Machine action expert's internal state across decisions in a VLA instead of resetting it each step.
7wOZfGOW1n.problem: Most VLA models restart the action expert at every decision, discarding evidence the robot can no longer see and computation the next decision could reuse.
7wOZfGOW1n.method: LycoReco uses a Continuous Thought Machine expert whose internal state persists across decisions and is refined with each new observation. It is compared with reset experts trained identically except for state lifetime.
7wOZfGOW1n.key_idea: Make state lifetime an architectural choice: the action expert keeps and refines its internal state across observations rather than reinitializing at each decision.
7wOZfGOW1n.evidence: Matched carry-versus-reset experiments on LIBERO, SIMPLER-WidowX and MIKASA memory tasks, plus a paired-cue test with identical current inputs and differing earlier cues.
7wOZfGOW1n.claimed_gains: LycoReco reaches 97.5% on LIBERO and 64.6% on SIMPLER-WidowX and leads compared systems on MIKASA memory tasks at 62.6%; carry with one internal update outperforms reset with twelve, and a review cites 25.8% for the reset variant on MIKASA.
7wOZfGOW1n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the matched carry-versus-reset design, especially the paired-cue experiment, isolates state lifetime and shows memory benefits.
7wOZfGOW1n.main_concern: The contribution beyond existing recurrent and memory-enabled policies is unclear, and the efficiency claim is not validated in the configuration behind the headline LIBERO result (K=1 frozen encoder versus K=10 adapted encoder).

spFrOKHwhv.one_liner: Single-step latent flow matching generates task-conditioned textual skills that an LLM decoder turns into guidance for a frozen agent.
spFrOKHwhv.problem: Textual skills for LLM agents depend on manually curated skill banks, retrieval, or reinforcement learning with indirect and delayed feedback.
spFrOKHwhv.method: SkillFM encodes and reconstructs textual skills in a continuous latent space with a codec, trains a conditional flow model with improved MeanFlow, samples a latent in one step at inference, and decodes it with an LLM into guidance for a frozen downstream agent.
spFrOKHwhv.key_idea: Generate skills by single-step MeanFlow sampling in a learned latent space, replacing test-time retrieval with task-conditioned generation.
spFrOKHwhv.evidence: Embodied tasks (ALFWorld), question answering (Search-QA) and web shopping (WebShop), with component ablations and cross-executor-family tests.
spFrOKHwhv.claimed_gains: Best overall performance among compared vector-based skill approaches on ALFWorld and Search-QA; a review cites 82.14% on seen and 84.33% on unseen ALFWorld tasks.
spFrOKHwhv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree one generator can serve different frozen executors, with encouraging ALFWorld results, cross-family transfer and supporting ablations.
spFrOKHwhv.main_concern: Evidence that latent flow generation beats retrieval is weak: baselines come from prior published results rather than a shared pipeline, the ablations fall below the no-skill baseline, and the Search-QA evaluation policy used test-set information.

iaUaspHLht.one_liner: Rewards agents for actions that are more informative about team return given teammates' actions, measured as partial-information-decomposition synergy.
iaUaspHLht.problem: Cooperative MARL lacks a reliable way to quantify task-relevant synergy among agents and turn it into a policy-learning signal.
iaUaspHLht.method: SDM defines synergistic dependency through Partial Information Decomposition as synergy beyond redundancy between an agent's action and the multi-step team return given teammates' actions. It estimates this conservatively and uses it to guide policy optimization while keeping the original task objective for value estimation.
iaUaspHLht.key_idea: Maximize a conservatively estimated PID synergy term: the extra information an agent's action carries about team return once teammates' actions are known.
iaUaspHLht.evidence: MPE, MAMuJoCo, SMAC and SMACv2, as an add-on to MAPPO and HAPPO, against policy-optimization baselines and explicit coordination objectives.
iaUaspHLht.claimed_gains: Consistent improvements over strong multi-agent policy optimization baselines and existing explicit coordination objectives; a review notes positive gains in all 12 MAMuJoCo backbone comparisons.
iaUaspHLht.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the information-theoretic framing is clear, plugs into MAPPO and HAPPO without changing execution, and gives gains on four benchmarks.
iaUaspHLht.main_concern: The synergy criterion does not isolate coordination (it is positive for separable rewards such as Y = A1 + A2 and does not distinguish harmful from beneficial interaction) and the empirical gains are noisy.

VVqh1L18Av.one_liner: Reinforcement-learned sequential selection of a few local temporal representations, kept alongside the global representation, for time series classification.
VVqh1L18Av.problem: Deep time series classifiers aggregate temporal representations into one global representation, which can obscure class-discriminative information in local regions.
VVqh1L18Av.method: LISTS sequentially selects a small number of local temporal representations that complement the global context and retains them with it for classification. The selector is trained by reinforcement learning with the classification objective as the learning signal.
VVqh1L18Av.key_idea: Formulate local-instance selection as sequential decision-making trained by RL with the classification objective as reward, then keep selected local features alongside the global representation.
VVqh1L18Av.evidence: All 30 UEA benchmark datasets against ten methods, a controlled synthetic study, ablations, and a theoretical analysis motivating the global-local formulation.
VVqh1L18Av.claimed_gains: 74.4% average accuracy and the best average rank among ten methods on the 30 UEA datasets.
VVqh1L18Av.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear, the method is simple, and results on 30 UEA datasets and a synthetic study support the global-local idea.
VVqh1L18Av.main_concern: RL-based instance selection is not justified against alternatives such as top-k attention, contiguous segments or saliency-based selection, and one reviewer found the paper hard to read.

nuPXk8JyWz.one_liner: Co-activation graphs of SAE features reveal mutually exclusive groups with aligned decoder directions that can be swapped to steer outputs.
nuPXk8JyWz.problem: SAE features are usually studied in isolation, leaving relationships such as features that occur in similar contexts but never together unexplored.
nuPXk8JyWz.method: Builds feature co-activation graphs and identifies mutually exclusive (ME) groups, analyses their semantic types and decoder-direction geometry, and tests causal relevance by replacing one feature with another ME alternative.
nuPXk8JyWz.key_idea: Select SAE feature groups with similar contexts but no co-occurrence, calibrated against shuffled graphs, and swap members to test causal steering toward the replacement concept.
nuPXk8JyWz.evidence: Four models, three SAE architectures and every layer, with swap interventions compared against several alternatives; semantic types are judged by a prompted LLM.
nuPXk8JyWz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the analysis is broad and statistically calibrated, recovering recognisable groups (digits, pronouns, months) with aligned decoder directions that steer behavior better than alternatives.
nuPXk8JyWz.main_concern: The payoff and novelty are unclear: semantic-type verdicts come from one prompted judge, steering gains over vanilla selection are small for most types, and the groups are mostly closed word classes.

6EolaRQIOE.one_liner: Photometric-uncertainty-derived metallic supervision and parallax-corrected cubemaps improve Gaussian splatting of indoor reflective objects.
6EolaRQIOE.problem: Reflective regions are hard to localize consistently across views, and distant-environment lighting assumptions break indoors where near-field geometry causes reflection parallax.
6EolaRQIOE.method: Uncertainty-Guided Metallic Supervision (UGMS) uses learned photometric uncertainty to derive metallic supervision for diffuse-specular decomposition, and Parallax-Corrected Cubemaps (PCC) model finite-distance environment lighting. The authors also add the IndoorRef12 synthetic benchmark.
6EolaRQIOE.key_idea: Derive metallic masks from learned photometric uncertainty to supervise diffuse-specular decomposition, and use proxy-box parallax-corrected cubemaps for finite-distance reflections.
6EolaRQIOE.evidence: IndoorRef12, a synthetic benchmark of 12 indoor environments, plus the GlossyReal dataset, with component ablations and material-swap experiments.
6EolaRQIOE.claimed_gains: Substantial improvements in reflection reconstruction, particularly in indoor scenes with strong near-field parallax; no numbers stated.
6EolaRQIOE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is valuable, the uncertainty-guided localization and parallax correction are well motivated, and results improve reconstruction quality, normals and reflective-region recovery.
6EolaRQIOE.main_concern: Generality and attribution are weak: real-world evidence is limited (GlossyReal has few objects), UGMS helps even at a mask IoU of 0.23, and near-field baselines such as SpecTRe-GS are not compared.

tamy0GP80r.one_liner: Gives a finite necessary-and-sufficient criterion for when fixed-memory softmax attention is a gradient, plus conditioning bounds.
tamy0GP80r.problem: It is unclear when untied softmax attention F(q) = U^T softmax(beta K q) admits a global potential, since known energy views cover only tied or specially structured maps.
tamy0GP80r.method: Derives a finite algebraic criterion by grouping equal key-pair sums, characterizes generic and binary Cartesian memories and constant-metric convex representations, and bounds the distance to the conservative value space from measured Jacobian asymmetry.
tamy0GP80r.key_idea: Attention is a gradient exactly when its Jacobian is symmetric, which reduces to finite algebraic conditions on groups of equal key-pair sums (k_i + k_j).
tamy0GP80r.evidence: Proofs plus deterministic numerical checks of the exact characterization and finite-query certificates, a near-Cartesian family, and a bifurcation construction; no trained models are used.
tamy0GP80r.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the finite algebraic characterization via Jacobian symmetry is a clean, well-motivated and broadly applicable theoretical result.
tamy0GP80r.main_concern: Practical significance and novelty are limited: no real trained models are tested, the Cartesian-memory case is hard to relate to practice, and prior work already derived the symmetry conditions.

RQVfKLuzYb.one_liner: Empirically shows stronger regularization, such as low-rank LoRA, amplifies hidden-bias transfer in subliminal learning and related poisoning settings.
RQVfKLuzYb.problem: It is unclear whether regularization limits covert transfer of hidden biases between language models through semantically unrelated data.
RQVfKLuzYb.method: Systematically varies LoRA rank, full fine-tuning, L1 and L2 penalties and data scale across subliminal learning, phantom transfer and logit-linear selection, with rank-dependent learning-rate tuning.
RQVfKLuzYb.key_idea: Hidden bias acts as a simple feature that capacity-limiting regularization pushes the student to learn first, so regularization amplifies transfer.
RQVfKLuzYb.evidence: Three setups (subliminal learning, phantom transfer, logit-linear selection) with controlled comparisons of LoRA rank, full fine-tuning, L1 and L2 penalties and unique data scale.
RQVfKLuzYb.claimed_gains: At small data scales low-rank LoRA produces strong transfer while high-rank LoRA and full fine-tuning produce none; no numbers stated.
RQVfKLuzYb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clear and comprehensive, with well-controlled experiments revealing a counterintuitive effect that reconciles earlier contradictory results on LoRA rank and optimizers.
RQVfKLuzYb.main_concern: The simplicity-bias mechanism is hypothesized rather than shown, and grouping low rank, weight penalties, data scale and DPO beta under one 'regularization' label stretches the concept.

Yyt95EDHQU.one_liner: Functional dependence measure yields coverage-error bounds and a central limit theorem for realized split-conformal coverage under temporal dependence.
Yyt95EDHQU.problem: Inference for realized coverage of conformal prediction is understudied, especially for temporally dependent data where mixing assumptions are hard to verify.
Yyt95EDHQU.method: For split conformal prediction with adjacent calibration and test sets, derives non-asymptotic coverage error bounds without mixing assumptions, a Bahadur representation and CLT, and a block-based standard-error estimator for a test, plus a long-memory analysis for Gaussian linear processes.
Yyt95EDHQU.key_idea: Measure temporal dependence with the functional dependence measure and use a Bahadur representation to obtain a CLT for realized coverage, with block-based standard errors for testing.
Yyt95EDHQU.evidence: Theory with numerical experiments, mostly on synthetic data generated under the theoretical assumptions.
Yyt95EDHQU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and the theory, including the first CLT for realized split-conformal coverage under temporal dependence, is detailed and connects to a practical test.
Yyt95EDHQU.main_concern: Assumptions are restrictive and checked mainly on synthetic examples (Gaussian linear residuals with power-law coefficients, no practical-model examples), and the long-memory results cover only a narrow class.

HKljbVg01v.one_liner: Mixture-of-experts classifier with crystal-system hierarchical routing, rule-biased gating and a symmetry-operation contrastive loss for PXRD space-group recognition.
HKljbVg01v.problem: Space-group recognition from powder X-ray diffraction is a 230-way, long-tailed, fine-grained problem where rare groups with fewer than 20 training examples are confused with frequent ones.
HKljbVg01v.method: Phys-MoE uses a hierarchical router that masks space groups inconsistent with the predicted crystal system, a rule-biased gating mechanism that encourages expert specialization across symmetry blocks, and a rule-semantic contrastive objective based on Jaccard similarity of symmetry-operation sets.
HKljbVg01v.key_idea: Inject crystallographic priors into routing and representation learning, masking inconsistent space groups by crystal system and aligning classes by shared symmetry operations.
HKljbVg01v.evidence: Experiments on CCDC, CoREMOF and an inorganic distribution-shift benchmark, with ablations and error and oracle analyses.
HKljbVg01v.claimed_gains: On CCDC, 81.70% overall Top-1 accuracy and 26.19% accuracy for space groups with fewer than 20 training examples.
HKljbVg01v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using the space-group-to-crystal-system mapping and symmetry-operation relationships as priors is well motivated and improves recognition, especially for rare space groups.
HKljbVg01v.main_concern: The symmetry-operation similarity behind the contrastive loss is under-specified (Appendix C.1 repeats the Jaccard definition) and ablations do not isolate its particular semantics.

jbqd9set4Q.one_liner: Sparse crosscoders with a swap readout show on-policy distillation reweights existing student features rather than acquiring teacher features.
jbqd9set4Q.problem: It is unclear what on-policy distillation actually transfers into a student's internal representations.
jbqd9set4Q.method: Trains a sparse crosscoder with one feature dictionary shared by the student before and after OPD and the teacher, and adds a swap readout that reads each checkpoint's activations on its own to measure how feature usage changes, including for unseen checkpoints.
jbqd9set4Q.key_idea: Read each student checkpoint's feature activations separately from a shared crosscoder (swap readout) to measure usage change, showing OPD reweights shared features.
jbqd9set4Q.evidence: Three OPD settings, feature-level intervention experiments, and an analysis of the SFT warm-up, with random-direction, noise and disjoint-token controls.
jbqd9set4Q.claimed_gains: OPD leaves the firing rates of over 98% of the student's frequently used features within 20%; no performance gains stated.
jbqd9set4Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the swap readout fixes a concrete measurement limitation of standard crosscoder analysis and that the feature-level interventions give useful causal evidence.
jbqd9set4Q.main_concern: The claim that OPD acquires no new features is stronger than the evidence, since detection sensitivity is not validated, only one middle-layer site and a fixed dictionary are used, and the small update size may explain the result.

xzKxcPL8v4.one_liner: Rewards open-ended generation from a rollout-by-rubric win-rate matrix, with data-dependent rubric weights and distance-to-ideal scoring.
xzKxcPL8v4.problem: Open-ended generation lacks standard answers, and pointwise rubric scores or merged single scores give limited information about relative response quality.
xzKxcPL8v4.method: MatrixReward compares every pair of sampled responses under each rubric, derives rubric weights from column spread and between-column correlation combined with prior weights, and scores each rollout by its relative closeness to positive and negative ideal profiles built from per-rubric maxima and minima.
xzKxcPL8v4.key_idea: Weight rubrics by how strongly and how non-redundantly they separate current rollouts, then reward each rollout by its closeness to the best and worst per-rubric ideals.
xzKxcPL8v4.evidence: Qwen3-8B on four open-ended query-answering benchmarks, with ablations of weighting and aggregation and a performance-cost analysis.
xzKxcPL8v4.claimed_gains: Average score of 63.02 on four benchmarks, about 2.0% above the strongest baseline; a review cites the distance-based aggregation ablation improving the average from 59.83 to 63.02.
xzKxcPL8v4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that preserving per-rubric pairwise feedback is a meaningful approach to reward design and that the framework is clearly presented with useful ablations and a cost analysis.
xzKxcPL8v4.main_concern: The same judge model supplies training rewards and benchmark scores without independent or human evaluation, uses about 3.4 times the judging tokens of the strongest baseline, and lacks multiple seeds or confidence intervals.

C2DA0NAhnX.one_liner: Models static surfaces as thermally constrained 2D Gaussian surfels and dynamic smoke as deformable 3D Gaussians, composited in one renderer.
C2DA0NAhnX.problem: Multiview observations of moving smoke entangle persistent surfaces with a transient participating medium, making clear-scene recovery difficult.
C2DA0NAhnX.method: PhySmoke represents persistent surfaces with thermal-constrained 2D Gaussians and smoke with deformable 3D Gaussians, renders both with a unified ray-wise compositor, and uses the estimated smoke contribution to guide restoration of lost visible detail.
