C2DA0NAhnX.key_idea: Give surfaces and smoke different primitives matched to their physical support, composite them along each ray with shared depth ordering, and use thermal boundaries and smoke estimates to separate them.
C2DA0NAhnX.evidence: Nine synthetic scenes plus public and self-collected real captures, with ablations including a mixed-renderer comparison against layer-wise compositing.
C2DA0NAhnX.claimed_gains: Improves all three macro image-quality metrics on nine synthetic scenes and reduces surface primitive counts; a review cites a 1.17 dB PSNR gain over layer-wise compositing.
C2DA0NAhnX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating surfaces from smoke with different representations is well argued, compact, and supported by ablations on the unified renderer and detail recovery.
C2DA0NAhnX.main_concern: The design rests on hand-crafted heuristics without sensitivity analysis, and evidence is narrow: synthetic scenes from one benchmark, a single seed, and no study of thermal registration error.

cpS85tgdVR.one_liner: Exploits merge-split structure of anchor replacement to compile the full one-replacement neighborhood into O(n+k) values, matching exhaustive search.
cpS85tgdVR.problem: Refining fixed-budget trajectory simplification outputs exhaustively requires evaluating every anchor replacement, O(k(n-k)) comparisons per round.
cpS85tgdVR.method: Segment-Delta replaces a retained anchor with a discarded sample, using the fact that an insertion splits one interval and overlaps a deletion only if the deleted anchor bounds it, to return the exact best replacement for segment-local additive and bottleneck objectives. A Transformer variant uses approximate candidate compilation with full-objective verification.
cpS85tgdVR.key_idea: An insertion splits one interval and conflicts with a deletion only at a bounding anchor, so all replacement deltas compile into O(n+k) values.
cpS85tgdVR.evidence: GeoLife and Porto datasets, classical and learned simplifiers, dynamic-programming comparisons, and correctness verification against exhaustive search.
cpS85tgdVR.claimed_gains: Reduces candidate comparisons from O(k(n-k)) to O(n+k); refining greedy outputs cuts mean error by 33.5-34.0% on length-1,000 GeoLife trajectories, with full-refinement speedups of 3.04/4.83x at n=1,000, k=100/250.
cpS85tgdVR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method returns exact results matching exhaustive search with correctness guarantees and far fewer candidate comparisons across classical and learned simplifiers.
cpS85tgdVR.main_concern: Actual speedups are modest (1.10-1.54x at length 1,000), comparison with other refinement methods and total-runtime accounting are missing, and conceptual novelty beyond problem-specific local-search acceleration is limited.

8o9IHeHKOh.one_liner: Truncates unreliable labels by GMM and neighbor consensus and filters false repulsion by shared neighbors for multi-label noisy hashing.
8o9IHeHKOh.problem: Multi-label instance-dependent noise adds spurious similarities (false attraction) or removes real correlations (false repulsion) in pairwise supervision, which robust hashing methods built for class-conditional noise do not handle.
8o9IHeHKOh.method: IDNRH combines Sample-to-Label Truncation, which partitions noisy samples with a GMM, reconstructs label confidence by multi-view neighbor consensus and truncates unreliable labels, with Repulsion-Filtered Soft Contrastive Learning, which uses shared-neighbor similarity and soft label similarity.
8o9IHeHKOh.key_idea: Separate the two corruptions: truncate labels per sample against false attraction and filter negatives by shared-neighbor similarity against false repulsion.
8o9IHeHKOh.evidence: Widely used multi-label datasets and a real-world noisy dataset across noise settings and hash lengths, including a CLIP-backbone-matched comparison.
8o9IHeHKOh.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms hashing methods under multi-label instance-dependent noise; no numbers stated.
8o9IHeHKOh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practically relevant, the design rationale is clear, and results are competitive across datasets, noise settings and code lengths.
8o9IHeHKOh.main_concern: Novelty over prior noisy-hashing work that already uses GMM partitioning and soft contrastive learning on label overlap is unclear, and those works are neither cited nor compared.

wysjE8cE3E.one_liner: Mines lower-to-higher pathology pairs across patients and aligns image and report burden deltas for CT vision-language pretraining.
wysjE8cE3E.problem: CT vision-language pretraining supervises only what is present, not how much, so graded burden language in reports collapses into a present-or-absent signal.
wysjE8cE3E.method: Spectrum represents each study at whole-study and organ scopes, mines confidence-filtered lower-to-higher burden pairs from different patients with a rule-based scorer, and applies Burden-Direction Alignment between pathology-conditioned image and report deltas after a target-conditioned aligner makes the endpoints comparable.
wysjE8cE3E.key_idea: Align image-feature deltas with report deltas along an order of weakly mined cross-patient burden pairs, with a target-conditioned aligner removing between-patient variation.
wysjE8cE3E.evidence: Two CT datasets with abnormality classification, retrieval and image-text matching evaluations, component ablations and aligner comparisons.
wysjE8cE3E.claimed_gains: not stated; reviews describe substantial improvements across evaluation tasks and two CT datasets without numbers.
wysjE8cE3E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning within-pathology burden ordering beyond image-report correspondence is a meaningful direction with scalable, low-annotation-cost supervision and strong results.
wysjE8cE3E.main_concern: Burden ordering itself is not quantitatively validated (no severity-estimation evaluation), the rule-based scorer's robustness and coverage are unclear, and the zero-shot setting is questionable.

UeAojyaC1e.one_liner: Single autoregressive Qwen3-Omni-based model jointly predicts speaker profiles, speaker-tagged text and BiCodec speech tokens for multi-talker speech translation.
UeAojyaC1e.problem: Existing speech-to-speech translation handles one speaker at a time, so translating whole multi-speaker conversations while preserving speaker identity and context remains unsolved.
UeAojyaC1e.method: COMUS adapts the Qwen3-Omni Thinker to autoregressively predict one stream of speaker profile tokens, speaker-labelled semantic tokens and BiCodec speech tokens over the entire recording. It is trained on the constructed SODA-SoulX corpus of about 26K hours of English-Chinese conversational speech.
UeAojyaC1e.key_idea: Generate speaker profile tokens and speaker-tagged translation tokens in one autoregressive pass over the full recording so speaker turns and identities stay consistent.
UeAojyaC1e.evidence: Real conversational datasets AMI and AliMeeting against cascaded baselines, plus noise and overlapping-speech tests and subjective listening tests.
UeAojyaC1e.claimed_gains: Speaker-attributed ASR-BLEU of 31.9 (English-to-Chinese) and 20.4 (Chinese-to-English), outperforming most cascaded baselines, with advantages in speaker similarity, translation accuracy and naturalness.
UeAojyaC1e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it targets a real gap in multi-talker speech translation, with a sensible speaker-profile design and strong results across translation, diarization, noise robustness and subjective evaluation.
UeAojyaC1e.main_concern: Comparisons with cascades are not controlled: COMUS uses full-conversation context and in-domain fine-tuning while baselines translate segments zero-shot, so the benefit of end-to-end modeling is unclear.

TTYWvkU5jV.one_liner: Two-stage JEPA latent state: prototypes filter unsupported visual factors, then sparse selection keeps action-relevant ones for robust planning.
TTYWvkU5jV.problem: JEPA latent world models can encode task-irrelevant backgrounds and distractors, which perturb state prediction and goal matching when unseen distractors appear at test time.
TTYWvkU5jV.method: DSSF first uses learnable prototypes to model the feature-space support of non-distractor factors and filter unsupported local factors, then sparsely selects information relevant to action-conditioned dynamics from the retained factors to build a compact latent state.
TTYWvkU5jV.key_idea: Separately model whether a visual factor is supported by the training distribution (prototypes) and whether it is relevant to control (sparse selection) before building the latent state.
TTYWvkU5jV.evidence: Unseen-distractor and cross-family distractor evaluations on four simulated tasks with matched-backbone and augmentation ablations, within a CEM planning pipeline.
TTYWvkU5jV.claimed_gains: The visible abstract gives no numbers; a review cites Push-T success rising from 28.60% (LeWM) to 70.13% with five static shape distractors while clean success stays at 87.93%.
TTYWvkU5jV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating visually supported from control-relevant information is useful and gives substantial robustness gains on four simulated tasks while preserving clean performance.
TTYWvkU5jV.main_concern: Evaluation relevance and attribution are unclear: synthetic pasted distractors share a mechanism with training, and prototype support modeling is not isolated from supervised nuisance segmentation.

retgbahmng.one_liner: Estimates the finite-sample split-half floor of plug-in Wasserstein distance from measured cells to diagnose underdispersion bias in single-cell perturbation benchmarks.
retgbahmng.problem: The plug-in Wasserstein distance used to rank single-cell perturbation models has a finite-sample floor, so predictions with no spread can outscore a real sample.
retgbahmng.method: PopFloor estimates the split-half floor from measured cells. An exact identity for unregularised squared 2-Wasserstein gives a threshold on the floor-to-held-out-variance ratio, relative to mean error, beyond which a spread-free prediction beats an equal-size target sample.
retgbahmng.key_idea: Compare the floor-to-variance ratio against one plus the relative mean error, an exact-identity condition under which a spread-free population beats a real sample.
retgbahmng.evidence: An exploratory recomputation on scPerturBench, reproduced CPA scores across five screens and three seeds, and pre-registered tests on disjoint cells of two unused screens.
retgbahmng.claimed_gains: scPerturBench's leader falls to fourth without Wasserstein distance, and reproduced CPA scores below the floor on 88.7 to 92.6% of the largest screen's perturbations across three seeds.
retgbahmng.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnostic is simple and interpretable and connects exact theory to practice, with pre-registered tests on unused screens showing predictive value beyond gene and cell counts.
retgbahmng.main_concern: Scope and added value are limited: it targets one metric in one task, the link to the original published leaderboard is incomplete without original predictions, and its benefit over existing multi-metric checks is unclear.

pizWKt2tIp.one_liner: Benchmarks five MLLMs on 4,000 real and AI-generated faces to test same-developer effects, provenance removal, and explanation reliability.
pizWKt2tIp.problem: It is unclear which signals drive MLLM judgments of AI-generated facial images and whether the visual evidence cited in their explanations is reliable across repeated judgments.
pizWKt2tIp.method: Builds a 4,000-image benchmark from seven generation sources plus real photographs and evaluates five MLLMs cross-source, using fixed-effects analysis for same-developer pairs, removing C2PA records, applying MarkNull to strip SynthID, and measuring judgment repeatability and image support of explanations.
pizWKt2tIp.key_idea: Controlled interventions (C2PA removal, MarkNull SynthID removal) plus a fixed-effects comparison test whether provenance cues and same-developer pairing drive MLLM detection.
pizWKt2tIp.evidence: Cross-source evaluation of five MLLMs on a 4,000-image benchmark from seven generators and real photographs, with pixel-level measurement of provenance interventions and repeatability checks.
pizWKt2tIp.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports no general same-developer detection advantage, no significant change from C2PA removal, and detector- and source-dependent changes from SynthID removal.
pizWKt2tIp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the comprehensive cross-source setup, the careful statistics for same-developer effects, and the repeatability tests beyond raw accuracy.
pizWKt2tIp.main_concern: MarkNull alters pixels beyond removing the watermark (raising fake rates on real photos), so the SynthID results are confounded and do not isolate reliance on provenance.

bI6zdvIIbH.one_liner: Processes long-context chunks in parallel and iteratively refines a shared memory, trained with RL and a turn-efficiency reward.
bI6zdvIIbH.problem: Recurrent-memory long-context methods overwrite early evidence with later irrelevant content, and their serial chunk dependencies make latency grow with context length.
bI6zdvIIbH.method: Each turn reads all chunks in parallel conditioned on the current shared memory, selects new or complementary evidence from each chunk, and merges it into a compact memory, for a bounded number of turns. RL with an auxiliary turn-efficiency reward lets the model exit adaptively once evidence suffices.
bI6zdvIIbH.key_idea: Replace sequential chunk-wise memory updates with parallel reads against a shared memory refined over a bounded number of turns, with RL-learned early exit.
bI6zdvIIbH.evidence: Evaluated with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and Qwen2.5-7B on HotpotQA at context lengths up to 3.6 million tokens against a recurrent-memory baseline, with RL and transfer ablations.
bI6zdvIIbH.claimed_gains: Outperforms the recurrent-memory baseline by +6.25 and +7.81 absolute points with 6.1x and 2.1x inference speedups on the two backbones, respectively.
bI6zdvIIbH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the parallel shared-memory design simple and clearly explained, with strong accuracy and latency results at very long contexts and useful ablations.
bI6zdvIIbH.main_concern: Reliability and attribution of gains are unclear: single training runs and single stochastic evaluations, one scalar reward whose effect on evidence selection is not isolated, and speedups that depend on parallel hardware despite more total compute.

lZ6sbeII1Q.one_liner: Bayesian optimization that transfers existing protein-interaction landscapes to a new partner via calibrated source means and learned pair representations.
lZ6sbeII1Q.problem: Mapping the full interaction landscape for every new protein partner is costly, and source landscapes mix shared mutational trends with partner-specific effects, which makes transfer hard.
lZ6sbeII1Q.method: SPIN-BO uses an adaptively calibrated source-response mean that learns from sparse target assays how to weight and combine source profiles, plus a Gaussian-process residual whose geometry comes from a source-supervised protein-pair representation built on pretrained protein language model embeddings. It recalibrates as target assays accumulate and picks the next variants to test.
lZ6sbeII1Q.key_idea: Combine a target-calibrated weighted mixture of source responses with a GP residual over source-supervised protein-pair embeddings, recalibrated as target assays accumulate.
lZ6sbeII1Q.evidence: Controlled semi-synthetic experiments and a multi-source bZIP experiment, compared against ALDE-style and EVOLVEpro-style target-only baselines (per reviews; abstract is cut off).
lZ6sbeII1Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the cross-partner transfer setting practical and well motivated, with two clearly separated transfer mechanisms and detailed experimental protocols.
lZ6sbeII1Q.main_concern: Source-aware transfer BO methods (DeltaBO, DynMeanBO, RGPE) are discussed but not compared, and the setting assumes complete, aligned source landscapes, which limits the evidence and applicability.

BASjNTb7kE.one_liner: Shows that FIT-only range calibration of the export codec reverses learner and bit-allocation comparisons in low-bit image retrieval.
BASjNTb7kE.problem: Low-bit retrieval comparisons at a fixed code rate can reflect the export codec rather than the learner, confounding conclusions about training and bit allocation.
BASjNTb7kE.method: Freezes trained descriptors (triplet, contrastive, DINOv2, SigLIP2) and applies codec interventions fitted on a FIT split, including range calibration and product quantization, then re-compares learners and bit allocations at the same payload.
BASjNTb7kE.key_idea: Calibrate the export codec's range on a FIT split before comparing learners, because a scale and grid mismatch can masquerade as a learner or allocation difference.
BASjNTb7kE.evidence: Stanford Online Products with frozen twenty-dimensional four-bit triplet descriptors against ten-dimensional eight-bit ones, learned-scale DINOv2 and SigLIP2 contrasts, one paired contrastive-versus-triplet training realization, and CUB as an adverse case.
BASjNTb7kE.claimed_gains: FIT-only range calibration improves frozen twenty-dimensional four-bit triplet descriptors by 14.22 average-precision points at the same ten-byte payload, moving the allocation effect from -5.61 to +8.50 points, and a four-bit-training advantage falls from +9.74 to -0.36 points.
BASjNTb7kE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper makes a relevant methodological point that the codec must be calibrated before attributing differences to the learner, with honest scoping and reported adverse results.
BASjNTb7kE.main_concern: The presentation is dense and hard to follow (undefined abbreviations from the abstract onward), and the evidence is limited to image retrieval with little methodological novelty beyond standard quantization practice.

SpWCXsAwOj.one_liner: Pre-trains line-level cuneiform recognizers on synthetic lines composed from real sign crops arranged by attested text sequences.
SpWCXsAwOj.problem: Paired cuneiform line images and sign sequences are scarce, even though isolated sign images and machine-readable texts exist separately.
SpWCXsAwOj.method: Given a normalized sign sequence from a text corpus, it samples real sign crops from a tablet-disjoint visual dictionary (augmented for rare signs), composes them into a synthetic line image, and pre-trains CRNN, SVTRv2-inspired CTC, and PaddleOCR-VL recognizers before adaptation on a few annotated tablets.
SpWCXsAwOj.key_idea: Compose real sign crops according to attested text sequences to create image-sequence pairs for pre-training line recognizers.
SpWCXsAwOj.evidence: Three recognition architectures adapted on 100 Ur III tablets, tested in-period, cross-period and cross-collection, with strict text-overlap controls and an extended-training baseline; the main evaluation uses ground-truth sign locations.
SpWCXsAwOj.claimed_gains: With adaptation on 100 Ur III tablets, sign error rates are 18-25% in-period, removing compositional pre-training raises error by 24-52 percentage points, and on natural line images the SVTRv2-inspired model's in-period SER falls from 89.2% to 52.8%.
SpWCXsAwOj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the pre-training gains persist across three architectures and under strict text-overlap controls, and that reusing existing sign images and texts addresses the annotation shortage.
SpWCXsAwOj.main_concern: The main experiments use ground-truth sign boundaries and reconstructed lines, so benefit for realistic automatic recognition is not convincingly shown on an untouched test set.

ncTSNdin7N.one_liner: Looped Transformer reading individual block updates via geometric decay and attention, with the input kept on a separate path.
ncTSNdin7N.problem: Parameter sharing in looped Transformers does not determine how repeated block outputs are stored and re-read, and weighting a full block output also reweights the history already in its input.
ncTSNdin7N.method: Gives a write-transport-read view of residual mechanisms and implements Loopback, which reads individual updates with the shared stack's input on a separate path, using geometric decay to set total update weight (and a recency prior) and attention to allocate that weight across updates.
ncTSNdin7N.key_idea: Control input strength, total update weight (geometric decay) and allocation across updates (learned attention) separately when reading a looped block's accumulated updates.
ncTSNdin7N.evidence: Validation loss on ClimbMix at scales from 191M to 3B with matched training tokens and executed depth, plus thirteen downstream tasks, against a standard Transformer and seven looped residual designs.
ncTSNdin7N.claimed_gains: Reaches lower validation loss than standard Transformer baselines with 40-75% of their parameters at 191M to 3B, has higher mean accuracy over thirteen downstream tasks at 1.4B and 3B, and has the lowest validation loss at 191M, 374M and 778M.
ncTSNdin7N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the clear write-transport-read unifying framework and ablations showing most of the gain comes from decay-controlled total update weight.
ncTSNdin7N.main_concern: Geometric decay alone accounts for nearly all the gain, and learned allocation adds only a few thousandths of a nat from single training runs, so the attention component's contribution and novelty are doubtful.

xbepGUau8C.one_liner: Single-stage unbiased Hadamard quantizer using pairwise-independent dithers, removing the residual stage of a prior two-stage scheme.
xbepGUau8C.problem: The two-stage randomized-Hadamard dithered quantizer of Feng et al. needs a second transform and residual quantization, which adds communication and enlarges the leading constant in its error bound.
xbepGUau8C.method: Shows that pairwise-independent dithers across Hadamard coordinates suffice, giving an unbiased single-stage inner-product estimator with b bits per coordinate and a bound of (3*pi*sqrt(3)/2 + o(1)) times the squared query norm over d*4^b as b grows.
xbepGUau8C.key_idea: Draw dithers that are only pairwise independent across randomized-Hadamard coordinates, which suffices for the error bound and removes the residual stage.
xbepGUau8C.evidence: Theoretical proofs only, with a dimension-free o(1) term uniform over unit inputs and fixed queries; reviewers note there are no practical examples.
xbepGUau8C.claimed_gains: Eliminates the residual-stage O(d)-bit payload and reduces the leading upper-bound constant by a factor of approximately 5.93 compared with the two-stage construction of Feng et al.
xbepGUau8C.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the result is a sound, clear improvement of an existing quantization algorithm, with detailed proofs and good mathematical clarity.
xbepGUau8C.main_concern: The contribution is a constant-factor improvement using largely the same techniques as prior work, and the paper is hard to follow without having read Feng et al.

uV1jv7mPtm.one_liner: Spherical rotary positional encoding via Wigner D-matrices gives SO(3)-equivariant attention and a transformer for spherical physical signals.
uV1jv7mPtm.problem: Planar projections distort spherical signals and discard rotational symmetry, while prior equivariant attention is either costly (steerable kernels, tensor products) or limited to Euclidean data.
uV1jv7mPtm.method: Wigner-RoPE represents lifted spherical positions as rotations from a reference direction using Wigner D-matrices, generalizing RoPE to rotations on the sphere. WRAP builds multi-frequency SO(3)-equivariant attention compatible with fused attention kernels, and stacking WRAP layers gives WRAP-former.
uV1jv7mPtm.key_idea: Lift S^2 positions to SO(3) and encode them with Wigner D-matrix rotary embeddings so attention depends on relative rotations.
uV1jv7mPtm.evidence: Manifold40 radar classification, Stanford 2D3DS segmentation and WeatherBench forecasting, with measured equivariance error and exact equivariance to a discrete group on HEALPix.
uV1jv7mPtm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a well-motivated, efficient method with theoretical support that is competitive across radar, segmentation and weather forecasting tasks.
uV1jv7mPtm.main_concern: Efficiency is a central motivation but runtime and model-size comparisons are missing, and on radar and segmentation the gains over a plain ViT are small against few baselines.

Iuo9cEivRq.one_liner: Audio-language model trained with SFT, on-policy self-distillation, and GRPO on expert-annotated ProQA to diagnose speech quality issues and recommend fixes.
Iuo9cEivRq.problem: Speech-quality assessment systems reduce a recording to a scalar score, giving no insight into what is wrong, how severe it is, or how to fix it.
Iuo9cEivRq.method: The authors build ProQA, 634 recordings with 11,412 axis-level annotations by professional audio engineers across 18 axes, and expand it with controlled augmentations over ten axes into 15,524 variants with known quality changes. AuditEar is trained in three stages: SFT, on-policy self-distillation from privileged expert context, and GRPO with verifiable rewards.
Iuo9cEivRq.key_idea: Controlled augmentations compound severity increments onto expert ratings to expand scarce expert labels, and on-policy self-distillation from privileged expert context guides training.
Iuo9cEivRq.evidence: Held-out ProQA test set against its zero-shot backbone and three audio-language baselines, plus transfer to external benchmarks (QualiSpeech and SpeechEval per reviews).
Iuo9cEivRq.claimed_gains: Relative improvements of 41.2% in per-axis severity accuracy, 64.1% in pairwise accuracy, and 86.4% in holistic fix-F1 over its zero-shot backbone, gains of up to 2x over the strongest of three baselines, and 3x-45x the correlation of (truncated) baselines on external benchmarks.
Iuo9cEivRq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the expert-annotated ProQA data is a valuable resource and the multi-stage training pipeline shows clear stage-wise gains that transfer to external benchmarks.
Iuo9cEivRq.main_concern: ProQA is small (634 recordings, one annotator per example, English only) relative to existing datasets such as QualiSpeech, baselines are mostly zero-shot, and signal-processing augmentations may be detectable without the dataset.

2r9ZRCBu9Q.one_liner: Reformulates the softmax denominator via the cumulant generating function, removing homomorphic division and max subtraction to cut multiplicative depth.
2r9ZRCBu9Q.problem: Softmax is hard to evaluate under homomorphic encryption because of its multivariate structure, the large dynamic range from exponentiation, and costly division.
2r9ZRCBu9Q.method: CGF-softmax rewrites the softmax denominator through the cumulant generating function, so neither homomorphic division nor explicit maximum subtraction is needed. Reviews indicate the deployed form keeps only second-order (mean and variance) terms.
2r9ZRCBu9Q.key_idea: Express the softmax normalizer as a cumulant-generating-function statistic of the logits, truncated to low-order cumulants, replacing division and max subtraction with simple statistics.
2r9ZRCBu9Q.evidence: Experiments on Vision Transformers and LLMs, plus integration into a multi-GPU FHE inference framework that measures end-to-end encrypted BERT-Base latency.
2r9ZRCBu9Q.claimed_gains: Reduces end-to-end encrypted BERT-Base inference latency by 36.3% (one GPU) and 39.6% (two GPUs) by eliminating all bootstrapping inside softmax.
2r9ZRCBu9Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a simple division- and max-free circuit that cuts depth and bootstrapping cost, with credible end-to-end latency measurements on language and vision models.
2r9ZRCBu9Q.main_concern: The error bounds cover the full CGF form, but the deployed second-order truncation is a trained surrogate whose error is not bounded and can break softmax properties.

ytBfMGjO7W.one_liner: Curvature profiles (degree-based curvature plus edge-rooted cycle counts) serve as edge features or guide propagation in the RicciMP layer.
ytBfMGjO7W.problem: It is unclear when edge-level structural information such as curvature helps GNNs: by adding structure that message passing misses, or by improving message propagation.
ytBfMGjO7W.method: It introduces curvature profiles that combine degree-based curvature and counts of cycles of different lengths, used either as edge features in standard graph networks or to guide propagation in the RicciMP layer. It separates the two roles theoretically and empirically.
ytBfMGjO7W.key_idea: Edge-rooted cycle profiles set positive edge conductances while a learned polynomial sets propagation range, disentangling structural information from message-propagation range.
ytBfMGjO7W.evidence: Exact constructions, expressivity theorems showing a cycle-order hierarchy incomparable with k-WL, and empirical comparisons of feature versus propagation use (ZINC per reviews).
ytBfMGjO7W.claimed_gains: Curvature-profile refinement is incomparable with coordinate-wise k-WL once the cycle order passes a k-dependent threshold, each distinguishing graph pairs the other misses; empirical numbers are truncated.
ytBfMGjO7W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the research question is relevant, the theory is well posed with correct proofs, and the experiments are broad, with clearly stated assumptions and a willingness to report negative results.
ytBfMGjO7W.main_concern: The contribution is incremental over GSN-e, Loopy WL, and known MPNN expressiveness results, Forman curvature reduces to degree information, and gains over cycle-only baselines are small.

6RXnT90ioE.one_liner: Open dataset and benchmark for predicting post-layout PPA and routability of standard-cell netlists under unseen sizes, topologies, and functions.
6RXnT90ioE.problem: Accurate PPA evaluation of standard cell candidates needs slow layout generation and simulation, and ML predictors' generalization to unseen cell designs is insufficiently evaluated.
6RXnT90ioE.method: Builds on the ASAP7 7 nm FinFET PDK, generating pre-layout netlists by cell library extension, topology generation, and transistor size assignment, with splits for unseen size configurations, topologies, and functions.
6RXnT90ioE.key_idea: Generate netlists along three axes (functions, topologies, sizes) so test splits isolate generalization to each kind of unseen design.
6RXnT90ioE.evidence: Evaluation of existing prediction methods on PPA and constrained routability prediction, with analysis of structural similarity to training circuits.
6RXnT90ioE.claimed_gains: 118,906 netlists for PPA prediction and 296,274 for constrained routability prediction; existing methods decline from unseen size configurations to unseen topologies and functions.
6RXnT90ioE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find CellBench a relevant, large-scale benchmark with a useful separation of size, topology, and function generalization.
6RXnT90ioE.main_concern: Practical utility is not validated (no evidence predictions improve cell selection or PPA optimization), and the generalization splits are not fully isolated because topology and function shifts are confounded.

fwwZr5jsJv.one_liner: Layerwise analysis of TabPFN-3 across 272 datasets showing expansion-compression dynamics and which inputs benefit from later layers.
fwwZr5jsJv.problem: Early layers of tabular foundation models already predict well, but this does not show later layers are dispensable for every input, and aggregate accuracy hides which inputs gain from extra computation.
fwwZr5jsJv.method: They study all 24 in-context-learning layers of TabPFN-3 over 272 classification datasets using representation geometry, prediction trajectories, truncation, and structural interventions, with related dynamics checked in four more tabular foundation models.
fwwZr5jsJv.key_idea: Track per-sample prediction trajectories and class-prototype separation across layers to show late-layer compression drives separation, especially for ambiguous queries, after predicted classes stabilize.
fwwZr5jsJv.evidence: All 24 layers of TabPFN-3 on 272 classification datasets, four additional tabular foundation models, and block-repetition and layer-order perturbations.
fwwZr5jsJv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the empirical characterization is broad and systematic, with a useful sample-level view of when extra depth helps.
fwwZr5jsJv.main_concern: The findings are descriptive with unclear actionable value and partly expected or circular, and no test-time method identifies which inputs need deeper layers.

N6uaeMe55R.one_liner: Wraps online conformal abstention as a pre-execution shield that adapts its intervention threshold from partial safety feedback.
N6uaeMe55R.problem: Safe online adaptation faces a safety-exploration imbalance and safety staleness, where risk control becomes outdated under coupled exogenous environment shifts and endogenous policy and scorer updates.
N6uaeMe55R.method: Online Conformal Shielding (OCS) selectively executes proposed actions or intervenes, updating its threshold from partial safety feedback while the task policy and scorer keep adapting. It reduces to online conformal abstention (OCA) to inherit selective-risk guarantees, with a prior-aware variant for early threshold selection.
N6uaeMe55R.key_idea: Treat each intervention as an abstention in online conformal abstention, so the threshold updates from partial feedback and selective-risk guarantees hold without modeling the source of shift.
N6uaeMe55R.evidence: A high-probability safety guarantee under non-anticipating interaction, plus experiments on VLA manipulation in ManiSkill and continuous control in Safety-Gymnasium.
N6uaeMe55R.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off after saying OCS keeps selective safety risk near the target level under coupled shifts)
N6uaeMe55R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the reduction to online conformal abstention is a principled abstraction and that the adaptive threshold maintains selective risk better than fixed-threshold gates.
N6uaeMe55R.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the threshold mechanism and guarantee are largely inherited from OCA, and the risk is measured over executed actions so heavier intervention lowers reported risk by construction.

fE7OJ1jpfh.one_liner: Sampling-based approximation of probabilistic dependency graph inconsistency using score-function gradients with Rao-Blackwellization over parameterized Bayesian networks.
fE7OJ1jpfh.problem: Existing methods for PDG inconsistency are either unreliable (first-order optimizers with ad-hoc constraint penalties) or prohibitively expensive (second-order optimizers and convex solvers) for all but the smallest PDGs.
fE7OJ1jpfh.method: The first sampling-based approach combines a score-function gradient estimator with Rao-Blackwellization to optimize over parameterized Bayesian networks. It also permits variational approximations, letting the choice of Bayesian-network structure trade computational efficiency for the tightness of the upper bound.
fE7OJ1jpfh.key_idea: Estimate intractable conditional probabilities from forward samples of a candidate Bayesian network and optimize with Rao-Blackwellized score-function gradients.
fE7OJ1jpfh.evidence: Experiments on synthetically generated or perturbed PDGs, compared with exact-gradient optimization and cluster-tree baselines on scalability.
fE7OJ1jpfh.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says the method scales to substantially larger and more complex PDGs than existing approaches can handle, without figures).
fE7OJ1jpfh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method addresses a clear computational bottleneck and scales to PDGs where existing methods exceed time limits, with a sound-looking derivation.
fE7OJ1jpfh.main_concern: All experiments use candidate Bayesian networks with the same structure as the generating network, so accuracy under unknown structure, known nonzero inconsistency, and naturally occurring conflicting beliefs is untested.

QYUcILhctw.one_liner: Policy-conditioned (functional) critics give convergent off-policy actor-critic under linear approximation and ensemble-based posterior-sampling-style exploration.
QYUcILhctw.problem: Off-policy actor-critic theory is far from practice because of the deadly triad interacting with a changing target policy, and standard critic ensembles do not represent joint uncertainty over return functions across policy space.
QYUcILhctw.method: They develop a convergent off-policy actor-critic with functional critics under linear function approximation (target-based TD, partial coverage, evolving behavior policies), a dual trust-coverage framework, and a replay-sampling design from an i.i.d. replay analysis. A deep functional actor-critic with ensembles supports exploration.
QYUcILhctw.key_idea: Make the critic a function of the policy so evaluation guarantees under partial feature coverage carry across policies and an ensemble gives posterior-sampling-style uncertainty over policy space.
QYUcILhctw.evidence: Theory under linear function approximation with a replay-buffer analysis, plus deep experiments (Dog and Humanoid tasks against SAC+ and TD3+ per reviews).
QYUcILhctw.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract is cut off before the empirical results)
QYUcILhctw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the convergence analysis under partial feature coverage and the separation of stability from exploration are interesting, and the deep implementation is competitive.
QYUcILhctw.main_concern: The theory needs strong assumptions (shared linear coefficients, Bellman completeness) not shown to hold for the neural system, and no ablation or comparison with PAVF isolates the new components.

WJj03oDgh9.one_liner: Learns masks over sentence-to-sentence attention in reasoning traces to find connections that preserve or change a reasoning outcome.
WJj03oDgh9.problem: Circuit discovery assumes fixed token sequences for single predictions, but interventions on reasoning models change the distribution of long, sampled reasoning continuations.
WJj03oDgh9.method: Trains masks over attention connections between sentences in a reasoning prefix on continuations sampled from the unmasked model, then tests on held-out unmasked continuations and fresh continuations generated under the mask. Three objectives: preserve answer distributions, increase correct-answer probability, shorten reasoning.
WJj03oDgh9.key_idea: Learn sparse sentence-level attention masks under an outcome objective, trained on unmasked rollouts and evaluated on rollouts regenerated under the mask.
WJj03oDgh9.evidence: Experiments with three objectives against a local connection baseline that scores connections by effects on subsequent token predictions, on held-out unmasked and mask-generated continuations, with ablations.
WJj03oDgh9.claimed_gains: Masks meet the objective with up to 80% of connections removed, and the approach is reported as more successful than a local connection baseline; distinct masks perform equally well.
WJj03oDgh9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find extending circuit discovery to long reasoning rollouts well motivated, the three objectives well defined and executed, and the evaluation on held-out and mask-generated continuations careful.
WJj03oDgh9.main_concern: Masks are trained per question on the evaluation objective, so gains may just reflect optimization, and non-unique sparse masks cannot separate unstructured reasoning from structured but redundant computation.

aJs9FKYiA6.one_liner: Runs autonomous in-silico vision neuroscience studies with an agent loop over literature, stimulus construction, brain encoding models, and analysis.
aJs9FKYiA6.problem: Running a vision neuroscience experiment end-to-end in silico requires reasoning over knowledge, building controlled stimuli, predicting neural responses, and analyzing data, which is not yet automated as one loop.
aJs9FKYiA6.method: Given a hypothesis, the agent reasons over literature, designs an experiment, builds a stimulus set from manipulated or synthesized images, runs it on candidate brain encoding models, analyzes responses, and uses results to design stronger tests, with optional human input at any stage.
aJs9FKYiA6.key_idea: Close the scientific loop with agents that design stimuli, query fMRI encoding models as stand-in subjects, analyze responses, and iterate on follow-up experiments.
aJs9FKYiA6.evidence: Three increasingly open-ended problems: reproducing published findings with original and newly built stimuli, designing experiments that drive two brain regions differently, and a third problem cut off in the visible abstract; reviews mention a 36-study replication test.
aJs9FKYiA6.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract.
aJs9FKYiA6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see an important, timely need and a promising proof of concept, with a clearly written evaluation that reports failures alongside successes.
aJs9FKYiA6.main_concern: There are no baselines or ablations and novelty is unclear against existing agentic science systems and a general-purpose coding agent given the same tools.

RnhqiqxVYo.one_liner: ATCG retrofits classifiers with a per-class binary-hierarchy Pinball head producing sparse trait barcodes for auditing predictions.
RnhqiqxVYo.problem: Flat classifier heads over opaque embeddings make it hard to audit predictions when classes contain heterogeneous latent subpopulations.
RnhqiqxVYo.method: A Pinball head is a per-class binary hierarchy that learns basis traits and a combinatorial barcode space. Evidence aggregates bottom-up via Max-Dominance through intermediate-layer traits, and a geometric Molding Bonus encourages sibling specialization to prevent trait collapse, so barcodes show whether evidence is consistent, conflicting or insufficient.
RnhqiqxVYo.key_idea: Aggregate class evidence bottom-up by Max-Dominance over a per-class trait hierarchy while a Molding Bonus pushes sibling traits into complementary patterns, yielding sparse barcodes.
RnhqiqxVYo.evidence: Controlled experiments and benchmarks (the abstract is truncated; reviewers mention MNIST classification and a concept-bottleneck-model application) with ablations in the appendix.
RnhqiqxVYo.claimed_gains: Enables sample-level auditing of decision evidence and cohort-level localization of intra-class shifts with little loss in accuracy; no numbers stated.
RnhqiqxVYo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the structural specialization training strategy is a working contribution and the framework offers an actionable way to identify subpopulations and track shifts, with well-documented experiments.
RnhqiqxVYo.main_concern: The paper lacks comparison with simpler auditing baselines (such as clustering pretrained embeddings or prototype methods), and the hierarchy is functionally equivalent to a flat maxout head.

zt6hZQsriy.one_liner: Metamorphic testing of black-box AI agents under tone, language, and formulation changes, comparing operation graphs of permissions, disclosures, and trajectories.
zt6hZQsriy.problem: Agent evaluations use a single phrasing of each request, so it is unknown whether intent-equivalent requests lead to operationally consistent behavior.
zt6hZQsriy.method: AgentMT transforms prompts along tone, language, and formulation, runs them under the same agent setting, and represents observable executions as operation graphs to compare permission decisions, information disclosure, and execution trajectories.
zt6hZQsriy.key_idea: Treat intent-preserving prompt rewrites as metamorphic relations and measure consequence inconsistency through operation-graph similarity, using repeated runs of the original prompt as the noise baseline.
zt6hZQsriy.evidence: Three datasets and commercial AI agents across 27 model-dataset-transformation combinations, with additional experiments on three frontier models.
zt6hZQsriy.claimed_gains: Prompt variations reduce mean operation-graph similarity relative to repeated runs in all 27 combinations by up to 0.275, with significant increases in consequence inconsistency in 20 of 27 model-transformation combinations.
zt6hZQsriy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question of agent reliability under rephrasing is timely, and the repeated-run baseline and behavioral measures (permissions, disclosure, tool use) make the study useful.
zt6hZQsriy.main_concern: Behavioral differences are not shown to be real failures, and the findings largely confirm known prompt sensitivity without explaining which rewordings or tasks cause which changes.

ByYWlCeXYW.one_liner: Separate semantic-dimension risks combine through adaptive Hedge weighting to avoid Cartesian-product group explosion.
ByYWlCeXYW.problem: Crossing multiple semantic grouping dimensions creates too many sparsely populated groups for stable Group DRO.
ByYWlCeXYW.method: Dimension-wise DRO prunes highly correlated grouping axes and computes a KL-regularized robust risk for each retained dimension. Hedge-style weights adaptively combine these risks by prioritizing harder dimensions.
ByYWlCeXYW.key_idea: Optimize KL-regularized group risk separately within each nonredundant dimension, then adaptively weight dimension risks with a Hedge-style scheme.
ByYWlCeXYW.evidence: The paper presents a claimed worst-case risk bound and experiments with component ablations on medical VQA, general VQA, and autonomous driving.
ByYWlCeXYW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize combinatorial group growth as a meaningful problem and consider dimension-wise optimization a practical direction.
ByYWlCeXYW.main_concern: The justification for cross-dimension risk aggregation is incomplete, including a reviewer-identified inequality error in the central worst-case guarantee.

l9IMRiLRHo.one_liner: Same-task reward contrasts propose textual skill edits, and stored-trajectory likelihood replay selects patches.
l9IMRiLRHo.problem: Skill optimizers waste costly executions and obscure useful behavioral differences when aggregating sparse reward evidence across tasks.
l9IMRiLRHo.method: SkillGRACE samples multiple rollouts per task and uses group-relative advantages to construct contrastive evidence for skill edits. It screens patches by teacher-forced replay likelihoods on stored trajectories using a policy-optimization-style objective.
l9IMRiLRHo.key_idea: Generate skill patches from same-task high- versus low-reward trajectories and rank them by advantage-weighted likelihood changes during replay.
l9IMRiLRHo.evidence: Experiments span three task types with a frozen executor serving as its own editor, rollout-count comparisons, and same-task versus cross-task evidence ablations.
l9IMRiLRHo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the coherent use of grouped trajectories and replay to reduce environment interaction during skill editing.
l9IMRiLRHo.main_concern: Efficiency reporting counts environment rollouts but omits patch-generation, replay, and deployment costs needed to assess total computational savings.

njXUMh7PEX.one_liner: Shared token calibration couples distillation losses with gradient-guided allocation of supervision across response groups.
njXUMh7PEX.problem: Teacher-student disagreement alone does not reveal which supervision benefits a student at its current capacity and training state.
njXUMh7PEX.method: Attune follows a matched-exposure arithmetic intervention study with token-level calibration and gradient-guided group weighting for on-policy distillation. It applies the same calibration to candidate and reference losses so allocation comparisons reflect the learning signal.
njXUMh7PEX.key_idea: Calibrate candidate and reference token losses consistently, then use their gradient comparisons to allocate supervision across groups.
njXUMh7PEX.evidence: Matched-token arithmetic interventions, independent-probe tests, and evaluations across eight benchmarks and two model families include three training seeds and uniform and shuffled controls.
njXUMh7PEX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the learner-state supervision question and controlled interventions and ablations examining the allocation components.
njXUMh7PEX.main_concern: Incomplete coupling ablations and missing comparisons with related gradient-reweighting methods leave the specific combined design's contribution unclear.

7cF9AJU5fo.one_liner: Gradient-norm-matched substitutes test whether intermediate GNN distillation gains require trained teacher representations.
7cF9AJU5fo.problem: Accuracy gains from intermediate-layer distillation may reflect auxiliary optimization effects, which ordinary ablations confound with gradient strength.
7cF9AJU5fo.method: DETAIL replaces teacher hidden states with a teacher-free variance-covariance objective or untrained-network states and also substitutes Gaussian gradient noise. At each update, it scales each substitute's student-encoder gradient to the real teacher gradient's norm.
7cF9AJU5fo.key_idea: Replace teacher-derived auxiliary signals while matching their encoder-gradient norm at every update to compare information-dependent and optimization-related effects.
7cF9AJU5fo.evidence: Preregistered ogbn-arxiv experiments use a GraphSAGE student with 16 hidden units per layer, a logit-distillation baseline, and 30 paired seeds.
7cF9AJU5fo.claimed_gains: Intermediate distillation adds +1.04 percentage points (95% confidence interval [0.77, 1.32]), while teacher-free and untrained-network controls recover 0.98 and 0.96 of that gain, with a +0.13 pp upper confidence bound on the real teacher's added benefit over the teacher-free objective.
7cF9AJU5fo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value careful controlled experiments showing that alternative auxiliary signals can reproduce most gains in the studied setting.
7cF9AJU5fo.main_concern: A tiny student and brief auxiliary-supervision schedule limit generalization to sustained intermediate-layer distillation.

dn3CjB1r5q.one_liner: Execution-verified parametric CAD programs support linked perception, code understanding, generation, and editing evaluations.
dn3CjB1r5q.problem: CAD evaluations often measure coarse shape similarity without testing engineering parameters, construction operations, and editable program structure.
dn3CjB1r5q.method: BenchCAD builds a synthetic, standard-anchored collection of industrial CadQuery programs. It evaluates visual and code question answering, image-to-code generation, and instruction-guided editing to examine parametric and executable design capabilities.
dn3CjB1r5q.key_idea: Use verified parametric programs across industrial part families to evaluate linked visual, code, generation, and editing tasks.
dn3CjB1r5q.evidence: The benchmark contains 17,900 execution-verified programs across 106 industrial part families and evaluates 10+ frontier models, with family-held-out and QA-answerability checks.
dn3CjB1r5q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value combining CAD generation with parameter understanding and design editing to expose failures hidden by whole-shape similarity.
dn3CjB1r5q.main_concern: Insufficient characterization of evaluation subsets and their parameter and reasoning coverage weakens interpretation of aggregate capability scores.

Iz9J6j55yz.one_liner: Hidden-state coverage and slowly decaying training modes explain delayed length generalization in a linear recurrent model.
Iz9J6j55yz.problem: Fitting short sequences does not ensure that a recurrent model learns a transition that remains correct on longer sequences.
Iz9J6j55yz.method: The study analyzes an overparameterized linear RNN on sequential modular addition, characterizing when hidden-state coverage forces correct recurrence. It relates local training curvature and rollout visibility to delayed length generalization.
Iz9J6j55yz.key_idea: Hidden-state coverage constrains decoder-invisible directions, whose slow learning and horizon-dependent visibility can delay long-sequence correctness.
Iz9J6j55yz.evidence: Proofs establish coverage-based arbitrary-length generalization and small-initialization convergence, with numerical evidence and local curvature analysis in sequential modular addition.
Iz9J6j55yz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the theoretical importance of length generalization and the detailed mathematical analysis of coverage and training dynamics.
Iz9J6j55yz.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the restricted setting and conditional local analysis explain grokking in practical recurrent training.

TtYJ56Prxu.one_liner: Instruction-conditioned attention routes navigation reasoning through a coarse-to-fine voxel hierarchy before predicting aerial actions.
TtYJ56Prxu.problem: Aerial navigation instructions refer to cues spread across distances and spatial scales in continuous three-dimensional environments.
TtYJ56Prxu.method: A multi-scale voxel map encodes geometry and semantics at successive resolutions. Instruction-conditioned decision tokens aggregate voxel features and route attention to finer regions before combining with navigation history to predict actions.
TtYJ56Prxu.key_idea: Use instruction-conditioned token attention to select finer regions of a hierarchical voxel map for action prediction.
TtYJ56Prxu.evidence: AerialVLN-s experiments evaluate seen and unseen environments, inference latency, and component ablations.
TtYJ56Prxu.claimed_gains: The abstract reports 16.2% SR and 12.5% SDTW on seen environments, 8.8% SR and 3.9% SDTW on unseen environments, and 0.09s inference latency per navigation step.
TtYJ56Prxu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard multi-scale voxel reasoning as a well-motivated, computationally efficient approach to aerial navigation.
TtYJ56Prxu.main_concern: Reviewers find the ablations insufficient to separate attention-based routing gains from voxel representation, depth inputs, and auxiliary supervision.

gRrIQrxMlF.one_liner: Conservation laws separate capacity growth from routing dynamics in deep linear networks on directed acyclic graphs.
gRrIQrxMlF.problem: Theory poorly explains how learning distributes computation across branching and merging network paths.
gRrIQrxMlF.method: The analysis decomposes learning into a capacity variable and a routing variable on a finite polytope using conserved quantities. For balanced, uniform-depth positive scalar networks, it characterizes autonomous routing flow and stable chain-equivalent subgraphs.
gRrIQrxMlF.key_idea: Use conserved quantities to project edge-weight dynamics onto a routing polytope separate from overall capacity growth.
gRrIQrxMlF.evidence: Theoretical stability results cover positive scalar DAG networks, with analyses of mixed depths and nonzero charges and illustrative nonlinear-network experiments.
gRrIQrxMlF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the mathematical separation of global growth and routing and its insight into path specialization.
gRrIQrxMlF.main_concern: Reviewers question the applicability of positive-scalar, asymptotic routing results to practical networks trained with finite budgets.

c078KIQwro.one_liner: Sampling-sharpness statistics predict aggregation thresholds for set-valued language-model outputs without annotation.
c078KIQwro.problem: Majority thresholds misinterpret sample frequency as correctness probability and can reduce F1 in set-valued self-consistency.
c078KIQwro.method: A predictor maps unlabeled sampling-sharpness statistics to an aggregation threshold and supplies a label-free triage rule. The study also matches sampling sharpness across base and instruction-tuned models to analyze calibration differences.
c078KIQwro.key_idea: Predict the candidate-retention frequency threshold from unlabeled sampling-sharpness statistics instead of fixing it at one-half.
c078KIQwro.evidence: Experiments examine 5 kinds of set-valued output and 31 checkpoints across 246 pairs, with threshold-search comparisons and sharpness-matched calibration analyses.
c078KIQwro.claimed_gains: The predictor recovers 68% of the oracle gain, beats grid search using ten labelled sentences by +0.013 F1, and ties grid search using twenty-five.
c078KIQwro.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize useful evidence that conventional majority thresholds lose F1 and that aggregation mainly improves precision.
c078KIQwro.main_concern: The practical case for the learned threshold predictor remains limited by sparse application evidence and small gains over a simple fixed threshold.

YKBR6CMbFR.one_liner: Residual-stream bandwidth interventions test why noisy prediction targets impede representation learning in pixel-space diffusion transformers.
YKBR6CMbFR.problem: Equivalent diffusion prediction targets behave differently in large-patch transformers, with noise and velocity prediction failing where clean prediction succeeds.
YKBR6CMbFR.method: The study attributes this asymmetry to retaining noise-dependent input variation through the residual stream. It tests spectral concentration and persistent-state bandwidth through controlled interventions, including expanded and reorganized residual streams.
YKBR6CMbFR.key_idea: Expand and reorganize persistent residual-state bandwidth to accommodate noise-dependent input variation required by noisy-target readouts.
YKBR6CMbFR.evidence: Experiments examine whitening, patch geometry, multiple residual streams, spatial assignment, learned skips, representation quality, and model scaling.
YKBR6CMbFR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clear research question and extensive experiments connecting prediction targets, residual-state bandwidth, and representation learning.
YKBR6CMbFR.main_concern: Reviewers find the causal explanation insufficiently isolated from changes in noise geometry, state organization, and additional representation supervision.

G2nehA5BO3.one_liner: Comparative hypotheses become inductive principles that language models revise using new observations during scientific discovery.
G2nehA5BO3.problem: Translating accumulated experimental observations into reusable scientific principles requires substantial expertise and effort.
G2nehA5BO3.method: Principia forms comparative hypotheses from related inputs and outcomes, then synthesizes recurring relationships into inductive principles. New task observations revise the hypotheses and trigger principle reconstruction at test time.
G2nehA5BO3.key_idea: Iteratively synthesize recurring relationships across comparative hypotheses and revise those hypotheses using new experimental outcomes.
G2nehA5BO3.evidence: Benchmarks cover molecular optimization, protein engineering, gene perturbation, and molecular property prediction, with component ablations.
G2nehA5BO3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the structured observation-driven knowledge construction and its empirical performance across scientific tasks.
G2nehA5BO3.main_concern: Reviewers agree that the generated principles lack systematic validation of scientific correctness and causality.

dWCLtrAWoc.one_liner: Smoothed unlikelihood updates constrained by base-policy KL let language models adapt at test time using failures alone.
dWCLtrAWoc.problem: Problem-specific test-time training often assumes fine-grained rewards unavailable when verifiers only identify failed solutions.
dWCLtrAWoc.method: Controlled Redistribution reshapes token-level predictive distributions through smoothed unlikelihood training and a KL constraint to the base policy. It learns from failures under a binary-verifier protocol that stops at the first success.
dWCLtrAWoc.key_idea: Penalize failed-token predictions with smoothed unlikelihood while constraining distribution changes through base-policy KL regularization.
dWCLtrAWoc.evidence: Countdown, math, and code experiments compare adapted optimization objectives and ablate smoothing and KL regularization across two models.
dWCLtrAWoc.claimed_gains: On challenging math problems, CoRed lets Qwen3-4B-Instruct solve more than 2× as many problems as the frozen base model within 4,096 attempts.
dWCLtrAWoc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the failure-only question clear and the experiments supportive of improved solve rates and first-success sample efficiency.
dWCLtrAWoc.main_concern: Reviewers question the incremental contribution over prior feedback-based adaptation and existing unlikelihood-plus-KL methods.

1MSSYyRPQA.one_liner: Multimodal pseudo-grounding, unbalanced transport, and cross-prompt reinforcement refine weakly supervised human-object interaction detection.
1MSSYyRPQA.problem: Image-level interaction labels lack explicit human-object pair assignments, allowing erroneous associations to reinforce themselves.
1MSSYyRPQA.method: GTR-HOI tiers MLLM pseudo-groundings by spatial agreement and transfers localization supervision through unbalanced optimal transport. Expert-routed visual and semantic scoring then undergo confidence-weighted cross-prompt PPO refinement.
1MSSYyRPQA.key_idea: Transfer uncertain pseudo-groundings to detector pairs through soft transport, then refine binary interaction decisions using weighted feedback from alternative prompts.
1MSSYyRPQA.evidence: HOI experiments include staged ablations, random-prompt controls, hard-IoU and balanced-transport comparisons, and confidence-tier localization analysis.
1MSSYyRPQA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value directly addressing instance-assignment ambiguity and supporting the staged pipeline with relevant internal controls.
1MSSYyRPQA.main_concern: Compute-matched consistency or soft-label baselines are missing, so the independent benefit of PPO is unclear.

bVmK5Grycd.one_liner: Error-correcting codes, soft decoding, and unbiased optimal-transport sampling jointly embed recoverable multi-bit text watermarks.
bVmK5Grycd.problem: Multi-bit LLM watermarks struggle to recover complete messages under edits while preserving generated-text quality.
bVmK5Grycd.method: UniCoMark combines fixed-length linear coding and soft-information decoding with a recovery-matched sampling rule. An unbiasedness constraint formulates sampling as optimal transport, alongside a recovery theorem for textual attacks.
bVmK5Grycd.key_idea: Match error-resilient code recovery to an unbiased optimal-transport sampler that preserves soft evidence for message decoding.
bVmK5Grycd.evidence: Experiments across models and datasets test payload and length sweeps, clean recovery, textual edits, and text-quality measurements.
bVmK5Grycd.claimed_gains: With 256 tokens and a 32-bit payload, accuracy reaches 94.9% versus 60.2% and perplexity 10.10 versus 11.22; with 512 tokens, accuracy is 88.0% under 15% token-level mixed edits.
bVmK5Grycd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the coherent coding-and-sampling design and strong exact-message recovery results.
bVmK5Grycd.main_concern: The evidence does not jointly establish high message recovery and preserved text quality under the same operating settings.

zZiESv7P9C.one_liner: Source-aligned Lean declarations and dependency graphs map formally checked proof reuse across bandit and reinforcement-learning results.
zZiESv7P9C.problem: Researchers struggle to identify inherited arguments, changed assumptions, and unmatched proof obligations across bandit and reinforcement-learning results.
zZiESv7P9C.method: BanditRLlib pairs source-facing theorems with plain-language proofs and exact Lean 4 declarations. Its atlas separates compiler-checked dependency reuse from conceptual correspondences and records source-alignment checks.
zZiESv7P9C.key_idea: Link source theorems to Lean declarations while distinguishing checked dependency edges from separately recorded conceptual proof connections.
zZiESv7P9C.evidence: The library formalizes a classical bandit backbone, five setting extensions, and known-reward Hoeffding UCB-VI, with examples of concentration-lemma reuse and a corrected heavy-tailed pull-count bound.
zZiESv7P9C.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize a substantial, concrete formalization effort that makes proof dependencies and source discrepancies inspectable.
zZiESv7P9C.main_concern: The atlas has not been evaluated for whether it improves researchers' proof understanding or development efficiency.

PYVtfs7M3k.one_liner: Nested view-budget sweeps isolate how preselection changes VLM image selection, localization, and final 3D grounding.
PYVtfs7M3k.problem: Restricting views can remove useful evidence, but its effect on zero-shot 3D grounding may depend on the VLM.
PYVtfs7M3k.method: Observe-Then-Ground makes the VLM select an image and a 2D target box, then fixes segmentation, RGB-D lifting, and 3D instance assignment. Only the supplied observations vary across nested ranked view budgets.
PYVtfs7M3k.key_idea: Hold the 2D-to-3D grounding pathway fixed while varying nested query-ranked image sets across VLMs.
PYVtfs7M3k.evidence: Experiments use 250 ScanRefer queries, nested CLIP-ranked Top-3/6/12/24 inputs, dense Qwen3-VL checkpoints, GPT-5.6, and Gemini.
PYVtfs7M3k.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled protocol for isolating view-preselection effects and informing model-specific view-budget choices.
PYVtfs7M3k.main_concern: A small single-dataset query panel and one primary selector limit generalization across datasets, ranking methods, and grounding pipelines.

Xy4YXfZ1bK.one_liner: A temporally ordered task graph composes frozen low-rank adapters for continual weather and climate model adaptation.
Xy4YXfZ1bK.problem: Weather and climate models must acquire sequential prediction tasks without losing earlier capabilities or revisiting historical data.
Xy4YXfZ1bK.method: GUST stores task knowledge in frozen low-rank adapters and selectively combines their updates through a temporally ordered task graph. Structured relations, learned task geometry, and online transfer feedback guide reuse.
Xy4YXfZ1bK.key_idea: Route and compose frozen adapter updates through a task graph whose selection uses task relations and observed transfer.
Xy4YXfZ1bK.evidence: Experiments study sequential atmospheric-variable expansion, regional coverage expansion, and climate-projection response objectives.
Xy4YXfZ1bK.claimed_gains: In variable continual learning, GUST reports average relative wRMSE of 1.10 and reduces relative forgetting from 39.55% to 9.67%; in regional continual learning, it reports relative wRMSE of 1.04.
Xy4YXfZ1bK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers consider continual adaptation of weather and climate models a meaningful practical problem.
Xy4YXfZ1bK.main_concern: Reported climate-projection metrics and regional-forgetting claims contain inconsistencies that undermine the experimental conclusions.

ndwYg43fWM.one_liner: Motion-adaptive feature sampling and explicit 3D supervision train geometrically consistent video depth predictions.
ndwYg43fWM.problem: Monocular video depth estimation lacks sufficient cross-frame modeling, geometric constraints, and scalable supervision for consistent 3D reconstruction.
ndwYg43fWM.method: G2 uses Motion-Adaptive Implicit Alignment to sample query-relevant cross-frame features and constrains back-projected depth with intra-frame and inter-frame 3D supervision. Multi-View Geometric Distillation transfers reconstruction-teacher geometry to unlabeled videos.
ndwYg43fWM.key_idea: Combine sparse motion-adaptive temporal feature sampling with direct supervision of back-projected geometry and teacher-generated pseudo 3D targets.
ndwYg43fWM.evidence: Zero-shot depth and reconstruction benchmarks include 7-Scenes, NRGBD, Sintel, and ScanNet, with ablations of alignment, geometric losses, and distillation.
ndwYg43fWM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize strong depth and reconstruction results and the practical value of supervising 3D geometric quality.
ndwYg43fWM.main_concern: The method is insufficiently distinguished from deformable attention and geometry-weighted depth regression through matched comparisons.

SKVaZxIPLD.one_liner: Reference-to-student confidence gaps dynamically mask reasoning-step losses during long-chain-of-thought supervised fine-tuning.
SKVaZxIPLD.problem: Uniform one-hot supervision can conflict with distribution-matching gradients when the student already exceeds reference confidence on sampled reasoning steps.
SKVaZxIPLD.method: CGSS precomputes reference scores for steps and obtains current student scores from the training forward pass. It uses their confidence gap to dynamically select step losses on a fixed trace corpus without full-vocabulary teacher distributions.
SKVaZxIPLD.key_idea: Mask each reasoning-step loss according to the gap between its precomputed reference score and the student's evolving confidence.
SKVaZxIPLD.evidence: Experiments across five mathematics and science benchmarks compare four students against vanilla SFT, static selection, and matched-rate random masking.
SKVaZxIPLD.claimed_gains: CGSS reports an average accuracy gain of up to 6.3 percentage points.
SKVaZxIPLD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize consistent reasoning gains and useful ablations of confidence-based dynamic selection.
SKVaZxIPLD.main_concern: The confidence gate's robustness is unclear because segmentation heuristics, margin choices, and sensitivity are insufficiently established.

SpZY5zC6JU.one_liner: Controlled recoverable perturbations and restricted reference guidance elicit corrective interactions for training multi-agent judges and verifiers.
SpZY5zC6JU.problem: Ordinary multi-agent rollouts often provide immediate approvals or repeated failures rather than useful checking and repair supervision.
SpZY5zC6JU.method: CoEvoke introduces recoverable difficulties during trajectory collection and supplies restricted reference-based investigative guidance. It records linked interactions, evidence, decisions, and task outcomes to train collaborative decision roles with frozen solvers.
SpZY5zC6JU.key_idea: Perturb collection-time candidates and provide limited reference guidance to produce checking, feedback, and repair trajectories.
SpZY5zC6JU.evidence: The dataset contains 4,567 trajectories over 4,130 software-engineering and reasoning tasks, with 2,287 same-task pairs and matched-data downstream training experiments.
SpZY5zC6JU.claimed_gains: Feedback increases by 47.72–100 percentage points, ACPBench-Hard success rises from 35.38% to 42.12% (+6.73 points), and SWE verifier training gains 7.60–9.40 points over interface-matched untrained references.
SpZY5zC6JU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the collection problem well motivated and recognize downstream benefits from inducing recoverable errors.
SpZY5zC6JU.main_concern: Missing simpler and distribution-matched controls leave unclear whether gains come from the framework or merely from more repair-label examples.

FcTalRSKPH.one_liner: Counterfactual message replacements and downstream reruns estimate credit for individual messages in LLM agent teams.
FcTalRSKPH.problem: Learned critics and trajectory scores approximate message credit without executing the counterfactual continuations that define it.
FcTalRSKPH.method: C3 replaces one message at a recorded decision point and continues the team to terminal reward. When the trace contains the full resumable state, Monte Carlo comparisons estimate message credit and supply training advantages.
FcTalRSKPH.key_idea: Hold the recorded prefix fixed, substitute alternative messages, and estimate their terminal-reward effects through repeated continuations.
FcTalRSKPH.evidence: Credit-noise analysis covers six workflows with two to ten decision points, independent continuation references, and training experiments on small mathematical agent teams.
FcTalRSKPH.claimed_gains: With 4 continuations, C3 reaches 0.69 rank correlation against a 16-continuation reference versus 0.29 for a critic, and uses 37% fewer training tokens than MAPPO.
FcTalRSKPH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find counterfactual continuation a clear credit-estimation approach and recognize gains on the evaluated math tasks.
FcTalRSKPH.main_concern: Training comparisons do not isolate credit assignment from differences in rollout sampling, role balance, and length normalization.

tDquT092cH.one_liner: Behavior cloning and learned-game equilibrium solving combine to estimate extensive-form game strategies from fixed datasets.
tDquT092cH.problem: Offline game data often omit unilateral deviations needed to verify equilibria, and shared evaluation resources are lacking.
tDquT092cH.method: The paper defines offline equilibrium finding and constructs datasets from random, expert, learning, and hybrid strategies. BOMB combines behavior cloning with a model-based component that can use online equilibrium solvers such as CFR or PSRO offline.
tDquT092cH.key_idea: Combine behavior-cloned strategies with equilibrium strategies computed in a learned game model.
tDquT092cH.evidence: Controlled experiments vary dataset composition and size across eight imperfect-information extensive-form games, including Leduc poker.
tDquT092cH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the offline equilibrium-finding formulation and datasets for studying behavior quality and coverage.
tDquT092cH.main_concern: Main experiments tune BOMB's combination weight through real-game interaction, violating the strictly offline information constraint.

ISGH4DAv4F.one_liner: Unresolved visual claims guide active view construction and transport-based evidence selection for zero-shot 3D grounding.
ISGH4DAv4F.problem: Local views lose relational anchors while global views obscure object details needed to distinguish similar candidates.
ISGH4DAv4F.method: ARIADNE decomposes expressions into candidate-specific attribute and relational claims and constructs captured, stitched, or rendered shared views. Online Evidence Transport matches unresolved evidence needs to views using visibility, quality, graph structure, and observation history.
ISGH4DAv4F.key_idea: Track unresolved candidate claims and match their evidence needs to complementary views through a regularized transport objective.
ISGH4DAv4F.evidence: ScanRefer and Nr3D evaluations include component ablations and comparisons using the same multimodal model.
ISGH4DAv4F.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find ambiguity-guided active perception well motivated and recognize competitive grounding results.
ISGH4DAv4F.main_concern: The evaluation does not establish the active planner's advantage over simpler strategies under matched observation and computational budgets.

he3e0nUDaI.one_liner: Counterfactual rescoring of realized responses assigns hindsight credit to agent-history deletion decisions.
he3e0nUDaI.problem: Sparse task rewards and token savings alone cannot distinguish useful history deletion from harmful information loss.
he3e0nUDaI.method: HiDe scores the same realized next response under reduced history and a matched context restoring newly deleted blocks, sharing the new observation. It combines response-dependence gaps with discounted token savings to supervise DELETE/WAIT decisions and task-gated trajectory rewards.
he3e0nUDaI.key_idea: Compare next-response likelihood with deleted history restored, then discount deletion savings when the response still depends on removed blocks.
he3e0nUDaI.evidence: Experiments assess task quality and input efficiency across several environments, including paired deletion deployment on 200 WebShop tasks.
he3e0nUDaI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate inexpensive hindsight supervision from forward rescoring without extra rollouts or a separate teacher.
he3e0nUDaI.main_concern: Sensitivity of one realized response does not reliably establish that deleted information is unnecessary for future task success.

ziKfm6LEJN.one_liner: Dependence analysis and target-domain calibration select complementary safety guards while controlling ensemble false alarms.
ziKfm6LEJN.problem: Correlated safety-guard errors can make naive fusion overcount evidence and raise false alarms with little detection benefit.
ziKfm6LEJN.method: A Gaussian-copula model analyzes excess evidence and limits on fusion gains from additional guards. A separate calibration method sets one alarm threshold for a selected configuration using target-domain safe examples, with finite-sample marginal control under exchangeability.
ziKfm6LEJN.key_idea: Measure guards' conditional information and calibrate the selected ensemble's final threshold on safe target-domain examples.
ziKfm6LEJN.evidence: Experiments cover five human-labelled datasets, up to ten open guards, and seven deployment settings, alongside dependence analysis and calibration guarantees.
ziKfm6LEJN.claimed_gains: A naive cascade raises a nominal 5% false-alarm rate to 30%, while selected subsets retain 96–100% of full-ensemble detection at 8–12% of its parameter-memory cost.
ziKfm6LEJN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize correlated guard failures as a practical problem and value the calibration guarantee and empirical analysis.
ziKfm6LEJN.main_concern: Gaussian assumptions fit actual guard scores poorly, with measured performance sometimes exceeding the predicted fusion limits.

m3ugNVlGNi.one_liner: Provisional answer hypotheses drive viewpoint checks and searches for answer-changing evidence before embodied agents commit.
m3ugNVlGNi.problem: Embodied agents may accept plausible interpretations before collecting enough evidence to establish their correctness.
m3ugNVlGNi.method: Sure-EQA re-examines existing support from alternative viewpoints and probes unseen regions for evidence that could change a candidate answer. Verification findings determine whether to accept, further test, or revise the hypothesis.
m3ugNVlGNi.key_idea: Use a provisional answer to direct environmental observations toward supporting or falsifying that specific hypothesis.
m3ugNVlGNi.evidence: A-EQA and EXPRESS-Bench experiments compare answer correctness and path-weighted performance, including continued exploration under matched additional observation.
m3ugNVlGNi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the diagnosis of premature commitment and the empirical evaluation of training-free environmental verification.
m3ugNVlGNi.main_concern: Comparisons omit existing verification methods needed to separate the contribution from established active-perception and self-correction approaches.

HaW2azPqbq.one_liner: Progressively stricter rubric checks adjust holistic self-confidence to reduce overconfidence in LLM answers.
HaW2azPqbq.problem: Verbalized confidence often remains high on incorrect answers, limiting its usefulness for deciding when to seek review.
HaW2azPqbq.method: The paper elicits verification scores under increasingly strict rubric criteria and combines them with direct self-assessment. Its calibration variants use rubric factors, including an adaptive repeatability gate, to revise reported confidence.
HaW2azPqbq.key_idea: Combine holistic confidence with scores from a ladder of increasingly stringent answer-verification rubrics.
HaW2azPqbq.evidence: Experiments cover eight reasoning and domain-knowledge benchmarks, three model families, and model scales from 8B to 32B, with matched-scaling and shuffled-pairing controls.
HaW2azPqbq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the calibration problem important and the training-free method simple, with broad empirical evaluation.
HaW2azPqbq.main_concern: The rubric aggregation and adaptive gate are heuristic, with insufficient evidence that their complexity adds value over simpler corrections.

g1IR4vp8WS.one_liner: Future-target reconstruction shapes shared video-world-model features for real-time endoscopic action prediction.
g1IR4vp8WS.problem: Current-observation policies struggle with tissue deformation, occlusion, and viewpoint changes without modeling future anatomical dynamics.
