g1IR4vp8WS.method: EndoWAM predicts future target regions from intermediate video-denoising features and couples a grounding diffusion transformer with a discrete action expert. Deployment removes the grounding branch and predicts actions from a single Video DiT forward pass.
g1IR4vp8WS.key_idea: Train shared predictive video features with future target-region supervision, then reuse those features for action prediction without the grounding branch.
g1IR4vp8WS.evidence: EndoMotion and physical closed-loop evaluations cover ureteroscopy, esophagoscopy, and ERCP, with ablations and unseen viewpoint, environment, and target tests.
g1IR4vp8WS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value physical endoscope evaluations and consistent performance benefits from target-grounded training.
g1IR4vp8WS.main_concern: The evaluation omits the detector-plus-rule controller that generates action labels, leaving improvement over the supervision source unclear.

YUaU4YBQGd.one_liner: Layerwise hidden-state clusters aligned across layers yield discrete computational trajectories for interpretation and failure prediction.
YUaU4YBQGd.problem: Continuous high-dimensional hidden dynamics are difficult to inspect as stable, behaviorally meaningful computational structure.
YUaU4YBQGd.method: HSS clusters hidden representations within layers and aligns adjacent-layer centroids into a shared geometric-state vocabulary. It converts forward passes into discrete state sequences for occupancy analysis, count-based prediction, and online failure monitoring.
YUaU4YBQGd.key_idea: Cluster each layer's activations and align neighboring centroids to encode forward computation as a discrete state sequence.
YUaU4YBQGd.evidence: Experiments test stability across seeds, sample sizes, models, and clustering choices, plus capability and safety prediction, online monitoring, reconstruction, and activation editing.
YUaU4YBQGd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple training-free representation and evidence that discrete states preserve useful computational structure.
YUaU4YBQGd.main_concern: Small predictive and monitoring gains lack sufficient uncertainty estimates and baseline-tuning detail to establish a reliable advantage.

9HVCTwPTpX.one_liner: Source-linked semantic trees combine structural and lexical selection to build focused contexts for long-document question answering.
9HVCTwPTpX.problem: Even when full documents fit in context, irrelevant material can obscure the evidence needed for a specific question.
9HVCTwPTpX.method: TreeFuse constructs a reusable semantic hierarchy in one generation and links node descriptions to original source spans. Query-time structural–semantic scoring and lexical attribution select source nodes, whose union with ancestor context retains local text and relations.
9HVCTwPTpX.key_idea: Use semantic and lexical scores to select source-linked tree nodes, then include ancestor context and original text for answering.
9HVCTwPTpX.evidence: Experiments evaluate three LongBench tasks across four frontier answer models, with baseline comparisons and selection-component ablations.
9HVCTwPTpX.claimed_gains: TreeFuse improves average QA-F1 by 1.72 points over full-context prompting while reducing answer-context length by 58.55%.
9HVCTwPTpX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value reusable source-grounded context construction and recognize competitive question-answering performance.
9HVCTwPTpX.main_concern: Different scorer strengths and preprocessing budgets prevent attributing the gains specifically to the semantic-tree representation.

F70tJ4q4Mc.one_liner: Affine alignment connects truncated time-series model states to native forecasting heads after layerwise recoverability probing.
F70tJ4q4Mc.problem: Intermediate time-series representations may contain forecast information yet remain incompatible with pretrained output pathways.
F70tJ4q4Mc.method: The study probes forecast recoverability and representation geometry across model depth to identify a forecasting tunnel. Lightweight affine adapters align retained intermediate states with the native prediction pathway for direct model truncation.
F70tJ4q4Mc.key_idea: Fit an affine map that makes intermediate hidden states compatible with the pretrained forecasting pathway after removing later blocks.
F70tJ4q4Mc.evidence: Layerwise probes and end-to-end timing evaluate Chronos-2, TimesFM-3, and TiRex across datasets with diverse sampling frequencies.
F70tJ4q4Mc.claimed_gains: Aligned Chronos-2 remains within a median 3.1% of the full model after retaining 4 of its 12 blocks while running 2.43× faster.
F70tJ4q4Mc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating forecast recoverability from head compatibility and measuring practical truncation speedups across architectures.
F70tJ4q4Mc.main_concern: Dataset-specific adapter fitting requires target-domain samples and full-model passes, limiting zero-shot acceleration and generalization claims.

8UtITubGZH.one_liner: Presage predicts output-length distributions from activations and sampling parameters to coordinate routing and admission in disaggregated LLM serving.
8UtITubGZH.problem: Unknown remaining generation lengths cause imbalanced decode-instance loads and preemption cascades under myopic routing and admission heuristics.
8UtITubGZH.method: A shared predictor combines intermediate activations with sampling parameters to estimate a five-class output-length distribution. A load-dependent router switches between token reservation and resource-pressure projection, while per-token-latency measurements guide admission within decode instances.
8UtITubGZH.key_idea: A shared sampling-aware length predictor couples inter-instance resource reservations with intra-instance admission control.
8UtITubGZH.evidence: Serving experiments compare prediction against matched TRAIL++ and μ-Serve baselines, measure overlap with prefill, and ablate predicted-demand routing.
8UtITubGZH.claimed_gains: The predictor improves cosine similarity by 16.5%–47.9%, runs at a median 12.7 ms latency, and completes within prefill for 99.8% of requests.
8UtITubGZH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate including sampling parameters in length prediction and using predictions for practical scheduling decisions.
8UtITubGZH.main_concern: Missing stronger matched scheduling and predictor comparisons leave the source and robustness of the serving gains unclear.

SbJGc2F0Tr.one_liner: TipsWarm maintains a bounded pool of skill-derived reminders and screens them for injection at each agent turn.
SbJGc2F0Tr.problem: Agents may retrieve skills only after committing to ineffective approaches, while persistent guidance can add irrelevant advice and maintenance costs.
SbJGc2F0Tr.method: TipsWarm extracts warm tips from reusable skills and maintains a budgeted reminder pool. Event-triggered LLM assessment updates the pool, while inexpensive per-turn screening selects tips for context injection.
SbJGc2F0Tr.key_idea: Separating event-triggered tip assessment from cheap per-turn filtering makes selected skill guidance available before explicit skill retrieval.
SbJGc2F0Tr.evidence: Three coding and iterative task-execution benchmarks compare TipsWarm with skill and general-memory baselines, including component ablations and augmentation of an existing skill bundle.
SbJGc2F0Tr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the early-guidance problem practical and the lightweight reminder mechanism easy to integrate with existing skill workflows.
SbJGc2F0Tr.main_concern: The evaluation does not isolate reminder scheduling from simpler proactive skill retrieval or concise-context injection under matched budgets.

CRKfy6oeGA.one_liner: POR jointly updates noisy image states using a posterior-overlap surrogate before resuming the original text-to-image sampler.
CRKfy6oeGA.problem: Distances between predicted clean images can miss overlapping posterior distributions that produce repetitive image groups for one prompt.
CRKfy6oeGA.method: POR derives a posterior-overlap upper bound related to symmetrized KL divergence under a posterior-variance condition. A model-based divergence estimate drives joint updates of a fixed image group at one early sampling timestep without evaluating posterior densities.
CRKfy6oeGA.key_idea: A model-estimated symmetrized KL surrogate repels overlapping clean-image posteriors through joint optimization of their noisy states.
CRKfy6oeGA.evidence: Experiments use Stable Diffusion 3 and FLUX.1-dev on COCO and DPG-Bench, alongside controlled overlap studies and quality-diversity comparisons.
CRKfy6oeGA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the distributional motivation for diversification and the theoretical rationale beyond distances between clean-image predictions.
CRKfy6oeGA.main_concern: The practical validity and tightness of the overlap bound during real sampling optimization remain insufficiently validated.

9hTYJwDSwS.one_liner: Sonar uses instruction-conditioned NLI scores and sentence-graph expansion to prune suspicious spans from untrusted external text.
9hTYJwDSwS.problem: External text exposes retrieval and tool-using agents to indirect prompt injections, while existing judges and trained detectors have generalization weaknesses.
9hTYJwDSwS.method: Sonar builds a local sentence graph conditioned on trusted instructions using entailment and contradiction scores from an off-the-shelf NLI model. It detects semantic outliers and directives, expands suspicious spans through neighboring semantic relations, and removes them before downstream use.
9hTYJwDSwS.key_idea: Instruction-conditioned semantic and directive signals seed sentence-graph expansion that identifies external text spans for removal.
9hTYJwDSwS.evidence: Experiments span multiple models, datasets, and attacks, including AlpacaFarm, nine baseline defenses, ablations, and task-fidelity measurements.
9hTYJwDSwS.claimed_gains: Sonar reduces attack success rates to at most 2.4% on AlpacaFarm while outperforming nine baseline defenses without modifying the downstream LLM.
9hTYJwDSwS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a broadly applicable defense that uses non-generative semantic analysis without fine-tuning the target LLM.
9hTYJwDSwS.main_concern: Semantically blended, implicit, or adaptively paraphrased attacks may evade the signals, and current adaptive evaluations do not adequately test the whole defense.

1QzAWMsbfU.one_liner: Dr. OPD alternates reward-driven token-weight updates with student distillation steps to prioritize useful teacher corrections.
1QzAWMsbfU.problem: Uniformly weighted teacher supervision ignores differences in how individual token corrections affect the student's final task performance.
1QzAWMsbfU.method: Dr. OPD formulates token-weighted on-policy distillation as bilevel optimization, selecting weights to maximize the resulting student's expected reward. An iterative solver alternates closed-form weight updates with a gradient step on the weighted student objective.
1QzAWMsbfU.key_idea: Expected downstream student reward determines token-level teacher weights through alternating bilevel optimization.
1QzAWMsbfU.evidence: A theoretical comparison under regularity conditions accompanies experiments on mathematical reasoning and code generation, with baseline comparisons and short training-trajectory analyses.
1QzAWMsbfU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value optimizing teacher-supervision weights for student task reward and find the resulting update simple and appealing.
1QzAWMsbfU.main_concern: Checkpoint and hyperparameter selection on evaluation benchmarks, without independent validation or multi-run uncertainty, may inflate the reported gains.

PrsdDBpbSu.one_liner: OneVLA shares an action head across navigation and manipulation and trains progressively with curated data and reasoning traces.
PrsdDBpbSu.problem: Task-specific VLA architectures separate navigation from manipulation and limit shared embodied capabilities.
PrsdDBpbSu.method: OneVLA uses a unified action head for navigation and manipulation and a multistage training procedure with curated data and chain-of-thought fine-tuning. Joint training aims to transfer information between the task domains.
PrsdDBpbSu.key_idea: Train navigation and manipulation through a shared action representation and head with progressive cross-task supervision.
PrsdDBpbSu.evidence: Simulated and real-robot experiments include joint-training comparisons and mobile manipulation on RoboCasa365.
PrsdDBpbSu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard joint navigation-manipulation learning as useful and recognize benefits from joint training.
PrsdDBpbSu.main_concern: The unified head's independent contribution is unclear without a matched shared-backbone baseline using separate task heads.

LrtMHO5gy0.one_liner: Kinematic counterfactual supervision binds predicted robot poses in generated futures to the actions proposed by world-action policies.
LrtMHO5gy0.problem: Demonstrations provide one action per state and do not constrain predicted futures under alternative actions.
LrtMHO5gy0.method: ANCHOR compares predicted-future robot poses with poses implied by forward kinematics and camera calibration. Perturbed actions supply counterfactual pose targets, while regions outside the arm's swept volume receive an invariance constraint.
LrtMHO5gy0.key_idea: Perturb actions and enforce their projected kinematic pose changes in predicted futures while preserving regions outside the swept volume.
LrtMHO5gy0.evidence: CF-BENCH measures action sensitivity under in-distribution and held-out perturbations, and task evaluation covers RoboCasa, RoboTwin 2.0, and LIBERO-Plus.
LrtMHO5gy0.claimed_gains: ANCHOR reaches keypoint responses of 0.79 in distribution and 0.71 on held-out perturbations, with task-success gains reported as "2.3--6.6 percentage" over base-FT.
LrtMHO5gy0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value physically grounded supervision for unexecuted actions and the focus on action-future consistency.
LrtMHO5gy0.main_concern: Dependence on accurate kinematics, camera calibration, and pose readout limits robustness and transfer beyond the simulated settings.

eVZQ4OtyrH.one_liner: ReDiM decodes low-dimensional corrections to a frozen RNA-to-protein predictor using spatial RNA and metabolic context.
eVZQ4OtyrH.problem: Direct RNA-to-protein predictors absorb context-dependent biological discordance into undifferentiated prediction error.
eVZQ4OtyrH.method: ReDiM freezes a reference predictor and represents observed-minus-reference protein residuals in a training-fitted 16-dimensional basis. It predicts coordinates from reference expectations, spatial RNA, and reaction-level flux enrichment scores derived from a metabolic network.
eVZQ4OtyrH.key_idea: Predict reference-relative protein residual coordinates from multiple RNA-accessible views and decode them through a fixed protein basis.
eVZQ4OtyrH.evidence: Domain-holdout experiments on ALD, ALS, and Brain compare residual representations and prediction controls, including full-dimensional residuals and shuffled metabolic features.
eVZQ4OtyrH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the explicit, inspectable correction representation and controls comparing it with alternative prediction designs.
eVZQ4OtyrH.main_concern: Small or inconsistent gains and incomplete matched controls leave the additional spatial and metabolic components' practical benefit uncertain.

CQaSbDjtYm.one_liner: Auxiliary wrist-image contact and force prediction trains VLA policies to represent the physical interactions caused by their actions.
CQaSbDjtYm.problem: Action imitation alone does not explicitly represent contact and force, while physical sensor supervision is often unavailable.
CQaSbDjtYm.method: Grounding Force trains a VLA to predict contact and force maps aligned with the wrist-camera image alongside actions. Training-only supervision uses simulation targets or pseudo-labels, and deployment requires no force or tactile sensors.
CQaSbDjtYm.key_idea: Supervise action-conditioned contact and force maps in the wrist-camera frame as auxiliary policy-training targets.
CQaSbDjtYm.evidence: Four backbones are evaluated on RoboCasa and RoboTwin 2.0, with simulation-trained pseudo-labels supporting single-arm and bimanual real-robot experiments.
CQaSbDjtYm.claimed_gains: Grounding Force improves simulation success rate by up to 7.3% and improves π0.5 by 13.0% on both real single-arm and bimanual robots.
CQaSbDjtYm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical image-aligned interaction targets and evaluation across VLA architectures and robotic settings.
CQaSbDjtYm.main_concern: Real-world pseudo-labels do not sufficiently establish accurate force information or isolate its contribution from grasp-related auxiliary supervision.

4DnDvAwDsJ.one_liner: DUET reads memory-use strategies from activations and dynamically adjusts memory-specific intervention directions and strengths during generation.
4DnDvAwDsJ.problem: Retrieving relevant memories does not ensure appropriate use, especially when some memories should influence output and others should be suppressed.
4DnDvAwDsJ.method: DUET uses strategy readouts from a frozen model to set control targets, updates memory-specific directions each generation step, and adapts intervention strength to output-distribution changes. Model parameters remain fixed.
4DnDvAwDsJ.key_idea: Read memory-use requirements from activations and adapt memory-specific steering directions and strengths at each decoding step.
4DnDvAwDsJ.evidence: Six backbones and three benchmarks support memory-use evaluation, with predicted-strategy controls and component ablations.
4DnDvAwDsJ.claimed_gains: On RPEval with Qwen3-8B, DUET achieves 67.83% Multi Macro and satisfies all memory-use requirements in 49.41% of mixed queries.
4DnDvAwDsJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value distinguishing memory-strategy identification from its enforcement during generation and examining mixed memory-use requirements.
4DnDvAwDsJ.main_concern: DUET and baselines use different valid test populations, so reported gains are not paired comparisons on a common query set.

dPjPHJEUe6.one_liner: Simultaneous confidence bands determine maximin prefix weights and preserve existing weights when sampled prefix values remain indistinguishable.
dPjPHJEUe6.problem: Finite-sample prefix-value estimates can make direct reweighting decrease the sampled-prefix objective in RLVR.
dPjPHJEUe6.method: TraceBand builds simultaneous confidence intervals and solves a closed-form maximin reweighting problem. It leaves weights unchanged when intervals share an intersection and guarantees nonnegative sampled-objective gain when the bands contain true values.
dPjPHJEUe6.key_idea: Choose prefix weights maximizing worst-case improvement over simultaneous value bands, abstaining from reweighting when all prefixes could have equal value.
dPjPHJEUe6.evidence: Theoretical reweighting guarantees accompany mathematical-reasoning and code-generation experiments across models with matched-sampling plug-in and continuation controls.
dPjPHJEUe6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the explicit treatment of estimation uncertainty and precisely scoped robust prefix-reweighting guarantees.
dPjPHJEUe6.main_concern: The study does not adequately quantify how conservative reweighting trades prevented harmful updates against foregone practical learning gains.

WbzQCFZBkR.one_liner: Component-specific LoRA installation of synthetic facts probes knowledge conflict, retrieval failure, and confident hallucination in transformers.
WbzQCFZBkR.problem: Language models can remain confident when context conflicts with stored facts or queried knowledge is absent.
WbzQCFZBkR.method: The study installs random entity-to-code facts through LoRA targeting MLP, QK, or VO components and varies training phrasings. It compares recall, reading, conflict, and missing-knowledge conditions using representations and output behavior.
WbzQCFZBkR.key_idea: Control fact content, robustness, and storage location through modular LoRA to separate retrieval and confidence failure modes.
WbzQCFZBkR.evidence: Synthetic-code experiments vary adapter placement and phrasing on a single 3B base model, supported by representation and sublayer-Jacobian analyses.
WbzQCFZBkR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value synthetic facts as a controlled way to isolate learned knowledge and distinct failure conditions.
WbzQCFZBkR.main_concern: Mechanistic conclusions from synthetic code facts on one model may not generalize to natural-language knowledge in pretrained weights.

ynzsieRXVE.one_liner: CASD separates consensus-based pseudo-answer choice from initial-trajectory context selection for label-free on-policy self-distillation.
ynzsieRXVE.problem: More accurate generated pseudo-answers do not necessarily provide better self-distillation supervision.
ynzsieRXVE.method: Compound Computation for Amplification represents generation calls and programmatic operations as a DAG to separate generation quality from learning outcomes. CASD uses terminal consensus to choose a pseudo-answer while preferring a matching initial reasoning trajectory as teaching context.
ynzsieRXVE.key_idea: Use aggregated consensus to select pseudo-answers but select matching initial-pool reasoning traces as privileged distillation context.
ynzsieRXVE.evidence: Model and benchmark comparisons include controls holding generation records and pseudo-answers fixed while varying teaching-context selection.
ynzsieRXVE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating answer selection from teaching-context selection and the controlled evidence that reference trajectories affect learning.
ynzsieRXVE.main_concern: Missing comparisons under matched generation budgets leave the need for aggregation and its benefit over existing self-distillation methods unclear.

ez7Swk45Se.one_liner: MAPS consolidates retrieved evidence into refined reasoning states and explores parallel retrieval directions to reduce query-intent drift.
ez7Swk45Se.problem: Interleaved reasoning and retrieval can reinforce redundant or drifting query trajectories and restrict search diversity.
ez7Swk45Se.method: MAPS retains retrieved knowledge with a refined reasoning state, then generates multiple retrieval directions in parallel. A refinement agent consolidates new evidence and updates the state for subsequent iterations.
ez7Swk45Se.key_idea: Replace accumulated reasoning history with a refined evidence state and branch retrieval into multiple parallel query directions.
ez7Swk45Se.evidence: Single-hop, multi-hop, and scientific QA evaluations include baselines, ablations, query/evidence similarity analysis, and stopping-round measurements.
ez7Swk45Se.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value identifying query-intent drift and studying refined reasoning states with parallel search.
ez7Swk45Se.main_concern: Unmatched inference and retrieval budgets prevent attributing gains to the proposed reasoning design rather than additional computation.

UJyQHtKArW.one_liner: Spectral head budgets and endpoint ablation errors produce fixed width and depth pruning masks for few-step video diffusion.
UJyQHtKArW.problem: Few-step video diffusion retains full model width and depth, while each pruning error has few later steps available for correction.
UJyQHtKArW.method: SEAE sets attention-head budgets from activation Gram-matrix spectral energy and selects heads by CSS-inspired elimination with scalar refitting. It scores block removal by final-latent error and intersects low-error candidates across timesteps into a static mask.
UJyQHtKArW.key_idea: Combine spectral-energy head allocation with endpoint-error block selection, retaining only block deletions acceptable across solver timesteps.
UJyQHtKArW.evidence: A four-step Turbo Wan2.2 5B TI2V study uses calibration forward passes, pruning ablations, and VBench-I2V evaluation.
UJyQHtKArW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical static pruned model and criteria accounting for module and timestep sensitivity.
UJyQHtKArW.main_concern: Near-unchanged aggregate quality scores conceal a substantial reduction in dynamic degree and motion.

DJOmNDQ2wH.one_liner: Analyzes sampled-token on-policy distillation failure dynamics via teacher top-p mass, cross-token gradient interference, and rollout state drift.
DJOmNDQ2wH.problem: On-policy distillation for LLM post-training frequently exhibits spurious agreement, repetitive loops, excessive length, and sharp performance collapse for poorly understood reasons.
DJOmNDQ2wH.method: The authors trace sampled-token on-policy distillation learning dynamics across three stages: local failure to resolve mismatch characterized by student mass on the teacher's top-p set, cross-position gradient interference from mismatched states, and mode suppression driving rollouts into unreliable teacher states. Reviews note they also propose a state-dependent forward-KL routing remedy motivated by this analysis.
DJOmNDQ2wH.key_idea: Trace sampled-token on-policy distillation failures from low student mass on the teacher's top-p set through cross-position gradient interference to mode-suppressing state drift during rollouts.
DJOmNDQ2wH.evidence: Theoretical gradient-dynamics analysis, leave-one-out empirical interventions, and post-training experiments (on Qwen3 models over math benchmarks such as AIME and AMC per reviews).
DJOmNDQ2wH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the systematic learning-dynamics investigation linking local token updates, cross-position gradient interference, and subsequent on-policy sampling drift.
DJOmNDQ2wH.main_concern: Empirical validation is restricted to small Qwen models on narrow math datasets under sampled-token updates, while the semi-gradient theory and heuristic forward-KL routing yield limited, under-explained gains.

T818Qd4Eks.one_liner: Learns risk-sensitive sequential Bayesian experimental design policies using a quantile critic over the full campaign information-gain distribution.
T818Qd4Eks.problem: Standard sequential Bayesian optimal experimental design maximizes expected information gain (EIG), ignoring variance and lower-tail risks of uninformative experimental campaigns.
T818Qd4Eks.method: DistBOED models the full distribution of campaign information gain induced by a sequential design policy using a distributional quantile critic paired with a campaign-level actor update. This framework trains policies under risk-sensitive functionals including conditional value at risk (CVaR), variance-penalized mean, and entropic risk measure.
T818Qd4Eks.key_idea: Model the full campaign information-gain distribution with a quantile critic and optimize sequential design policies under tail- and variance-sensitive risk functionals.
T818Qd4Eks.evidence: Evaluated across three sequential experimental design scenarios optimizing CVaR, variance-penalized mean, and entropic risk measure against EIG baselines.
T818Qd4Eks.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that optimizing risk-sensitive functionals of the full information-gain distribution rather than mean EIG alone is well motivated for reliability-critical experimental campaigns.
T818Qd4Eks.main_concern: Reviewers question defining realized information gain via non-negative posterior-prior KL divergence rather than potentially negative entropy reduction, alongside finite design-menu constraints and limited risk-aware baselines.

qvQRTKAL9N.one_liner: Constructs full tree-search paths from any depth in one flow-map evaluation with dynamic exploration-to-refinement step scheduling.
qvQRTKAL9N.problem: Inference-time tree samplers for generative models require excessive function evaluations (NFEs) for node valuation and rely on uniform small transitions that prevent adaptive search.
qvQRTKAL9N.method: Bootstrap Flow-Map-Tree (BFMT) constructs full tree paths from any tree depth using a single flow-map function evaluation to provide lookahead node valuation. It combines this single-NFE estimation with dynamic transition time-step scheduling to shift sampling budget from broad global exploration to fine-grained local refinement of high-utility modes.
qvQRTKAL9N.key_idea: Evaluate terminal tree-path states from any depth in a single flow-map call while dynamically scheduling transition step sizes from global exploration to local refinement.
qvQRTKAL9N.evidence: Theoretical transition-validity and polynomial error-decay guarantees alongside experiments and ablations on high-dimensional image generation and molecular optimization (QED/SA per reviews).
qvQRTKAL9N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value cutting tree-search NFE scaling via single-evaluation node lookahead backed by theoretical convergence guarantees and thorough image-generation experiments.
qvQRTKAL9N.main_concern: Molecular optimization experiments rely on simple QED/SA rewards with missing formulation details and lack non-reward quality metrics to rule out reward over-optimization.

19r4PNX4jz.one_liner: Decouples target-state committed-length prediction from hardware cost calibration to dynamically select the lowest-cost speculative drafter per step.
19r4PNX4jz.problem: Different speculative drafters excel on different text patterns, hardware platforms, and batch sizes, making any single static drafter suboptimal across workloads.
19r4PNX4jz.method: SpecRouter trains a 0.58M-parameter network on exact offline greedy-verification labels from target hidden states to predict how many tokens each drafter will commit at a prefix. Combining predicted committed lengths with a separately calibrated hardware cost model, it runs only the drafter with the lowest predicted cost per committed token.
19r4PNX4jz.key_idea: Predict each drafter's committed tokens from the target model's hidden state and divide calibrated hardware latency by predicted tokens to execute only the cheapest drafter.
19r4PNX4jz.evidence: Evaluated under greedy decoding across 16 workloads (100 held-out requests each) on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B against EAGLE-3, hindsight per-workload fixed drafters, and online drafter routers.
19r4PNX4jz.claimed_gains: Speeds up decoding by 2.75× on Llama-3.1-8B and 2.95× on Qwen3-8B (30% and 27% above EAGLE-3) with a 0.58M-parameter predictor, reaching up to 4.34× against online drafter-selection methods.
19r4PNX4jz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value decoupling exploration-free offline payoff supervision from hardware cost calibration so a lightweight predictor transfers across GPUs and batch sizes.
19r4PNX4jz.main_concern: Both offline label collection and evaluation assume greedy decoding rather than stochastic sampling, and simple prefix-statistic or static-cost ablations achieve nearly identical speedups.

0BsHBcwSje.one_liner: Assigns class-specific diffusion guidance from cluster entropy and feature dispersion for training-free dataset distillation.
0BsHBcwSje.problem: Class-agnostic mode guidance ignores differences in within-class structure and dispersion during training-free diffusion dataset distillation.
0BsHBcwSje.method: CAGS computes class-specific guidance coefficients once from cluster entropy and intra-class feature dispersion, then samples toward cached modes with a frozen generator and fixed classifier-free guidance.
0BsHBcwSje.key_idea: Maps class-wise cluster entropy and intra-class dispersion to mode-guidance coefficients before sampling from a frozen generator.
0BsHBcwSje.evidence: Experiments vary datasets, classifiers, image budgets, and generation seeds, including Stable Diffusion 1.5 and paired fixed-guidance comparisons.
0BsHBcwSje.claimed_gains: Paired final-epoch evaluations over five generation seeds show gains of 2.25, 3.88, and 3.04 percentage points over disabled mode guidance on ConvNet-6, ResNet-18, and ResNetAP-10, respectively.
0BsHBcwSje.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that changing one scalar per class is cheap, simple, training-free, and evaluated broadly with negative results reported.
0BsHBcwSje.main_concern: Reviewers most often argue that inadequately matched fixed-guidance controls and narrow coefficient ranges leave class-adaptive allocation unisolated.

UV98A7Ejiw.one_liner: Interpolates source and target objectives to stabilize adaptation while retaining useful source information.
UV98A7Ejiw.problem: Abruptly replacing source training with a target objective can harm optimization and distort representations that remain useful under distribution shift.
UV98A7Ejiw.method: Loss smoothing linearly interpolates source and target objectives during adaptation and is analyzed through a controlled shared-feature toy study and experiments across four adaptation regimes.
UV98A7Ejiw.key_idea: Linearly interpolates source and target losses during adaptation, then removes source supervision after the objective transition.
UV98A7Ejiw.evidence: Experiments cover pretrained vision and language models, continual supervised learning, overtrained LLM fine-tuning, and offline-to-online reinforcement learning with replay and regularization controls.
UV98A7Ejiw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that one simple recipe receives unusually broad cross-domain evaluation with consistent directional improvements and useful toy analysis.
UV98A7Ejiw.main_concern: Reviewers most often note that the shared-feature mechanism is demonstrated only in the toy study, not shown to drive gains in pretrained models.

hz6k97rh6w.one_liner: Compiles engineer–agent traces into executable, verifier-checked tasks through a shared evidence contract.
hz6k97rh6w.problem: Reusing engineering traces as training tasks requires recovering missing context and unresolved states without changing source objectives.
hz6k97rh6w.method: CARET jointly constructs workspaces, instructions, verifiers, and reference solutions under an evidence contract, then applies bounded revision and fresh-sandbox admission checks.
hz6k97rh6w.key_idea: Links source evidence to workspace facts, unresolved dependencies, and verifier properties before admitting tasks through fresh-sandbox execution checks.
hz6k97rh6w.evidence: The corpus contains 10,139 tasks and 24,187 trajectories, evaluated through SFT and RL at 4B-Instruct, 8B, and 14B scales on three benchmarks.
hz6k97rh6w.claimed_gains: CARET achieves the highest PinchBench and WildClawBench pure-text scores in all six scale–stage comparisons after SFT and subsequent RL.
hz6k97rh6w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the evidence contract and explicit execution gates form a carefully engineered pipeline for preserving requirements and solvability.
hz6k97rh6w.main_concern: Reviewers most often argue that unmatched teachers, data mixtures, and training budgets prevent attributing benchmark gains to task-construction quality.

yHVcEoxOlW.one_liner: Analyzes how preference optimization increases top-score concentration and depletes informative self-rewarding comparisons.
yHVcEoxOlW.problem: Self-rewarding language models can saturate near the rubric's highest score, creating ties and reducing informative preference feedback.
yHVcEoxOlW.method: The paper decomposes preference updates and actor–judge score changes, derives saturation conditions, and relates the sampling budget for informative comparisons to remaining non-top probability.
yHVcEoxOlW.key_idea: Decomposes score evolution into response-distribution and evaluation-behavior changes, isolating a preference-update component that raises top-score probability.
yHVcEoxOlW.evidence: Support includes update-direction theorems, score-decomposition propositions, and experiments using one model, one corpus, and one evaluation benchmark.
yHVcEoxOlW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the actor–judge and allocation decompositions provide coherent distinctions for analyzing score saturation and preference availability.
yHVcEoxOlW.main_concern: Reviewers most often argue that the local theoretical conditions are not empirically validated against realistic training dynamics or practical performance harm.

24jagwDpAK.one_liner: Repeats answer-conditioned attention equilibria between feedforward updates for memory-efficient recurrent reasoning.
24jagwDpAK.problem: Looping entire Transformer blocks wastes computation by repeating expensive feedforward updates whenever attention is refined.
24jagwDpAK.method: The fixed-point reasoner holds values and an answer-conditioned anchor fixed while updating queries and keys to equilibrium, then revises the answer with a feedforward transformation and trains by implicit differentiation.
24jagwDpAK.key_idea: Holds values and an answer-conditioned anchor fixed while iterating queries and keys to equilibrium before each feedforward answer revision.
24jagwDpAK.evidence: Controlled experiments compare parameter- and inference-FLOP-matched recurrence controls with five seeds on algorithmic reasoning tasks and ARC-AGI-1.
24jagwDpAK.claimed_gains: Implicit differentiation yields O(1) training memory and reduces per-iteration compute by 58%–73%.
24jagwDpAK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling attention refinement from feedforward revision is intuitive and supported by carefully matched recurrence controls.
24jagwDpAK.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite contradictory headline results across the abstract, tables, and figures as undermining confidence in the empirical evaluation.

ULyXCdVPZI.one_liner: Compresses linear-attention checkpoints using shared-anchor residuals derived from native recurrent state updates.
ULyXCdVPZI.problem: Retaining recurrent-state checkpoints for prefix reuse creates GPU-memory pressure and expensive recomputation in hybrid linear-attention serving.
ULyXCdVPZI.method: WEAVE combines shared-anchor residuals, recurrence-driven encoding, periodic compaction, and fused GPU kernels within vLLM's native prefix-cache path.
ULyXCdVPZI.key_idea: Encodes checkpoint changes relative to a shared anchor directly from native model updates, then periodically compacts the residuals.
ULyXCdVPZI.evidence: Evaluation uses Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and Kimi-Linear-48B across reasoning, long-context, and agentic workloads on six benchmarks with vLLM integration.
ULyXCdVPZI.claimed_gains: WEAVE achieves up to 4.26× compression, 6.96× lower TTFT, and 3.14× higher SLO-constrained token goodput while maintaining task quality.
ULyXCdVPZI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exploiting native state evolution is practical and well motivated, with useful GPU-kernel and vLLM integration.
ULyXCdVPZI.main_concern: Reviewers most often criticize the absence of existing recurrent-state compression and prefix-cache management baselines beyond basic quantization.

RY1Aa0YJZU.one_liner: Fuses frozen generation and understanding scores for caption discrimination without generating images.
RY1Aa0YJZU.problem: It remains unclear whether image generation supplies useful visual evidence beyond strong understanding-only methods in unified multimodal models.
RY1Aa0YJZU.method: The method scores each observed image conditioned on candidate captions through the generation pathway and calibrates a linear combination with understanding scores while keeping the model frozen.
RY1Aa0YJZU.key_idea: Uses caption-conditioned image likelihood from the generation pathway as auxiliary evidence alongside understanding scores in a calibrated linear combiner.
RY1Aa0YJZU.evidence: Experiments cover six unified models, a cross-model control, five compositional benchmarks, independent replication, null-score replacements, and visual interventions.
RY1Aa0YJZU.claimed_gains: Generation significantly improves 10 of 27 evaluated pairs by 1.2–8.1 percentage points over the strongest understanding-only baseline.
RY1Aa0YJZU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that progressively stronger baselines, matched calibration, null controls, and replication make the evaluation unusually careful.
RY1Aa0YJZU.main_concern: Reviewers most often question the significance of residual gains, which cluster in weaker understanding models and shrink against stronger controls.

xBRHPTmWv3.one_liner: Refines online human reactions with selected causal history during training while keeping bounded-context inference.
xBRHPTmWv3.problem: Relevant interactions can fall outside an online policy's recent window, but enlarging inference context adds redundancy and runtime dependencies.
xBRHPTmWv3.method: SCHA-React compresses selected completed events and fuses them with recent features during flow-matching refinement, then disables the historical pathway for bounded-context motion decoding.
xBRHPTmWv3.key_idea: Retrieves and compresses causally completed historical events for training-time fusion, then disables the historical pathway at deployment.
xBRHPTmWv3.evidence: DuoBox experiments use 2,525 verified annotations, including 1,310 admissible events, across reactive, two-character, and 1,800-frame closed-loop settings.
xBRHPTmWv3.claimed_gains: SCHA-React achieves the lowest reported per-frame, per-transition, and per-clip FIDs among evaluated methods on DuoBox.
xBRHPTmWv3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using history only during refinement preserves a practical online interface and improves several motion-generation evaluations.
xBRHPTmWv3.main_concern: Evaluation is confined to one boxing dataset, with FID gains not matched by uniform physical-statistic improvements.

zJbOCnI1sQ.one_liner: Intrinsically rewards exploration using world-model prediction changes between paired same-world interaction trajectories.
zJbOCnI1sQ.problem: Agents must explore to identify hidden world structure without being distracted by unpredictable observations such as noisy TVs.
zJbOCnI1sQ.method: Double Take trains a next-frame world model on paired rollouts from the same world and simulates an instantaneous second look by replaying observations within a supposed first take.
zJbOCnI1sQ.key_idea: Trains a world model to transfer shared-world structure between paired rollouts, then rewards prediction changes from replayed observations as information gain.
zJbOCnI1sQ.evidence: Experiments in procedurally generated environments compare exploration and information gathering with intrinsic-motivation baselines and oracle performance.
zJbOCnI1sQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the same-world double-take construction is a principled way to distinguish learnable structure from stochastic distractions.
zJbOCnI1sQ.main_concern: Reviewers most often highlight the gap between information-gain theory and the practical estimator, whose approximations and out-of-distribution queries lack guarantees.

Bz94vBlccS.one_liner: Derives reference-mixing thresholds for recovering target distributions under repeated best-of-N distillation.
Bz94vBlccS.problem: Repeated best-of-N retraining can preserve rare errors and drift among correct answers, making long-run distribution recovery uncertain.
Bz94vBlccS.method: The paper analyzes an idealized population model with exact fitting and fixed score distributions, deriving rare-error recovery conditions and matching bounds under reference mixing.
Bz94vBlccS.key_idea: Uses a rare-error multiplier to characterize when verifier-guided selection eliminates incorrect answers despite repeated distributional retraining.
Bz94vBlccS.evidence: The support includes exact necessary-and-sufficient recovery boundaries, convergence rates, matching upper and lower bounds, and explicit nonconvergence constructions.
Bz94vBlccS.claimed_gains: For fixed N, the worst-case reference weight needed for global recovery scales as Θ(δ²), where δ is the largest uniform distance between score distribution functions.
Bz94vBlccS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the mathematical analysis provides an exact recovery boundary and shows why pairwise verifier accuracy alone cannot determine recursive recovery.
Bz94vBlccS.main_concern: Reviewers most often emphasize that exact population fitting and fixed answer-conditioned score distributions leave a substantial gap to practical retraining.

BRD11UvH89.one_liner: Jointly selects exploration goal batches by combining visitation novelty with mutual-information distinguishability in a temporal latent space.
BRD11UvH89.problem: Independent novelty-based goal selection can pick redundant nearby goals in a batch, causing overlapping Go-Explore exploration rollouts.
BRD11UvH89.method: EGGS scores goal batches using visitation-entropy novelty plus a mutual-information term measuring goal distinguishability in a learned temporal representation. Each selected goal then guides a Go-Explore rollout that reaches the goal before continuing exploration.
BRD11UvH89.key_idea: Augments visitation-novelty goal selection with a mutual-information distinguishability term over learned temporal representations to diversify batched Go-Explore rollouts.
BRD11UvH89.evidence: Evaluated on six 2-D environments, AntMaze, locomotion benchmarks, and downstream hierarchical RL and zero-shot goal-reaching tasks.
BRD11UvH89.claimed_gains: In controlled 2-D environments, EGGS achieves the highest mean coverage AUC in all six tasks and the highest mean final normalized visitation entropy in five of six.
BRD11UvH89.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reducing batch goal redundancy is clearly motivated and easy to understand.
BRD11UvH89.main_concern: Reviewers point out inconsistent ablation gains from the mutual-information term on AntMaze Large, mixed downstream goal-reaching results, and limited conceptual novelty over prior Go-Explore methods.

ws9A4dwlOj.one_liner: Shares GPU KV-cache memory across co-located Mixture-of-Models engines via elastic lending and safe targeted page reclamation.
ws9A4dwlOj.problem: Fixed KV-cache partitions strand memory in multi-model workflows, while naive lending cannot reclaim pages from busy upstream engines when downstream demand spikes.
ws9A4dwlOj.method: KVLease pairs per-model allocation guarantees with elastic capacity lending and targeted return across co-located vLLM and SGLang engines. To reclaim borrowed pages safely, selected pages stop accepting new allocations and return once active references and GPU accesses complete, keeping KV contents private.
ws9A4dwlOj.key_idea: Lends idle KV pages across co-located models and reclaims them safely from busy borrowers by halting new allocations until active GPU references drain.
ws9A4dwlOj.evidence: Replicated trace evaluations across heterogeneous GPUs, vLLM and SGLang engines, and diverse Mixture-of-Models workloads.
ws9A4dwlOj.claimed_gains: Across heterogeneous GPUs, serving engines, and MoM workloads, KVLease achieves 28-53% lower end-to-end p95 latency.
ws9A4dwlOj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical vLLM/SGLang integration and the safe targeted-return mechanism for multi-model KV sharing.
ws9A4dwlOj.main_concern: Reviewers note the single-GPU scope (TP=PP=1 with small 7-20B models) and reliance on synthetic or replayed workloads without quality-cost comparisons against a single larger model.

B7VRDmO6CM.one_liner: Wraps LLM data agents in a continuously updated workspace model tracking asset state, action effects, and deliverable constraints.
B7VRDmO6CM.problem: Data agents struggle in large, opaque workspaces where trial-and-error exploration is costly and static semantic layers miss execution dynamics.
B7VRDmO6CM.method: Data World Model (DWM) wraps the agent's function-calling loop with a measured workspace state, an operation model predicting action transformations, and a constraint model verifying deliverable requirements. It monitors tool interactions and updates its state representation continuously.
B7VRDmO6CM.key_idea: Monitors agent tool calls with a continuously updated model of workspace state, predicted operation effects, and deliverable validation constraints.
B7VRDmO6CM.evidence: Experiments across seven data-agent benchmarks and two backbone models, measuring task accuracy and total token usage.
B7VRDmO6CM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses a practical bottleneck in complex data workspaces and shows consistent accuracy and token improvements across seven benchmarks.
B7VRDmO6CM.main_concern: Reviewers feel the "world model" framing overclaims what are largely statistical checks and validation rules, and note missing controlled comparisons against strong harnesses on the same backbone.

si0vOQPaF6.one_liner: Proves tight complexity lower bounds showing fixed-timescale two-time-scale SGDA is suboptimal for nonconvex-PL min-max games.
si0vOQPaF6.problem: It was unknown whether two-timescale stochastic gradient descent ascent (SGDA) could match faster min-max algorithms like Smoothed-AGDA through step-size tuning.
si0vOQPaF6.method: The authors construct worst-case hard instances for simultaneous and alternating two-timescale SGDA with fixed timescale ratios and non-increasing step sizes on smooth nonconvex-PL games. They derive tight matching complexity lower bounds and demonstrate failure modes when the timescale ratio is too small.
si0vOQPaF6.key_idea: Constructs hard nonconvex-PL min-max instances proving matching complexity lower bounds for fixed-ratio SGDA and a separation from Smoothed-AGDA.
si0vOQPaF6.evidence: Theoretical lower and upper bound proofs covering deterministic and stochastic settings for both simultaneous and alternating SGDA.
si0vOQPaF6.claimed_gains: Proves a tight complexity lower bound of Omega(kappa^2 l eps^-2 + kappa^4 l sigma^2 eps^-4) for fixed-ratio non-increasing-stepsize SGDA and shows failure when the timescale ratio is o(kappa^2).
si0vOQPaF6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the tight lower bounds cleanly close a theoretical gap and confirm SGDA's suboptimality relative to Smoothed-AGDA.
si0vOQPaF6.main_concern: Reviewers question the broader significance given faster algorithms already exist, and note proof-strategy overlap with prior work and citation/scope presentation issues.

xWYHwshOj9.one_liner: Benchmarks life-science AI agents on 784 deterministically graded bioinformatics tasks across six omics and protein domains.
xWYHwshOj9.problem: Existing life-science agent benchmarks test only a few tasks per field, failing to evaluate deep capabilities within specific bioinformatics domains.
xWYHwshOj9.method: OmicsBench compiles 784 expert-constructed short- and long-horizon tasks spanning spatial-omics, single-cell transcriptomics, epigenomics, variant interpretation, microbial surveillance, and protein function. Each task pairs a real dataset and prompt with a deterministic grader.
xWYHwshOj9.key_idea: Aggregates 784 deterministically graded short- and long-horizon bioinformatics tasks across six specialized omics and protein-function domains.
xWYHwshOj9.evidence: Evaluates 31 model-harness pairs across all 784 tasks with failure-mode, cost, and refusal analyses.
xWYHwshOj9.claimed_gains: Across 31 model-harness pairs on 784 tasks, no agent scores higher than 50%.
xWYHwshOj9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the comprehensive 31-pair model-harness evaluation and the focus on realistic bioinformatics workflows.
xWYHwshOj9.main_concern: Reviewers note limited originality because tasks come from prior preprints, and question whether deterministic graders unfairly penalize alternative scientifically valid analysis choices.

wJ8HkA8vGN.one_liner: Shows that perturbing deterministic latent reasoning chains raises pass@k without improving majority-vote accuracy.
wJ8HkA8vGN.problem: Latent-reasoning models follow deterministic hidden-state trajectories, and recent work perturbs these chains at test time assuming the resulting answer diversity reflects genuine exploration.
wJ8HkA8vGN.method: The authors compare latent-chain perturbation methods (MC-dropout and additive Gaussian noise) against explicit chain-of-thought sampling on a shared backbone, alongside post-reasoning perturbation ablations. They also provide a formal analysis contrasting stochastic trajectory marginalization with uninformed state perturbations.
wJ8HkA8vGN.key_idea: Compares latent-chain perturbations against explicit CoT sampling on a shared backbone and proves perturbed deterministic states carry no model belief for majority voting.
wJ8HkA8vGN.evidence: Supported by formal propositions and empirical comparisons across multiple models, including post-reasoning perturbation and confidence/entropy ablations.
wJ8HkA8vGN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper identifies an important, counterintuitive phenomenon—that latent-chain perturbations raise pass@k without majority-vote gains—and presents it clearly.
wJ8HkA8vGN.main_concern: Reviewers question the theoretical analysis (noting propositions only cover noise, not MC-dropout), use of dated models, and whether the effect stems from limited model capability.

Y4GjO4J3NZ.one_liner: Trains a shared RL skill curator conditioned on online executor behavioral profiles to adapt across heterogeneous agents.
Y4GjO4J3NZ.problem: Learned agent skill curators suffer cross-executor degradation when paired with executors different from the one they were trained with.
Y4GjO4J3NZ.method: EASE maintains an online behavioral profile summarizing an executor's recent execution patterns and conditions a shared curator on this profile, the trajectory, and retrieved skills to add, modify, or delete skills. The curator is trained jointly across multiple frozen executors via reinforcement learning with retrieval-aware and behavior-aware temporal attribution.
Y4GjO4J3NZ.key_idea: Conditions a shared RL-trained skill curator on an online behavioral profile of the downstream executor and optimizes it with behavior-aware temporal attribution.
Y4GjO4J3NZ.evidence: Evaluated on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, and WebShop across seen and unseen heterogeneous executor families, with ablations on behavioral profiling and deployment cost.
Y4GjO4J3NZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that building a shared, behavior-adaptive skill curator that transfers across executors is an important problem backed by solid experiments and ablations.
Y4GjO4J3NZ.main_concern: Reviewers note that the benefit of multi-executor training is not isolated from behavioral conditioning, and question the need for a separate trained curator over self-curating executors or plain-text optimizers.

KzVeHIzvVq.one_liner: Introduces 45 synthetic multi-region neural datasets and metrics to benchmark inter-regional communication models.
KzVeHIzvVq.problem: Models inferring unobserved inter-regional neural communication lack standardized benchmarks and are validated on fragmented, custom synthetic testbeds.
KzVeHIzvVq.method: The authors construct IRCB '26, a benchmark of 45 synthetic multi-region neural population datasets generated with ground-truth communication, paired with evaluation metrics separating activity reconstruction, effectome recovery, and communication fidelity/specificity.
KzVeHIzvVq.key_idea: Provides 45 synthetic multi-region neural datasets with ground-truth connectivity and decoupled metrics for reconstruction, effectome recovery, and communication fidelity.
KzVeHIzvVq.evidence: The benchmark is demonstrated on two communication models (MR-LFADS and RRR) to surface failure modes across task conditions.
KzVeHIzvVq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper addresses a genuine gap in computational neuroscience, is well written, and thoughtfully separates reconstruction from communication metrics.
KzVeHIzvVq.main_concern: Reviewers note that using continuous-time vanilla RNNs with modularized region roles may bias the benchmark against switching or GP models, and only two baselines are evaluated.

zHKkrJTPKu.one_liner: Replaces bounded fuzzy logic operators in differentiable inductive logic programming with unbound real-valued non-selective operators.
zHKkrJTPKu.problem: Existing differentiable inductive logic programming methods relax forward chaining using bounded truth values and selective fuzzy operators, causing vanishing or imbalanced gradients.
zHKkrJTPKu.method: The authors propose unbound logic (LuHorn/DiffLu), relaxing truth values to unbound real numbers and splitting rule applicability (a min gate) from additive value propagation so backward gradients remain non-selective and non-vanishing. They also combine the differentiable logic module with neural perception for end-to-end visual ILP.
zHKkrJTPKu.key_idea: Relaxes truth values to unbound reals and decouples rule applicability gating from additive payload propagation to keep backward gradients non-selective.
zHKkrJTPKu.evidence: Supported by theoretical soundness proofs for real-valued forward chaining and experiments on inductive logic programming and visual ILP tasks.
zHKkrJTPKu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the decomposition into a min gate and additive payload is mathematically clean and recovers classical forward-chaining semantics.
zHKkrJTPKu.main_concern: Reviewers point out that no operator-swap ablation or gradient measurement isolates the claimed trainability benefit from the larger hypothesis space (many-body-atom rules).

01f2FYocEa.one_liner: Maintains instruction-conditioned typed interaction state with frozen perceptual tools and retrieves it selectively for generalist robot policies.
01f2FYocEa.problem: Visual-memory robot systems compress raw frames rather than tracking interaction-derived state like persistent entity relations, progress, or routes.
01f2FYocEa.method: SimpleARM uses the task instruction to specify what to monitor, updates compact typed state online via frozen perceptual tools, retrieves state only when a subgoal depends on history, and grounds recalled entities in the current view for frozen generalist robot policies.
01f2FYocEa.key_idea: Tracking instruction-specified typed interaction state with frozen perceptual tools and retrieving it only for history-dependent subgoals enables training-free robot memory.
01f2FYocEa.evidence: Evaluates across all 16 tasks of RoboMME over three policy seeds, plus matched component-removal ablations.
01f2FYocEa.claimed_gains: Achieves 67.17% mean success across 16 RoboMME tasks vs. 44.51% for the strongest non-oracle baseline.
01f2FYocEa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing robot memory as maintaining and selectively retrieving typed interaction state is well-supported by targeted component ablations.
01f2FYocEa.main_concern: Reviewers criticize heavy reliance on RoboMME-specific lexical rules and calibrated parsers, large drops under instruction paraphrasing, and baselines lacking the same frozen perception stack.

SfOVAitWjL.one_liner: Curates a 10B-token timestamped temporal text stream (2010-2022) to benchmark language models as prequential stream compressors.
SfOVAitWjL.problem: Prequential coding motivates language modeling on single documents, but continual compression across temporal document streams remains understudied.
SfOVAitWjL.method: The authors build a verifiably timestamped 10B-token temporal stream spanning 2010-2022 (including document revisions) and evaluate standard LM pretraining, long-context models, and exact-match prefix retrieval by bits per byte.
SfOVAitWjL.key_idea: Evaluates language models as online prequential compressors over a chronologically ordered, revision-aware 10B-token text stream.
SfOVAitWjL.evidence: Empirical compression measurements on the curated 10B-token stream across context lengths and retrieval interventions.
SfOVAitWjL.claimed_gains: Long-context models reach 0.69 bits per byte (BPB) compared to 0.49 BPB for exact-match prefix retrieval and an estimated 0.43 BPB achievable rate.
SfOVAitWjL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the carefully timestamped temporal corpus construction and clear quantification of long-range memory headroom.
SfOVAitWjL.main_concern: Reviewers note hard-to-read writing, unclear connection to continual learning experiments, and a headline time-order gain confounded by diff formatting.

jRtbLHcLrO.one_liner: Iteratively re-encodes intermediate synthesized circuits as new decoder conditioning in a population-based inference search.
jRtbLHcLrO.problem: Existing token-level search for generative logic synthesis runs from a single fixed input encoding and lags classical optimizers on hard sub-circuits.
jRtbLHcLrO.method: ReCoDe wraps an encoder-decoder circuit synthesizer in an iterative population search that re-encodes intermediate decoded circuits as fresh conditioning inputs to explore structurally distinct representations.
jRtbLHcLrO.key_idea: Re-encodes a model's own functionally equivalent intermediate circuits as new conditioning inputs across a parallel search population.
jRtbLHcLrO.evidence: Evaluations on several thousand IWLS fanout-free windows at K=8, 10, and 12 inputs using CT and GTAC backbones under exact equivalence and error constraints.
jRtbLHcLrO.claimed_gains: Under exact equivalence, ReCoDe reduces the size of the hardest windows by 18–22% relative to a single decode and outperforms token-level search at the same decode budget in 3 to 10x less time.
jRtbLHcLrO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree ReCoDe is a simple, training-free inference-time method that works across window sizes and two circuit synthesizer backbones.
jRtbLHcLrO.main_concern: Reviewers note that matched-budget comparisons against MCTS-1000 use very small subsets, fixed-conditioning best-of-N baselines are missing, and retraining details for K=10 and K=12 are underspecified.

nUWhOVFbTu.one_liner: Couples token-wise likelihood suppression with knowledge distillation from a frozen pretrained teacher for federated LLM unlearning.
nUWhOVFbTu.problem: Federated LLM unlearning suffers from limited local retain data in single-client requests and inconsistent forgetting directions across heterogeneous multi-client forget sets.
nUWhOVFbTu.method: FedCoDS multiplies token-wise likelihood suppression on forget tokens with knowledge distillation toward a shared frozen pretrained base model and adds a retain-side KL regularizer.
nUWhOVFbTu.key_idea: Couples token-wise likelihood suppression with knowledge distillation from a shared frozen pretrained model to align cross-client updates and constrain drift.
nUWhOVFbTu.evidence: Experiments on TOFU and MUSE benchmarks using 1B and 7B models under single-client and multi-client federated unlearning settings.
nUWhOVFbTu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the distinction between single-client and multi-client federated unlearning and note consistent retention and forgetting metrics on TOFU and MUSE.
nUWhOVFbTu.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the multiplicative coupling is justified over additive combinations or baselines equipped with the same retain-side KL regularization.

p0QruD1HwN.one_liner: Links hallucinated out-of-candidate entities in SFT targets to runaway repetition and steers list closing via activation pulses.
p0QruD1HwN.problem: Training on structured-extraction targets containing out-of-candidate entities induces runaway repetition by suppressing list-closing behavior.
p0QruD1HwN.method: The authors isolate out-of-candidate targets via length-matched block replacement in long-document relation extraction and apply a single activation pulse along the cleaned-minus-raw direction at stopping points.
p0QruD1HwN.key_idea: Diagnose supervision-induced stopping failures via length-matched block replacement and restore list-closing behavior with an activation-space steering pulse.
p0QruD1HwN.evidence: Experiments evaluate Qwen3 models (1.7B, 4B, 8B) on Chinese long-document relation extraction with block-replacement and random-direction controls.
p0QruD1HwN.claimed_gains: Across Qwen3 1.7B, 4B, and 8B, removing hallucinated targets reduces continuous pattern repetition by 24.65-34.63 percentage points; replacing 15% of cleaned blocks raises 4B repetition from 5.52% to 9.71%; and an activation pulse reduces raw 4B repetition by 10.94 percentage points at natural stopping points.
p0QruD1HwN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the length-matched block-replacement control that isolates content defects from target-length confounds.
p0QruD1HwN.main_concern: Reviewers cite narrow scope (one Chinese relation-extraction task and one model family) and wide confidence intervals showing unreliable content retention under steering.

0olLNq4Hkm.one_liner: Splits NER datasets using integer linear programming to minimize entity and context leakage under class-balance constraints.
0olLNq4Hkm.problem: Native NER splits leak entities and surrounding contexts between train and test sets, while naive leakage-removal splits unbalance entity classes.
0olLNq4Hkm.method: EMPIRE formulates NER dataset partitioning as an integer linear program minimizing weighted entity and context leakage while fixing split sizes and bounding per-class shares.
0olLNq4Hkm.key_idea: Solve an integer linear program balancing entity-overlap and context-similarity penalties subject to split-size and per-class balance constraints.
0olLNq4Hkm.evidence: Experiments span 24 NER datasets evaluating BiLSTM-CRF and fine-tuned Llama-2-7B models.
0olLNq4Hkm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the useful insight that class-support imbalances confound leakage-reduced NER evaluations across 24 datasets.
0olLNq4Hkm.main_concern: Reviewers point out that DataSAIL already combines similarity-aware ILP splitting with multi-label stratification, undermining the paper's stated novelty and baseline omission.

x6pGCtvHa1.one_liner: Reweights mid-training tokens using an RL-tuned model's priors to improve both base and subsequent post-trained LLMs.
x6pGCtvHa1.problem: Standard LLM pipelines are unidirectional from pretraining to post-training, while using RL models for knowledge distillation during mid-training causes teacher overfitting that fades after post-training.
x6pGCtvHa1.method: ReMiT uses an existing RL-tuned checkpoint to compute bounded dynamic token weights during the late-pretraining mid-training phase, prioritizing reasoning-relevant tokens in the next-token prediction loss without training a separate teacher.
x6pGCtvHa1.key_idea: Applies bounded token reweighting from an RL-tuned checkpoint to the mid-training next-token loss to transfer reasoning priors back into the base model.
x6pGCtvHa1.evidence: Evaluated on 1B, 2B, and 3B models (including OLMo-1B, Youtu-LLM-2B, SmolLM3) through full SFT, DPO, and RLVR post-training pipelines.
x6pGCtvHa1.claimed_gains: Empirically achieves an average improvement of 3%.
x6pGCtvHa1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the bounded token-reweighting mechanism simple, practical, and effective at improving post-training outcomes compared to knowledge distillation.
x6pGCtvHa1.main_concern: Reviewers flag potential data leakage from using an OLMo RL checkpoint already trained on the downstream post-training datasets, alongside mismatched RHO-1 reference baselines and limited iterative rounds.

2qVCj3Jfhx.one_liner: Audits AI research agent claims via sealed outcome validation, matched recovery challenges, and feedback-attribution gates.
2qVCj3Jfhx.problem: Reported final artifact scores do not distinguish genuine discovery from prior knowledge, extra sampling, or unauthorized experimental feedback.
2qVCj3Jfhx.method: The Discovery Certification Protocol (DCP) enforces a three-gate audit under a registered model, information boundary, and budget: Gate 1 checks improvement, Gate 2 tests zero-recovery bounds by matched challengers without run history, and optional Gate 3 compares truthful versus neutral feedback from a shared checkpoint, verified deterministically from frozen records.
2qVCj3Jfhx.key_idea: Audits research agent claims via sealed outcome validation, matched-budget challenger recovery bounds, and truthful-versus-neutral feedback continuation tests.
2qVCj3Jfhx.evidence: Evaluated on controlled SQLite and virtual catalyst audits plus Yacht and Ionosphere response-surface tasks with 96 recovery attempts and 30 continuation trials.
2qVCj3Jfhx.claimed_gains: Yacht and Ionosphere pass the Core kernel with 0/96 recoveries (upper bound 0.0468), Yacht scores 0.7677 on 32 switch-effect reconstructions with 0.0315 MAE, and truthful continuations recover targets in 9/30 and 16/30 trials.
2qVCj3Jfhx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the protocol asks an important evaluation question and cleanly separates achieved outcomes from process repeatability and resource accounting.
2qVCj3Jfhx.main_concern: Reviewers argue the 45 file-copy positive controls do not prove challenger adequacy, leaving recovery bounds weak and real-data tasks dominated by measurement access.

qE6KJK7UJL.one_liner: Unifies hard-clipped and soft-compressed robust optimal transport via penalized path weights with exact outlier-recovery guarantees.
qE6KJK7UJL.problem: Robust optimal transport methods produce outlier flags, but lack finite-sample guarantees that those flags exactly recover contaminated observations.
qE6KJK7UJL.method: PW-ROT assigns each transport path a weight w in [0,1] with a linear penalty on 1-w, reducing in closed form to OT under a bounded cost family parameterized by threshold lambda and power r (recovering ROBOT at r=1 and smooth soft compression for r>1). The authors prove estimation error bounds, consistency, and high-probability exact outlier recovery under separation.
qE6KJK7UJL.key_idea: Penalizes transport-path weights linearly to derive a power-indexed bounded ground-cost family bridging hard clipping and soft compression with exact outlier-recovery bounds.
qE6KJK7UJL.evidence: Theoretical proofs of error bounds, consistency, and exact outlier recovery, plus numerical experiments.
qE6KJK7UJL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the unified formulation connecting ROBOT to soft compression and the finite-sample exact outlier recovery guarantees.
qE6KJK7UJL.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty beyond classical half-quadratic/M-estimation and ROBOT, note restrictive Gaussian/separation assumptions, and cite unclear presentation.

Mexg9Kpoyx.one_liner: Co-evolves a latent reward model with a video diffusion generator using real-video anchors to prevent distributional escape.
Mexg9Kpoyx.problem: Optimizing video diffusion models against a fixed latent reward model causes distributional escape and reward hacking, degrading perceptual and motion quality.
Mexg9Kpoyx.method: CoRe treats latent-space alignment as a dynamic game, continually refitting the latent reward model on the generator's current samples while anchoring it to real-video preferences so the generator cannot exploit out-of-support reward regions.
Mexg9Kpoyx.key_idea: Continually refits the latent reward model on current generator outputs while anchoring it to real-video preferences to block distributional escape.
Mexg9Kpoyx.evidence: Evaluated on Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B against the pretrained model, fixed-reward optimization, and prior alignment baselines.
Mexg9Kpoyx.claimed_gains: Consistently improves generation quality over the pretrained model and prior alignment methods while avoiding quality collapse (exact numbers not stated in abstract).
Mexg9Kpoyx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the empirical diagnosis of latent reward hacking and the intuitive idea of co-evolving the reward model online.
Mexg9Kpoyx.main_concern: Reviewers note insufficient distinction from prior adversarial preference optimization (APO), missing fixed-RM controls with identical regularization, and small (<1 point) VBench gains on one 1.3B model.

jwMCEmPmgj.one_liner: Characterizes when selection-biased models can be debiased from recorded source provenance alone and derives minimax recovery rates.
jwMCEmPmgj.problem: When models trained on selection-biased data are reused without access to their training sets, it is unclear when the unbiased population rate can be recovered.
jwMCEmPmgj.method: The paper establishes necessary and sufficient graph/matrix conditions on shared training sources for consistent population-rate recovery, derives minimax MSE rates, extends the test to cross-task acquisition, and provides a source-record screening criterion.
jwMCEmPmgj.key_idea: Uses source-sharing provenance records to give exact if-and-only-if identifiability conditions and minimax bounds for debiasing reused models without raw data.
jwMCEmPmgj.evidence: Supported by minimax theorems and proof-of-concept experiments with controlled selection bias on HelpSteer3.
jwMCEmPmgj.claimed_gains: Minimax mean squared error scales as Theta(m^-1) for recoverable source-sharing patterns, while remaining bounded away from zero otherwise.
jwMCEmPmgj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the rigorous necessary-and-sufficient theoretical characterization of selection-bias recoverability from source provenance.
jwMCEmPmgj.main_concern: Empirical validation is thin—limited to a small-sample HelpSteer3 study without selection-bias baselines—and heavy undefined terminology makes the presentation hard to follow.

eIqQo4Yldw.one_liner: Introduces the SoccerCanon broadcast recognition benchmark and stitches face, appearance, and jersey-number experts via query-specific reliability.
eIqQo4Yldw.problem: Broadcast soccer player recognition suffers from blur, occlusion, and small faces where single cues and general VLMs fail.
eIqQo4Yldw.method: The authors build SoccerCanon by adding canonical identity annotations to SoccerNet-v3 frames and propose a training-free stitching framework that weights face, appearance, and jersey-number vision experts using query-specific reliability and conflict discounting.
eIqQo4Yldw.key_idea: Combines specialized face, appearance, and number vision experts in a training-free framework weighted by per-query cue reliability.
eIqQo4Yldw.evidence: Evaluated specialized vision models and VLMs on SoccerCanon (1,108 player instances: 613 validation, 495 test across 424 identities and 213 matches).
eIqQo4Yldw.claimed_gains: Face recognizers drop from about 96% R@1 on clean photos to 40-47% on SoccerCanon, while expert stitching reaches 60.94% R@1.
eIqQo4Yldw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree SoccerCanon captures a challenging, realistic multi-cue recognition setting where face recognizers degrade sharply.
eIqQo4Yldw.main_concern: Ablations show limited benefit from reliability weighting over fixed weights, excluding match-lineup metadata is questioned, and renaming a small subset of SoccerNet raises attribution concerns.

dhUXnwxGDe.one_liner: Decomposes natural-language multi-robot requirements into assume-guarantee contracts in a formal verification and repair loop.
dhUXnwxGDe.problem: LLM-based multi-robot planners lack rigorous verification layers to guarantee that decomposed contracts compose and remain realizable at scale.
dhUXnwxGDe.method: An LLM Translator converts natural language into LTL specifications and a Decomposer generates system and component assume-guarantee contracts, iteratively repaired using traceable failure witnesses from a formal verification and GR(1) reactive synthesis layer.
dhUXnwxGDe.key_idea: Couples an LLM contract decomposer with formal refinement, realizability, and GR(1) synthesis checks that return traceable witnesses for iterative repair.
dhUXnwxGDe.evidence: Evaluated on three multi-robot shared-resource coordination scenarios and scalability tests.
dhUXnwxGDe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree integrating formal verification witnesses into LLM contract decomposition is a sound neurosymbolic design.
dhUXnwxGDe.main_concern: Evaluation is limited to three simple, symmetric mutual-exclusion scenarios without external planner baselines, and NL-to-LTL translation itself remains unverified.

AmcaiNI92S.one_liner: Weighting coordinate digits by decimal place value creates targeted and untargeted adversarial attacks against GUI grounding models.
AmcaiNI92S.problem: Bounded screenshot perturbations can move generated GUI coordinates away from intended controls, causing agents to execute unintended clicks.
AmcaiNI92S.method: MissClick-U reconstructs soft clicks from digit probabilities and place values to maximize coordinate displacement. MissClick-T minimizes target-answer cross-entropy over the full coordinate sequence with decimal place-value weighting.
AmcaiNI92S.key_idea: Coordinate-generation losses account for each digit's numerical place value, aligning token-level optimization with physical click displacement or redirection.
AmcaiNI92S.evidence: Experiments evaluate OS-Atlas and UGround across three GUI platforms with attack baselines, objective ablations, perturbation budgets, transferability, and preprocessing tests.
AmcaiNI92S.claimed_gains: MissClick-U improves ASR by 16.62 and 30.72 percentage points, while MissClick-T raises targeted ASR from 13.13% to 52.15% on OS-Atlas and from 15.61% to 67.79% on UGround.
AmcaiNI92S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that targeting executed click geometry rather than ordinary text tokens is relevant and that targeted attack gains are substantial.
AmcaiNI92S.main_concern: Two reviewers argue that decimal place-value weighting and numerical token losses closely follow prior work, limiting the attack's methodological novelty.

ZO4otoIWPJ.one_liner: Re-extracting frozen neural MOCO solution pools by greedy hypervolume selection reveals extractor-conditioned finite-set rankings.
ZO4otoIWPJ.problem: Official neural multi-objective combinatorial-optimization tables mix preference-wise scalarized extraction with set-level hypervolume evaluation.
ZO4otoIWPJ.method: PAS applies zero-search greedy hypervolume subset selection to each constructor's full frozen decoded pool. U2N then adds restricted post-hoc Pareto local refinement, and the authors recommend parallel official and PAS reporting.
ZO4otoIWPJ.key_idea: Separating preference-to-solution evaluation from set-level extraction shows that hypervolume rankings depend on how finite Pareto archives are selected.
ZO4otoIWPJ.evidence: The audit re-scores frozen pools from five open-source constructors across four problem families and 56 finite-K settings without additional neural passes or local search for PAS.
ZO4otoIWPJ.claimed_gains: PAS strictly exceeds official scalarized extraction on 53 of 56 finite-K settings.
ZO4otoIWPJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing preference-wise quality from set attainment is meaningful and that frozen official pools make the audit reproducible.
ZO4otoIWPJ.main_concern: Reviewers consistently note that PAS gains follow from selecting a superset by hypervolume and that reported rank reversals are tiny or statistically inconclusive.

9n2epdSB7R.one_liner: Mapping point clouds, RGB-D, and unposed RGB into semantic 3D instances enables shared training-free visual grounding.
9n2epdSB7R.problem: Existing 3D visual-grounding systems bind scene representations and reasoning to particular input modalities, restricting use across sensing conditions.
9n2epdSB7R.method: OMG builds a Modality-Unified Scene Interface of semantic 3D instances linked to local evidence. Query-Conditioned Spatial Abstraction represents relevant relations, while Adaptive Evidence Verification selectively checks visual and geometric cues for ambiguous candidates.
9n2epdSB7R.key_idea: A common semantic-instance interface decouples modality-specific perception from one shared spatial-reasoning and evidence-verification procedure.
9n2epdSB7R.evidence: Experiments on ScanRefer and Nr3D cover point-cloud, posed RGB-D, and unposed multi-view RGB inputs with component and perception-pipeline comparisons.
9n2epdSB7R.claimed_gains: On ScanRefer, OMG achieves Acc0.25/0.5 of 51.3/46.2%, 53.1/47.8%, and 35.64/18.24% for point-cloud, RGB-D, and unposed RGB inputs, respectively, and 50.2% Top-1 on Nr3D.
9n2epdSB7R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating a shared spatial interface from local modality-specific evidence is practical and clearly specified.
