9n2epdSB7R.main_concern: Two reviewers argue that cross-modality gains are confounded by different upstream reconstruction, proposal, and backbone choices rather than isolated grounding improvements.

R0Pleqp0lW.one_liner: Models agentic token budgets as state in stochastic Petri nets to derive capacity curves and an exact budget-aware allocation policy.
R0Pleqp0lW.problem: Agent benchmarks score task accuracy while ignoring token budgets, masking ranking reversals and exhaustion failures under deployment allowances.
R0Pleqp0lW.method: The authors represent agent workflows as budget-augmented stochastic Petri nets with state (M, b), disabling unaffordable transitions to compute reliability capacity curves B*(epsilon) and solving for the optimal budget-aware policy in one backward pass over the acyclic state space.
R0Pleqp0lW.key_idea: Augments stochastic Petri net workflow states with remaining token budget so unaffordable transitions disable and optimal allocation reduces to one backward pass.
R0Pleqp0lW.evidence: Theoretical analysis of capacity curves and ranking inversions plus offline replay on 8,190 published agent trajectories (primarily AppWorld).
R0Pleqp0lW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling mission-level token budgets and capacity curves is a practical and valuable complement to unconstrained accuracy benchmarks.
R0Pleqp0lW.main_concern: Empirical validation only truncates logged trajectories from budget-unaware agents on a single benchmark rather than running live budget-aware allocation policies.

BvgYiIvQpY.one_liner: VeTo filters LLM reasoning paths by combining macro-level verbalized confidence with micro-level token-confidence jitter across confidence regimes.
BvgYiIvQpY.problem: Test-time selection methods uniformly favor stable or high-confidence reasoning paths, ignoring that unstable paths can be correct when the model is uncertain.
BvgYiIvQpY.method: Verbalized-Token Synergistic Filter (VeTo) analyzes how token stability relates to correctness across confidence levels and uses verbalized confidence to decide whether to favor low- or high-jitter reasoning paths when selecting among sampled trajectories.
BvgYiIvQpY.key_idea: Conditions token-confidence jitter filtering on macro-level verbalized confidence, favoring stability when confident and preserving high-jitter paths when uncertain.
BvgYiIvQpY.evidence: Evaluated across eight math, multidisciplinary, code, and multimodal benchmarks on Qwen, Llama, and InternLM with budgets N=4 to 64, plus misleading-prefix analyses and ablations.
BvgYiIvQpY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the finding that stable paths can be wrong while unstable paths can be right, as well as the broad multi-family and multi-budget evaluation.
BvgYiIvQpY.main_concern: The method is heuristic and sensitive to unexplained per-family hyperparameters (jitter window size), requires token probabilities plus self-evaluation overhead, and shows small gains in the low-confidence regime.

rdv0N1hTNQ.one_liner: Audits LLM alignment datasets training-free via one-shot in-context log-likelihood shifts aggregated on a directed k-NN influence graph.
rdv0N1hTNQ.problem: Preference and instruction-tuning datasets accumulate label noise and contradictions that deduplication misses, while exact Data Shapley or full LLM judging is too costly.
rdv0N1hTNQ.method: The pipeline computes one-shot conditional log-likelihood shifts between semantically similar records in O(k) forward passes per record, aggregates outgoing influence, incoming influence, and topological uniqueness over a directed k-NN graph, and routes only tail records with contrasting neighbors to an LLM judge.
rdv0N1hTNQ.key_idea: Approximates in-context Data Shapley using O(k) one-shot log-likelihood shifts on a directed k-NN graph to route only extreme-tail records to an LLM judge.
rdv0N1hTNQ.evidence: Evaluated intrinsically on error detection and extrinsically on alignment fine-tuning across two benchmarks (including HelpSteer2) with multi-provider LLM arbitrator checks.
rdv0N1hTNQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the training-free k-NN in-context influence audit practical and note that distinguishing incoming contradiction from outgoing demonstration quality is useful.
rdv0N1hTNQ.main_concern: Error confirmation relies solely on LLM arbitrators with low inter-model agreement (60–68% pairwise) and no human re-annotation, and multi-seed downstream alignment gains are negligible.

nndExuEEk7.one_liner: Jointly clusters image-text pairs in dual correlation and geometric spaces and refines text prototypes with an LLM for multimodal dataset distillation.
nndExuEEk7.problem: Existing prototype-guided multimodal dataset distillation methods construct visual and textual prototypes separately, failing to preserve joint image-text correspondence.
nndExuEEk7.method: UPSyn projects paired image-text representations into two cross-modal common spaces capturing correlation (via RCCA) and geometry (via WP), then performs consensus clustering across both spaces to discover joint prototypes. An LLM subsequently aggregates and summarizes entities around each textual prototype to guide distilled image-text synthesis.
nndExuEEk7.key_idea: Discovers multimodal prototypes by consensus clustering across dual correlation and geometric cross-modal spaces, followed by LLM-based textual prototype summarization.
nndExuEEk7.evidence: Evaluated on Flickr30K and MS-COCO against coreset, pixel-optimization, and generative multimodal dataset distillation baselines with ablations.
nndExuEEk7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling joint image-text correspondence rather than clustering modalities independently is well motivated and yields consistent empirical improvements.
nndExuEEk7.main_concern: Reviewers note insufficient theoretical justification for combining both RCCA and WP dual spaces, missing comparisons to optimization-based MDM, and unclear necessity of the LLM refinement module.

TmxI5HlbMw.one_liner: Maintains a decomposed foreground-background 3D Gaussian recurrent world state shared between 4D occupancy forecasting and end-to-end driving planning.
TmxI5HlbMw.problem: Existing driving world models rely on dense grids or latent states that obscure explicit 3D geometry and weaken the connection between future scene evolution and trajectory planning.
TmxI5HlbMw.method: HGWM represents the world state as semantic 3D Gaussians split into static background and actor-centric foreground fields with hierarchical geometry-aware communication and sparse local refinement. A residual transition operator with sparse expert routing autoregressively evolves Gaussian attributes, and the same evolving Gaussian state is rendered to 4D semantic occupancy and queried directly for multi-modal ego trajectory planning.
TmxI5HlbMw.key_idea: Evolves foreground and background semantic 3D Gaussians via a residual transition operator with sparse expert routing and shares that explicit geometric state for both occupancy rendering and trajectory planning.
TmxI5HlbMw.evidence: Evaluated on camera-only nuScenes and two additional autonomous driving benchmarks (including NAVSIM and closed-loop driving) with component ablations.
TmxI5HlbMw.claimed_gains: Under the reported camera-only nuScenes protocol, HGWM achieves 25.49% semantic mIoU and 49.86% binary IoU at 3s.
TmxI5HlbMw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling foreground and background 3D Gaussians is reasonable and that the experiments cover multiple driving benchmarks.
TmxI5HlbMw.main_concern: Reviewers point out that ablations do not isolate the causal benefit of sharing the Gaussian state for planning from added modules, and note limited novelty relative to recent Gaussian world models.

Tr9BRSMMZk.one_liner: Combines gradient sketching, fast KNN coverage selection, and a distilled multi-head classifier for scalable multi-benchmark LLM data filtering.
Tr9BRSMMZk.problem: Heuristic LLM data filters cannot target specific downstream benchmarks, while prior gradient-based selection methods are too expensive to scale to modern pretraining corpora.
Tr9BRSMMZk.method: Benchmax defines coverage-based gradient selection criteria using gradient sketching and fast KNN search to identify diverse samples that benefit target benchmarks. It then distills these selection criteria into a lightweight multi-head classifier that simultaneously scores each sample's impact across many benchmarks at trillion-token scale.
Tr9BRSMMZk.key_idea: Distills gradient-sketching and KNN coverage selection criteria into a multi-head classifier to score pretraining data across multiple target benchmarks at low cost.
Tr9BRSMMZk.evidence: Evaluated via mid-training experiments and compute/storage cost analyses comparing Benchmax against HQ DCLM and fastText filters.
Tr9BRSMMZk.claimed_gains: Scores 1 trillion tokens for approximately $500 in cloud costs.
Tr9BRSMMZk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper is easy to follow and presents a practical, scalable pipeline for benchmark-targeted gradient-based data filtering.
Tr9BRSMMZk.main_concern: Reviewers find the empirical gains unconvincing (noting headline gains rely on a synthetic metric while an MMLU-only filter matches or beats Benchmax on accuracy) and cite missing strong target-aware baselines like LESS and MATES.

wRak3yNj2F.one_liner: Analyzes homomorphic encryption error propagation through Transformers to allocate operation-wise CKKS scales and modulus levels, reducing bootstrapping.
wRak3yNj2F.problem: Using uniform conservative precision and scaling factors across all operations in CKKS homomorphic encryption wastes ciphertext modulus and triggers frequent, costly bootstrapping during Transformer inference.
wRak3yNj2F.method: The authors model local numerical errors from individual homomorphic operations and analyze how they propagate to the final Transformer output error. Using this sensitivity analysis, they formulate an optimization problem to assign operation-wise scaling factors and modulus levels so more operations fit within a modulus chain while meeting a target accuracy.
wRak3yNj2F.key_idea: Quantifies each homomorphic operation's propagated contribution to final Transformer output error and solves for operation-wise CKKS scales and modulus allocations.
wRak3yNj2F.evidence: Evaluated on standard and HE-friendly Transformer settings (BERT-based classification on MRPC) compared against THOR, reporting modulus consumption, bootstrapping counts, and accuracy.
wRak3yNj2F.claimed_gains: Compared with THOR, reduces modulus consumption by 30.0% and the number of bootstrapping operations by 83.6% for the standard Transformer.
wRak3yNj2F.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that allocating CKKS precision by downstream error sensitivity targets a real bootstrapping bottleneck in encrypted Transformer inference.
wRak3yNj2F.main_concern: Reviewers note gaps in validating the propagated-error estimator, discretization issues when rounding continuous scales to powers of two, and limited evaluation (BERT on MRPC rather than LLMs) missing recent HE-LLM baselines.

sUj5VKmh2a.one_liner: Generates model-conditioned coding benchmarks with controllable API knowledge components to diagnose unfamiliar API learning failures.
sUj5VKmh2a.problem: Standard code-generation evaluations report failed solutions without distinguishing whether a model lacks API knowledge, receives poor knowledge delivery, or fails to apply supplied knowledge.
sUj5VKmh2a.method: The authors build NovelAPIBench, an automated diagnostic pipeline that identifies APIs unfamiliar to a target model, generates executable coding tasks with separately controllable knowledge components (such as signatures and usage examples), and classifies failures into six categories. They evaluate direct supply, retrieval from an API pool, and fine-tuning across 21 libraries and six backbone models.
sUj5VKmh2a.key_idea: Construct model-conditioned executable coding tasks with modular API knowledge components and a six-category failure taxonomy to separate knowledge content, delivery, and application.
sUj5VKmh2a.evidence: Primary benchmark of 1,670 tasks covering 856 APIs across 21 libraries in five domains and six backbone models, with shared-task analyses, human failure-label validation, and API-disjoint adaptation splits.
sUj5VKmh2a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the model-conditioned benchmark design and the diagnostic separation of knowledge content, delivery, and application with careful controls.
sUj5VKmh2a.main_concern: Reviewers note that execution checks verify target-API call fingerprints rather than full end-to-end functional correctness, and question whether failing without documentation on unknown APIs reflects a meaningful model deficiency.

tzbFpg2uHY.one_liner: Defines excess spectral suppression against a Bayes reference in target SVD space to diagnose budget-induced tail-mode loss.
tzbFpg2uHY.problem: Comparing forecaster output spectra directly against data spectra cannot separate legitimate MSE shrinkage of unpredictable variance from genuine bias against predictable low-energy modes.
tzbFpg2uHY.method: The authors define excess suppression (ES) as the per-mode skill gap to a Bayes reference in the target matrix's SVD mode space, using an analytic Bayes predictor on synthetic data and a cross-fitted attainable-skill reference on real benchmarks. They analyze reduced-rank and deep-linear theory and evaluate MLP bottlenecks, FITS, PatchTST, and iTransformer.
tzbFpg2uHY.key_idea: Measure per-mode forecasting skill loss relative to a Bayes reference in target SVD space to separate genuine excess spectral suppression from optimal shrinkage.
tzbFpg2uHY.evidence: Reduced-rank and deep-linear theoretical analysis, synthetic experiments with an analytic Bayes predictor, and evaluations on eight real time-series benchmarks across bottlenecked networks, FITS, PatchTST, and iTransformer.
tzbFpg2uHY.claimed_gains: At rank 32, bottlenecked networks leave 2.0-3.5x more attainable tail skill unrealized than the MSE-optimal rank-32 linear predictor, and narrowing FITS's cutoff on Electricity discards up to 97% of attainable tail skill while changing total MSE by under 0.6%.
tzbFpg2uHY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the Bayes-referenced excess suppression definition well-posed and appreciate the controlled synthetic validation and capacity-constraint diagnostics.
tzbFpg2uHY.main_concern: Reviewers question the arbitrary choice of K=48 and modes 25-48 as the tail, note that ES does not uniquely separate underprediction from over-amplification, and flag that main results rely heavily on MLPs with weak real-data noise-floor calibration.

FQ3HdqbQLP.one_liner: Benchmarks long-context LM harnesses on accuracy and cost using tasks requiring selective verification over dense distractors.
FQ3HdqbQLP.problem: Existing long-context benchmarks show saturated accuracy and similar costs across modern LM harnesses, failing to distinguish retrieval and reasoning strategies.
FQ3HdqbQLP.method: The authors introduce LongHarness Bench, four evaluation suites (including Constraint Solving Search, Equivalent Program Pair Search, and Program Execution Tracing) containing semantically relevant distractors where selective condition checking and adaptive local-global reasoning reduce search cost. They evaluate multiple frontier model families across four harnesses while holding model and context fixed.
FQ3HdqbQLP.key_idea: Hold the base LLM and dense-distractor long-context tasks fixed while varying agentic harnesses to expose accuracy-cost tradeoffs from selective verification and search strategies.
FQ3HdqbQLP.evidence: Evaluations of multiple frontier model families (including GPT-5.6-sol, Kimi-K2.6, Qwen3.8-27B, and GLM-5.3) across four harnesses and four evaluation suites.
FQ3HdqbQLP.claimed_gains: The best model-harness combination reaches 68% macro-average accuracy across the four suites, while similarly accurate systems can differ by over an order of magnitude in cost.
FQ3HdqbQLP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate isolating harness quality on the same underlying model and context, and praise the structured, selective-verification task designs.
FQ3HdqbQLP.main_concern: Reviewers report major accounting discrepancies between reported dollar costs, token counts, and the stated 3M cumulative token limit, making the central cost-efficiency comparisons difficult to verify.

wQ8HYxyEbA.one_liner: Shows adaptive RL prompt selectors concentrate on LLM-judge errors and mitigates this with per-prompt rollout caps and audits.
wQ8HYxyEbA.problem: Adaptive prompt selectors in RLVR focus rollouts on mixed-reward prompts, but when rewards come from an imperfect LLM judge, they cannot separate hard learnable prompts from prompts the judge grades wrongly.
wQ8HYxyEbA.method: The authors study how dynamic prompt selection interacts with LLM-as-a-judge errors across math and science domains using replay and difficulty-matched replay controls. They propose capping per-prompt rollouts and auditing capped prompts to suppress repeated exploitation of judge mistakes.
wQ8HYxyEbA.key_idea: Cap repeated rollouts per prompt and audit capped prompts to stop mixed-reward RL selectors from concentrating training on LLM-judge grading errors.
wQ8HYxyEbA.evidence: Controlled RLVR experiments across selection methods, model and group sizes, learning rates, and math and science tasks with exact-verifier and replay controls.
wQ8HYxyEbA.claimed_gains: Under an LLM judge, up to a quarter of rollout groups train toward wrong behavior (versus 5% under uniform sampling), wrongly accepted prompts increase two to four fold, and the cap-plus-audit fix removes most of this for ~4% more verifier calls.
wQ8HYxyEbA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the interaction between adaptive prompt selection and imperfect LLM judges as a timely, practically relevant failure mode backed by clean replay controls.
wQ8HYxyEbA.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical regime (small prompt pools and weak reference-free judges), note that Science selectors do not concentrate on error-prone prompts as the title implies, and flag coupling in the Math mastery metric.

HgYNJsQ9nc.one_liner: Audits composition-only safety failures in linearly composed LoRA adapters where neither base nor individual adapters fail.
HgYNJsQ9nc.problem: Evaluating LoRA adapters individually misses safety failures that emerge only when multiple adapters are composed together.
HgYNJsQ9nc.method: The authors define composition-only failures as requests where a composed model responds harmfully while the base model and every constituent adapter do not, and audit task-trained and public adapter banks across multiple base model families. They compare partner types (task vs. norm-matched and spectrum-matched random), refusal-data retraining, and weight averaging.
HgYNJsQ9nc.key_idea: Measure request-level composition-only harmful responses alongside total harm to expose safety regressions created by LoRA composition that aggregate or single-adapter audits miss.
HgYNJsQ9nc.evidence: Empirical audits across five base model families, in-house task-trained adapters and public adapter banks, two harm judges, regenerated responses, and retraining/averaging interventions.
HgYNJsQ9nc.claimed_gains: On one base model, pairing a weakly harmful adapter with a real task partner produces two to three times the composition-only failure rate of a norm-matched random partner.
HgYNJsQ9nc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the request-level distinction between composition-only failures and total harm, the broad multi-family evaluation, and candid reporting of negative predictor results.
HgYNJsQ9nc.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited conceptual advance beyond prior adapter-composition safety studies, lack of prompt-matched human verification against judge false positives/negatives, and no null model separating composition from ordinary model churn.

p883EHzezf.one_liner: Distills SONAR sentence embeddings on English alone using swappable multilingual concept lexicons for bitext-free zero-shot transfer.
p883EHzezf.problem: Multilingual sentence encoders rely on parallel corpora that do not exist for most low-resource languages, whereas bilingual dictionaries and lexicons are far more widely available.
p883EHzezf.method: The authors build a multilingual concept space by propagating ConceptNet vectors over the PanLex translation graph and public dictionaries, then distill a student Transformer from SONAR on English text alone using word frequencies and static concept embeddings. New languages are added without training by swapping lexical lookup tables, optionally interpolated with a small character-level model for out-of-lexicon words.
p883EHzezf.key_idea: Keep a Transformer distilled from SONAR on English frozen and perform zero-shot cross-lingual transfer purely by swapping static multilingual concept lookup tables plus a character-level fallback.
p883EHzezf.evidence: Evaluations across all 216 FLORES+ devtest languages, including 13 languages unsupported by SONAR, plus frequency-weighted concept-vector baselines and lexical deletion studies.
p883EHzezf.claimed_gains: Reaches 90.0% xsim and 39.0% xSIM++ across 216 FLORES+ languages (52.1% xSIM++ with the character-level model), and scores 50.1% vs. 43.5% for SONAR on 13 unsupported languages (46.9% vs. 26.2% on the six with least lexical overlap).
p883EHzezf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the bitext-free lexicon-swapping architecture is clean, practical for low-resource languages, and clearly isolates the transfer channel.
p883EHzezf.main_concern: Reviewers view the technical contribution as an incremental combination of established cross-lingual word embeddings, graph propagation, and teacher distillation, and note missing held-out-language calibration checks.

Flr2hAQUyN.one_liner: Relaxes arbitrary-arity Horn rules into continuous distributions over predicates and variables optimized with REINFORCE over symbolic forward chaining.
Flr2hAQUyN.problem: Existing neuro-symbolic inductive logic programming models impose restrictive language biases that prevent learning complex, arbitrary-arity Horn rules and direct variable bindings.
Flr2hAQUyN.method: The authors propose a logically complete Horn-rule model family that parameterizes categorical and Bernoulli distributions over predicates, arguments, head/body roles, and logical variables using learned embeddings. During training, discrete rules are sampled from the continuous relaxation, evaluated via symbolic forward chaining, and updated with REINFORCE gradient estimates.
Flr2hAQUyN.key_idea: Parameterize a logically complete stochastic relaxation over arbitrary-arity Horn-rule syntax and variable bindings, optimizing sampled rules with REINFORCE against symbolic forward chaining.
Flr2hAQUyN.evidence: Experiments on standard ILP benchmarks and complex high-arity rule benchmarks comparing against existing gradient-based rule learners and LLMs.
Flr2hAQUyN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the expressive arbitrary-arity Horn-rule representation with direct variable-binding learning and strong empirical results over tested differentiable ILP baselines.
Flr2hAQUyN.main_concern: Reviewers criticize relying on high-variance black-box REINFORCE over non-differentiable forward chaining instead of differentiable deduction, omitting modern symbolic ILP baselines, and dense presentation lacking clear parameterization justification.

wWErr35E9t.one_liner: Isolates how selective retention of high-loss non-stop continuation tokens alters learned stopping behavior in summarization fine-tuning.
wWErr35E9t.problem: Preserving content targets and complete-stop supervision during fine-tuning does not guarantee preserved learned stopping, because non-stop continuation loss terms also shape termination behavior.
wWErr35E9t.method: The authors decompose next-token loss into continuation and conditional content supervision and run controlled selective-repair experiments that vary only which non-stop loss positions remain active while holding data, content/stop losses, denominator, and compute fixed. They compare high-non-stop-loss retention against random support, conditional-token-difficulty support, donor stopping, and a global EOS bias.
wWErr35E9t.key_idea: Hold content and EOS losses fixed while selectively retaining high-non-stop-loss continuation positions to isolate how continuation supervision governs learned stopping.
wWErr35E9t.evidence: Controlled summarization fine-tuning experiments primarily on CNN/DailyMail with SmolLM2-1.7B, plus negative or inconclusive checks on XSum, Qwen2.5, and native training.
wWErr35E9t.claimed_gains: Retaining 820 high-non-stop-loss positions among 8,192 improves flat ROUGE-L by .0694 over matched random support and .0679 over conditional-token-difficulty support on 256 articles, and stays .0571 above full-pool random support on 1,536 articles.
wWErr35E9t.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean mathematical loss decomposition and tightly controlled experimental design isolating continuation supervision.
wWErr35E9t.main_concern: Reviewers highlight poor generalization and limited practical impact, as positive gains appear only in a specific CNN/DailyMail repair regime with SmolLM2 and fail to transfer to XSum, Qwen2.5, or native training.

dsoD4WNKRM.one_liner: Builds and iteratively refines task-oriented ontologies, knowledge graphs, and executable reasoning functions for LLM agents via judge feedback.
dsoD4WNKRM.problem: LLM agents relying on parametric knowledge or unstructured context miss implicit domain relations, while manually building task-usable ontologies is costly and automatic ontologies often omit decision-relevant structure.
dsoD4WNKRM.method: The authors present OaK (ontology-as-a-kernel), which dynamically constructs a domain ontology and knowledge graph from task requirements and training data, synthesizes executable task-adaptation functions for graph reasoning, and uses judge feedback to iteratively refine both the schema and functions.
dsoD4WNKRM.key_idea: Combine dynamic task-oriented ontology and knowledge-graph construction with executable graph-reasoning functions refined iteratively through judge feedback.
dsoD4WNKRM.evidence: Evaluations on TravelPlanner, CRMArenaPro, and ToolQA across two LLM backbones (DeepSeek-v4-flash and GPT-4o-mini) with component ablations.
dsoD4WNKRM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that structuring domain-specific agent reasoning through schemas, knowledge graphs, and executable functions is intuitive and yields aggregate gains across the three benchmarks.
dsoD4WNKRM.main_concern: Reviewers note that ablations do not isolate the ontology schema's own contribution, reliability claims lack direct grounding/violation metrics, extraction errors are unmeasured, and backbone models are dated or narrow.

bbHvsnllU6.one_liner: Stores frozen transformer layer-1 residual states at prompt placeholders and recomputes upper layers to reuse, compose, and update memory.
bbHvsnllU6.problem: Whether a frozen transformer can treat its own internal residual states as reusable, composable, and updatable memory without training remains unclear.
bbHvsnllU6.method: The authors store one residual vector per token position after the second decoder layer (layer 1) during context reading, then insert those vectors at placeholder positions in new prompts and recompute all upper layers. They evaluate long-context QA, four-way passage-question memory composition swaps, source-free memory revision, and episode-derived notes.
bbHvsnllU6.key_idea: Cache layer-1 residual states of a frozen transformer and inject them at placeholder positions in new prompts, recomputing layers 2 and above to enable training-free memory reuse and composition.
bbHvsnllU6.evidence: Controlled experiments across Qwen3.8-27B, Qwen3.5, and Granite 4.2 8B on multi-round coreference up to 136,577 tokens, LongBench, LoCoMo, synthetic handbooks, DROP four-way swaps, and SQuAD.
bbHvsnllU6.claimed_gains: Qwen3.8-27B scores 75.5 vs. 75.0 for full history on multi-round coreference up to 136,577 tokens; on 24 DROP pairs Granite 4.2 8B answers 47/96 with states vs. 13/96 with joined KV caches; an episode-written note routes 170/256 unseen records vs. 130 with episodes in context.
bbHvsnllU6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the experimental hygiene, bootstrap resampling discipline, and controlled four-way swap tests.
bbHvsnllU6.main_concern: Reviewers point out that parity with full history holds largely by construction because upper layers are recomputed from exact layer-1 states, leaving high read-time compute and unclear practical benefit over keeping the source text.

6pPSQusrg2.one_liner: Estimates time-varying Bradley-Terry ability trajectories from sparse comparisons using temporal basis expansions and penalized logistic likelihood.
6pPSQusrg2.problem: LLM and sports leaderboards must infer time-varying abilities from sparse, imbalanced head-to-head comparisons where models or teams are temporarily absent.
6pPSQusrg2.method: The authors formulate a dynamic Bradley-Terry estimator representing item-specific ability trajectories and contextual effects with temporal basis functions fitted via penalized logistic likelihood. By pooling comparisons across time, it interpolates latent abilities across temporary absences, backed by identifiability and estimation-rate bounds.
6pPSQusrg2.key_idea: Model time-varying Bradley-Terry abilities with temporal basis expansions and penalized logistic likelihood to pool bilateral comparison data across temporary item absences.
6pPSQusrg2.evidence: Theoretical recovery and estimation-rate bounds, extensive simulations with imbalanced schedules and absences, and real-data interpolation experiments.
6pPSQusrg2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree dynamic ranking under sparse, imbalanced comparisons is practical and appreciate the systematic identifiability and estimation-error analysis.
6pPSQusrg2.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments compare only against static and kernel Bradley-Terry baselines while omitting competing dynamic trajectory models such as KickScore, and question real-time forecasting versus retrospective interpolation.

n0xrH5tsvY.one_liner: Orchestrates a population of branch-isolated coding Search Agents using a global-context Shepherd Agent for open-ended optimization.
n0xrH5tsvY.problem: Single long-running coding agents accumulate context and edit one program state greedily, converging prematurely onto one high-level approach.
n0xrH5tsvY.method: SwarmResearch runs a Shepherd Agent with global context that dynamically steers a population of Search Agents without prescribing exact edits, while each Search Agent operates with local context inside its own isolated Git branch.
n0xrH5tsvY.key_idea: Separate global search steering in a Shepherd Agent from local execution in Search Agents isolated in independent Git branches to adapt parallelism across search depths.
n0xrH5tsvY.evidence: Evaluated on 15 open-ended optimization tasks against LLM-guided evolution, multi-agent baselines (including COARL and EvoX), and fixed serial/parallel scaling.
n0xrH5tsvY.claimed_gains: Discovers better or comparable solutions to competing LLM-guided evolution and multi-agent methods on 13 of 15 open-ended optimization tasks.
n0xrH5tsvY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that preventing premature convergence in long-running coding agents is an important problem and that the global-orchestrator plus Git-branch-isolation harness is intuitive.
n0xrH5tsvY.main_concern: Reviewers criticize running each method only once per task with no statistical uncertainty, missing ablations separating orchestration from branch isolation, and potential baseline budget discrepancies.
